About 3‑GIS
3‑GIS is a leading software provider for critical infrastructure industries, helping utility and telecommunications organizations manage complex networks, assets, and operations with confidence. Across electric and gas markets, 3‑GIS delivers purpose-built solutions that improve data quality, streamline workflows, and support safer, more efficient operations.
We’re equally proud of our culture. 3‑GIS is a collaborative, fast‑moving, and genuinely fun place to work. We take our work seriously, support one another, and believe people do their best work when they enjoy the team they’re part of and feel empowered to make an impact.
Role Overview
We’re hiring a sales leader to own and grow the utilities business for the Americas, with direct responsibility for the 3‑GIS utility portfolio including Productivity, Lifecycle, MIMS, and SPANS. This role is built for a strategic seller and market leader who can create pipeline, lead complex enterprise sales cycles, and establish 3‑GIS as the partner of choice for utility organizations modernizing GIS, field operations, workforce management, and joint use processes.
You will serve as the sales leader for these products across the Americas, pipeline development, new logo acquisition, and expansion within existing utility accounts. Success in this role requires executive presence, strong domain credibility in electric and gas utility workflows, disciplined forecasting, and the ability to translate operational challenges into clear business value across multiple product lines.
Key Responsibilities
• Lead Americas sales for 3-GIS utility solutions, including Productivity, Lifecycle, MIMS, and SPANS
• Own bookings, pipeline creation, forecast accuracy, and revenue growth for the utilities portfolio across electric and gas markets
• Develop and execute territory and account plans focused on investor-owned utilities, municipals, cooperatives, and other utility providers across the Americas
• Run complex, consultative sales motions from discovery through close, aligning customer challenges to the right combination of utility products and services
• Build executive relationships with utility leaders across GIS, operations, engineering, field services, and IT
• Partner closely with Sales Engineering, Product, Marketing, and Delivery to shape compelling value propositions and remove friction from the buying process
• Represent the voice of the utility market internally by bringing competitive insight, customer feedback, and market trends into go-to-market planning
• Maintain rigorous CRM discipline for opportunity management, account planning, next steps, and forecasting
• Serve as a visible market leader for the utilities business at customer meetings, industry events, and strategic partner engagements
What Success Looks Like
• Delivers and exceeds annual revenue targets for the utilities portfolio across the Americas
• Builds a healthy, qualified pipeline across Productivity, Lifecycle, MIMS, and SPANS with clear progression and disciplined deal execution
• Expands 3‑GIS market presence and credibility in electric and gas utility segments through strong customer engagement and strategic wins
• Creates repeatable growth by aligning product value to utility business priorities such as operational efficiency, compliance, field productivity, and network data quality
• Operates with strong forecasting rigor, executive communication, and clean CRM data
Required Qualifications
• 10+ years of quota-carrying sales experience with significant success in utilities software, GIS, field operations, workforce management, or infrastructure technology
• Proven track record leading complex enterprise sales and growing revenue across a defined region or market
• Strong understanding of utility workflows and buying centers, particularly across GIS, engineering, operations, field services, and asset management
• Ability to position multi-product solutions and connect technical capabilities to measurable business outcomes
• High proficiency in CRM systems (Salesforce preferred), forecasting, territory planning, and executive reporting
• Excellent communication, negotiation, presentation, and relationship-building skills
Preferred Qualifications
• Experience selling into electric and gas utilities across North America or broader Americas markets
• Familiarity with Esri ecosystems, utility network modernization, inspection programs, workforce management, or joint use processes
• Experience managing long, multi-stakeholder sales cycles involving security, procurement, legal, and executive sponsors
What We Offer
• Competitive compensation with strong upside tied to new logo performance
• Autonomy, trust, and a direct line of sight to impact
• A team that’s serious about winning and supportive in how we get there
• A fun, collaborative culture where people enjoy working together
This is a remote work from home position Share

Senior Product Manager - Utilities
Remote Full Time Experienced Share
At 3-GIS, the Product Manager for Utilities will play a key role in strengthening our position in the utilities market by working closely with customers, sales, and internal teams to ensure our products align with real-world operational needs. This role is highly customer-facing and focused on deepening our domain understanding of utilities workflows, supporting both existing customers and new sales opportunities, and helping transition customer-specific customizations into scalable, reusable product capabilities.
This is an ideal role for someone who enjoys working directly with customers, translating real-world problems into product requirements, and helping evolve an existing product suite rather than building entirely new products from scratch.
Duties and responsibilities:
Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Customer Engagement & Industry Understanding:
· Serve as a primary product point of contact for utilities customers, building a strong understanding of their operational workflows, challenges, and priorities
· Develop and maintain domain knowledge across electric, gas, and other utility network management practices
· Act as the internal advocate for utilities customers, ensuring their needs are understood and appropriately represented
Customization to Core Product Integration:
· Work with existing customers to capture, refine, and document requirements for existing customizations
· Translate customer-specific implementations into scalable, broadly applicable product capabilities
· Partner with engineering to ensure new functionality is designed to meet general market needs rather than single-customer use cases
· Help define acceptance criteria and validate that delivered features meet both customer and product standards
Product Requirements & Backlog Management:
· Create clear and actionable product requirements, including functional and non-functional specifications
· Work with Product Owners and engineering teams to prioritize enhancements, defects, and customer-driven initiatives
· Balance competing priorities across customer commitments, product health, and strategic direction
Sales & Pre-Sales Support:
· Support new sales efforts by participating in customer discussions, demonstrations, and solution alignment
· Help articulate how 3-GIS products meet utilities industry needs, even as offerings continue to evolve
· Provide input into proposals, RFP responses, and solution positioning
Cross-functional Collaboration:
· Collaborate closely with engineering, support, services, and sales to ensure alignment across delivery and customer expectations
· Support go-to-market messaging by providing utilities-specific insights and use cases
· Work with services and support teams to understand implementation challenges and recurring customer issues
Market & Product Assessment:
· Contribute to ongoing assessment of the utilities market, including customer needs, competitive positioning, and product viability
· Provide input into product strategy, including identifying gaps, risks, and opportunities
· Evaluate when existing functionality should be enhanced, standardized, or retired
Required Qualifications:
· Bachelor’s degree in GIS, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field
· 5+ years of experience in product management, business analysis, consulting, or a customer-facing technical role
· 5+ years of working knowledge of electric utility network operations including how utilities use GIS for asset management, field operations, and network documentation
· Experience working with customer requirements and translating them into technical specifications
· Familiarity with GIS platforms (Esri preferred)
· Strong communication and stakeholder management skills
· Ability to work across technical and business teams
· Ability to operate effectively in evolving product and market conditions
· Strong problem-solving abilities and a proactive, results-oriented mindset.
Preferred Qualifications:
· Experience with utility network models or asset management systems
· Experience working with customized enterprise software environments
· Familiarity with SaaS or enterprise software product lifecycle
· Experience supporting sales or pre-sales engagements
· Working knowledge of electric utility network operations in the gas & water domain including how utilities use GIS for asset management, field operations, and network documentation
Working conditions:
This position operates in a professional office environment. This role requires routine use of standard office equipment such as computers, phones, and copiers. This role may require up to 35% travel (customer sites, industry events, internal collaboration).
Physical requirements:
The physical requirements outlined here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this position.
This is a largely sedentary role.
This is a remote work-from-home position.

AALTO, a global leader in Stratospace. Based in Farnborough, AALTO is an Airbus subsidiary that manufactures, operates, and delivers services with its solar-powered, stratospheric platform: Zephyr.
Zephyr’s persistence enables continuous flight for months at a time. Its current flight-time record of over 67 days in the stratosphere. From above 60,000+ft, or 20km above ground, AALTO can deliver several applications including direct-to-device connectivity and high-resolution Earth observation.
AALTO operates in a new operational layer between most of air traffic and low-Earth orbit, Stratospace. This is where high-altitude platforms led by Zephyr deliver services to commercial and government partners. We can help monitor environments, observe borders, track natural disasters and connect unconnected communities.
Join us as we create a new domain of aerospace: Stratospace. You’ll be part of a highly-skilled, innovative and passionate group of people – Team AALTO. Together, we can Unlock Stratospace.
About The Role
As Ethics and Compliance Analyst, you will support the day-to-day delivery of our Ethics, Compliance, Privacy and Corporate Responsibility programmes, turning policies into practical processes and helping colleagues navigate their responsibilities with confidence. From third-party due diligence and data protection to community initiatives and engaging communications, your work will connect people, processes and purpose.
Working closely with Legal, Human Resources, Procurement, Finance, Communications and colleagues across the business, you’ll coordinate key activities, maintain accurate records and help improve the way our programmes operate.
Responsibilities to include:
· Ethics & Compliance Program Support Support programme delivery and Airbus and AALTO policies; maintain records, answer enquiries and prepare reports and dashboards. Help Finance audit expenses in high-risk jurisdictions and support Kenya sponsorships, per diems and government visit approvals.
· Third-Party Due Diligence (KYC/KYS) Coordinate KYC/KYS screening, review third-party risks, escalate red flags and track mitigation, approvals and renewals.
· Procurement Integrity & Business Conduct Support Support supplier reviews and onboarding, liaise with Airbus on red flags and implement supply chain screening and monitoring.
· Conflict of Interest Management Administer disclosures, check submissions, maintain registers and track mitigation actions and communications.
· Whistleblowing & Speak-Up Program Support reporting channels and compliance-related HR investigations; maintain confidential records, track cases and report trends.
· Privacy & Data Protection Support Support privacy requests, assessments, data mapping and incident tracking; manage TrustArc, maintain records and promote awareness.
· Compliance Assessments & Continuous Improvement Support ICSA, audits and reviews; gather evidence, identify control gaps, track corrective actions and improve procedures and guidance.
· Training & Awareness Coordinate mandatory training, track completion and create campaigns, learning materials and intranet content.
· Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) Coordinate CSR, volunteering, community and sustainability activities; maintain records and prepare updates.
· Donations & Sponsorships Coordinate due diligence and approvals, maintain registers, and monitor and report on donations and sponsorships.
· Internal Communications & Newsletter Management Lead the quarterly Legal and Compliance Newsletter, coordinate content and approvals, and manage the communications calendar.

To secure positive recommendations for our life changing medicines by demonstrating cost- effectiveness through the development of the highest quality and most robust submissions possible.

• Lead the development of UK HE deliverables, working in close collaboration with global colleagues and external vendors.

• Understanding of economic concepts relevant to UK HTA.
• Understanding of evidence synthesis techniques.
• Experience of developing and adapting CE models.
• Experience of developing CE and budget impact elements of UK HTA submissions.
• Experience of identifying and addressing evidence gaps relevant to demonstrating CE.
• Ability to work collaboratively across matrix functions.
• Ability to translate complex concepts into simple language.
• Ability to work to timelines.

• Inspires and motivates others toward a shared purpose.
• Influences colleagues to achieve cross-functional alignment.
• Deals comfortably with risk and ambiguity, changing course when needed.

At its core, this is an AI-focussed role; you’ll be in charge of setting up the foundations that empower engineers to produce first-class developer documentation with AI at scale. You’ll use AI to automate checks, maintain quality, and allow for rapid iteration in the content itself, as well as in the documentation platform. You'll join a team of around 60 people, working directly alongside senior engineering and leadership. No layers, no bureaucracy, and real ownership from day one.
Remote-first
We hire the best people wherever they are across the UK and Europe, trust them to own their work, and share decisions and feedback openly. Twice a year, in February and August, we all meet in person, and we expect everyone to be there.
Remote-first comes with trade-offs. On one side: flexibility, no commute, long stretches of focus time, and a wider pool of people to hire from. As our only recruiter, you'll need to manage your own time and stay close to the hiring managers and candidates you work with.

job_description:
About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
About Anthropic
Anthropic's mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
About the role
As a Senior Data Center Preconstruction & Capacity Delivery Manager at Anthropic, you'll make sure our EMEA deals are ready to execute before we commit to them, and you'll take time out of every program before the lease is signed. Delivery dates and costs on AI infrastructure deals are largely fixed at signature. What is missed before then is hard to recover afterwards, and our leverage over the schedule is at its highest while the deal is still open.
About 75% of your time goes to preconstruction and pre-lease management, from first desktop review through Letter of Intent (LOI) to lease execution. You'll test whether each opportunity can be delivered, rigorously accelerate its program, and shape the deal so that what a developer commits to can be held to, verified and delivered.
The other 25% goes to delivery. You'll carry that work through mobilization, embed with the partners building leased and partnered capacity, and lead them to deliver on the fastest possible schedule while maintaining a safe construction site and protecting the finished quality of the data center.
Our EMEA pipeline is getting off the ground, so you'll set the standard for how deals become ready for execution here. This role offers a unique opportunity to shape how Anthropic secures and activates the compute infrastructure needed to train and deploy frontier AI systems, working at the intersection of real estate, construction, and cutting-edge AI infrastructure.
Responsibilities - preconstruction and pre-lease management (about 75%):
• Lead.  This is a role where leadership trumps management and process.  You will be expected to engage developers, contractors, utilities and our transaction teams early enough to shape the outcome of each deal rather than report on it afterwards.
• Confirm deal readiness and serve as the gatekeeper to validate transaction viability from LOI through lease execution, ensuring all predevelopment, planning, technical and business requirements are met before commitment
• Give transaction leads an early delivery view from desktop study on capacity, power, permitting, connectivity, schedule and cost, so that the sites moving to LOI are ones that can be delivered
• Run independent, evidence-based delivery due diligence on each opportunity, tested against source documents rather than relayed claims, covering capacity, power, permitting, connectivity, procurement, schedule, cost, and whether the developer's team, contractors and supply chain can deliver
• Interrogate every developer schedule from the native file rather than summary dates, testing logic, durations, production rates and critical paths, planning backwards from commissioning, and establishing the unconstrained date before any commercial protection is added
• Rigorously accelerate programs during the pre-lease phase by making schedule work a priority for the developer while the deal depends on it, pulling forward design, permitting, power, early works and procurement, and sequencing the build around how capacity turns up
• Assess contractor and supply-chain capacity and long-lead equipment needs for each opportunity, setting a long-lead strategy that secures delivery capacity ahead of need and making the case for early equipment funding where it protects a date
• Challenge Total Development Cost and delivery schedules against the assumptions behind Yield-on-Cost and IRR, flagging where time-to-power or cost exposure puts the investment case at risk
• Shape the delivery terms of the LOI, lease and supporting exhibits with transaction and legal teams, including phasing and target dates, landlord scope, diligence cost, ownership and reliance, risk allocation and governance, and check that the developer's contract with its general contractor carries the same milestones and aligns incentives around accelerated delivery
• Give deal and delivery leadership a clear go/no-go recommendation at each decision point up to signature, with the risks, conditions and mitigations behind it
• Keep one delivery-readiness record and one risk register across all EMEA opportunities, assigning every risk to an accountable owner, tracking it to resolution, and escalating where cost or schedule is threatened
• Direct owner's representatives and third-party advisers and assure what they produce, bringing design and engineering, cost, schedule, commercial, contracts and procurement into a single view of risk and readiness
• Develop and refine the preconstruction playbook, a reference log of unit costs and benchmarks, and the operating model needed to scale the function, using AI tools including Claude for first-pass assessment, document review and benchmarking so your time goes to judgment and negotiation
• Prepare and present regular executive reporting on readiness and risk for each opportunity and across the portfolio, including time from signature to construction start, risks found before versus after signature, and baseline-to-actual variance, supporting forward capacity planning and strategic decision-making
Responsibilities - delivery leadership (about 25%):
• Document the baseline at signature for design, budget, schedule, long-lead position, open risks and conditions, so delivery starts from an assured position whether you carry the project forward yourself or hand it to a delivery colleague
• Partner with landlords and developers post-deal to serve as Anthropic's primary point of contact, coordinating across internal stakeholders, tracking construction progress, and facilitating critical information exchange between development partners and Anthropic stakeholders
• You will be expected to be at one or more project sites in adequate amount to shape the culture, approach, and aggressiveness that define those extended site teams. The goal is to impact outcomes in a favorable manner.
• You are expected to be a force multiplier that develops and enhances the skillset that development partners, contractors, and key trades bring to the project(s) you are overseeing.  That means being a subject matter expert in the various cross functional elements of data center delivery and increasing the team's performance with that knowledge and commitment to alignment.
• Represent Anthropic in key technical and operational decisions required by partners during the development process, ensuring our infrastructure requirements are met while maintaining strong partnerships
• Drive seamless handoffs to operational state with heavy focus on engagement across networking and deployment teams, enabling rapid workload turn-ups and minimizing time-to-production
• Identify and mitigate risks throughout the delivery lifecycle, proactively addressing blockers that could impact timeline, cost, or technical requirements, and feed what you learn on site back into diligence and the playbook
You may be a good fit if you:
• Have 8+ years of experience in preconstruction, development, or cost and commercial management on data center or other large mission-critical programs within EMEA, including time leading delivery on site.  You won't have a big direct team to delegate to but will instead be able to treat the entire cross functional organizations around each deal and jobsite as your team.
• Have a track record of testing developer and contractor claims on cost, schedule, power and permitting against source documents, and of telling a deal team when a date does not hold up.
• Have taken time out of programs before construction started, and can show how.  You read a native schedule fluently and know which levers in design, permitting, power and procurement move a date.
• Have shaped delivery terms in development, lease or construction agreements, working with legal teams, and have led tendering and bid analysis.  You understand how cost and schedule flow through to the investment case.
• Have a strong understanding of the end to end (dirt to delivery) data center development process to include entitlements and permitting, planning and supply chain, execution, commissioning, and handover. You are not an administrator but an active player in the arena comfortable making decisions without the need to consult across multiple external parties.
• You should understand the nuances of data center design and construction across EMEA markets- who the players are, how power and permitting differ, what contractual norms get in the way of speed of delivery, how teams can be incentivized to build and deliver faster than normal.
• Have built or scaled a team or function, including directing third-party advisers.
• In this role you will often be on an island and responsible for your own destiny.  You will have free rein to develop your own approaches with the mission guidance being your only bounds.  No one will be there to empower your efforts, you will create your own influence by building relationships and diving in at all phases to deliver success.
• You must thrive operating with ambiguity and have a willingness to own outcomes, knowing that the buck stops with you.
It's a bonus if you:
• Understand AI/ML infrastructure requirements, including high-density power and advanced cooling systems
• Have had preconstruction or leadership positions (Preconstruction Manager, General Superintendent, Project Manager) within a GC, EPC or developer on hyperscale data center projects or in self performance of hyperscale data center development projects.
• Prioritize extreme ownership and have the ability to create winning cultures across diverse teams and job sites.
• Are deeply familiar with lease negotiations, construction contracts, or real estate development processes and have strategies to move those arrangements from traditionally transaction and risk managed arrangements to collaborative efforts that align incentives around accelerated delivery of facilities.
• Have secured long-lead equipment or manufacturing capacity ahead of a signed deal, including through frame agreements or early funding arrangements.
• Have run quantitative schedule risk analysis, or built parametric cost benchmarks across a portfolio of sites.
• Speak additional European languages.

Become a vital member of our Complex Projects, Delivery Partner team, proudly taking on some of the world's most exciting and prestigious projects. Join us, and you'll be part of our genuinely collaborative environment, where everyone is supported to make the most of their talents. It's about recognising everyone's contributions equally while delivering excellence together.
When you join our practice team, you'll share our vision to be the industry’s foremost capability in Estimating & Cost Advisory and always doing what's right.
Enjoy a diverse and exciting workload surrounded by talented colleagues ready to lend a hand. You'll support multi-disciplinary and specialist project teams on high-profile schemes across a range of sectors, delivering high impact estimating services to a range of key clients. Plus, you’ll have the opportunity to grow your career and develop our internal capabilities.
We are looking to hire a Cost Assurance Consultant – Cost Verification and Assurance to support our growing business. In Complex Projects we work across three major markets:.
Infrastructure (Water, Defence, Aviation, etc.).
Transport (Rail, Highways, Local Authorities, etc.).
Energy (Nuclear, Renewable Energy, Power, etc.).
Your role
• Provide cost verification, audit and assurance activities, including forensic reviews across large-scale complex infrastructure projects.

• Engage with client teams, contractors and other project stakeholders to complete cost verification/substantiation together with obtaining key documentation and data.
• Deliver high-quality assurance reports and present those findings to senior stakeholders.
• Support the presentation of outputs and recommendations to clients and their wider supply chain.
• Support the integration of innovative digital tools for data analysis and reporting.
About you
• Demonstratable experience of delivering cost and commercial assurance/audit activities.
• Competent in the interpretation of a wide range of contracts, with experience in the application of the principles of a schedule of cost components.
• Experienced and comfortable analysing large data sets as well as experience of different costing systems.
• The ability to interrogate and assess data sets and produce outputs that can be used in the decision-making process.
• Bachelor’s degree in an Estimating, Quantity Surveying, Engineering, Construction sectors or Equivalent Work Experience.
• Chartership with or demonstrably working towards RICS, ICE, AACE, ACostE or similar.
• Good working knowledge of NEC3/4 suit of contracts across all option types.
• Ability to work autonomously in a fast-paced environment, working through challenges as they develop during the delivery stage.

Job Description
Overview
The successful candidate will be the PMC's subject-matter expert and strategic lead for digital transformation, technology innovation and digitally enabled performance improvement across the programme.
The role will identify, evaluate and drive the adoption of emerging technologies, digital platforms, data-driven solutions and innovative working practices that enhance the performance of both the PMC organization and the O&M contractors.
Working closely with Client leadership, PMC functional teams and contractor organizations, the Performance Manager will establish a structured transformation roadmap and translate emerging technology into practical applications that improve operational performance, asset reliability, passenger experience, safety, cybersecurity, productivity and management decision-making.
The successful candidate will combine strategic thinking with hands-on transformation experience, and will be capable of challenging established practices, developing compelling business cases and taking new ideas from concept through pilot, implementation and benefits realization.
Your role
Digital Transformation & Strategy
• Develop and maintain the programme-wide digital transformation and innovation strategy, aligned with the Client's operational, asset management and customer-service objectives.
• Establish a practical digital transformation roadmap covering short-, medium- and longer-term initiatives for the PMC and O&M organisations.
• Identify opportunities to replace manual, fragmented and legacy processes with integrated digital workflows and data-driven solutions.
• Assess organisational digital maturity and identify opportunities for improving technology adoption, data utilisation, automation and collaboration.
• Translate emerging technology developments into practical solutions and proposals relevant to complex operational environments.
• Establish prioritisation criteria for transformation initiatives based on operational value, implementation feasibility, cybersecurity exposure, cost, scalability and expected benefits.
• Develop compelling business cases, option assessments, implementation strategies and benefits-realisation plans for proposed initiatives.
• Provide strategic advice to senior Client and PMC leadership regarding digital trends, emerging technologies and their potential application within the programme.
Technology Innovation
• Continuously scan the technology market for solutions capable of improving operational efficiency, reliability and customer experience.
• Evaluate opportunities involving Artificial Intelligence, machine learning, advanced analytics, predictive technologies, digital twins, IoT/connected assets, intelligent automation, mobile applications and cloud-enabled platforms.
• Identify opportunities for predictive and condition-based maintenance using asset condition, failure and performance data.
• Explore appropriate applications of AI and advanced analytics for incident management, maintenance planning, asset reliability, passenger demand, performance forecasting and management reporting.
• Develop structured proof-of-concept and pilot programmes before recommending wider deployment.
• Evaluate technology proposals submitted by the O&M contractors and provide independent recommendations to the Client.
• Encourage interoperability and avoid unnecessary proliferation of disconnected applications and information silos.
Data, Analytics & Performance Improvement
• Promote a data-driven performance culture across PMC and O&M organisations.
• Work with performance, operations, maintenance and asset management teams to improve the availability, quality and use of operational information.
• Identify opportunities to integrate information from operational, maintenance, asset, customer and business systems to provide improved performance visibility.
• Support development of executive dashboards, management information systems and analytical tools providing meaningful performance insights.
• Establish mechanisms for identifying trends, recurring failures, emerging risks and opportunities for performance improvement.
• Encourage movement from retrospective reporting towards predictive and prescriptive performance management.
• Define measurable success criteria and KPIs for transformation initiatives and monitor realised benefits against approved business cases.
Cybersecurity & Digital Resilience
• Promote cybersecurity-by-design when introducing new digital technologies and applications.
• Work closely with cybersecurity, IT and operational technology specialists to ensure proposed solutions appropriately consider security architecture, information protection and operational resilience.
• Ensure technology initiatives appropriately recognise the distinction and dependencies between enterprise IT and operational technology environments.
• Support cybersecurity risk assessments associated with system integration, remote connectivity, cloud solutions, IoT devices, third-party applications and data exchange.
• Promote appropriate governance of privileged access, system interfaces, supplier connectivity and technology changes.
• Support assessment of cyber-related risks associated with O&M contractor technology proposals and transformation programmes.
• Encourage digital solutions that strengthen rather than compromise the resilience and availability of critical operational systems.
O&M Contractor Transformation & Assurance
• Challenge the O&M contractors to continually improve their use of technology, digital processes, automation and data analytics.
• Review contractor technology roadmaps and assess alignment with Client objectives and the wider programme transformation strategy.
• Encourage sharing and adoption of proven innovations and good practices across both O&M organisations where commercially and operationally appropriate.
• Identify duplicated systems, technology gaps and opportunities for improved integration across the wider operating environment.
• Monitor implementation of approved transformation initiatives and escalate delivery, integration or benefits-realisation issues.
• Benchmark contractor digital capabilities against appropriate international practices and comparable complex operational environments.
• Provide independent assurance that contractor-proposed digital solutions deliver demonstrable operational value rather than technology adoption for its own sake.
Digital Governance & Architecture
• Support establishment of programme-wide governance for digital initiatives, technology investments and innovation proposals.
• Define frameworks for progressing initiatives through idea identification, assessment, business case, approval, pilot, implementation, adoption and benefits realisation.
• Collaborate with IT, OT, cybersecurity, data, engineering and operations specialists to ensure technology solutions are integrated appropriately.
• Promote common technology principles, information standards and interface requirements across the programme.
• Support governance of technology vendors, solution providers and specialist consultants where required.
• Ensure digital transformation initiatives appropriately consider scalability, maintainability, interoperability, resilience and whole-life value.
Change Management & Adoption
• Recognise that successful digital transformation requires organisational and behavioural change, not simply deployment of new technology.
• Develop stakeholder engagement and adoption strategies for major transformation initiatives.
• Work with O&M leadership and functional teams to identify operational barriers to technology adoption and develop practical mitigation measures.
• Establish digital champions and communities of practice where appropriate.
• Support development of training, knowledge-transfer and competency-building programmes associated with new technologies.
• Monitor user adoption and ensure intended operational benefits are actually achieved following implementation.
• Promote continuous improvement, innovation and constructive challenge across the PMC and contractor organisations.
Stakeholder & Leadership Engagement
• Act as the programme's senior point of reference for digital transformation and technology-enabled improvement.
• Present transformation strategies, investment proposals, business cases and implementation progress to senior Client and PMC leadership.
• Facilitate workshops with operations, maintenance, engineering, asset management, customer experience, IT, cybersecurity and other relevant functions.
• Engage with external technology organisations, specialist suppliers, research organisations and industry bodies where appropriate.
• Communicate complex technical concepts in clear business language suitable for executive decision-making.
• Build consensus between technical, operational and commercial stakeholders with differing priorities.
About you
• Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Information Systems, Engineering, Digital Technologies, Data Science, Cybersecurity, Business Technology or another closely related discipline.
• Minimum 10–15 years of relevant professional experience, including substantial experience in digital transformation, technology strategy, enterprise transformation or technology-enabled operational improvement.
• Demonstrable experience leading complex digital transformation initiatives from concept and business case through implementation and benefits realisation.
• Experience working within a large, operationally complex organisation or major infrastructure/service environment.
• Demonstrable understanding of cybersecurity, IT/OT environments, data governance, systems integration and digital resilience.
• Experience influencing senior stakeholders and working across multidisciplinary organisations and contractor/supplier environments.
• Metro or rail experience is a plus
• Relevant professional certifications such as CISSP, CISM, TOGAF, ITIL, PMP/PRINCE2, COBIT or recognised cloud/data/technology certifications, depending upon the candidate's particular specialism.
• Experience within rail, metro, public transport or another safety-critical asset-intensive environment is advantageous but not mandatory.
• Previous experience working within a PMC, management consultancy, major operator, technology consultancy or complex outsourced operating environment would be advantageous.

This includes:
• Tax-free salary.
• Life insurance coverage.
• Medical insurance.
• Annual leave balance.
• Company gratuity scheme.
• Discretionary bonus program.
• Annual flight contribution.
• Transportation & housing allowances.

The Cost Clerk will provide accurate, timely and well-controlled cost administration for a construction project. • Monitor actual costs, commitments and forecasts against budgets, identifying anomalies, duplicate charges, coding errors, missing liabilities and emerging variances.
• Prepare regular cost reports, reconciliations and supporting schedules for project and commercial reviews.
• Assist with period-end activities, including accruals, prepayments, cost transfers, reconciliations and completion of audit-ready working papers.

• Contribute to improvements in cost-control processes, reporting accuracy and data quality.
• Comply with company policies, delegated authorities, contractual requirements and site health, safety and environmental procedures.

We're looking for a driven and enthusiastic Customer Service Manager to join our Yeovil store. This is an exciting opportunity for an experienced retail leader who thrives in a fast-paced environment, enjoys developing people and takes pride in maintaining high standards.
As a key member of the store management team, you'll be responsible for leading the front-end operation, ensuring customers receive a friendly, efficient and seamless shopping experience from the moment they enter the store. Working closely with the wider management team, you'll help drive service excellence, support store performance and create a positive environment for both customers and colleagues.

What You'll Be Doing

 • Leading the front-end operation to ensure a fast, friendly and efficient customer experience.

 • Supporting, coaching and developing colleagues to deliver their best.
 • Ensuring cash handling, banking and compliance processes are completed accurately.

What We're Looking For
We're keen to hear from leaders who can:

 • Lead from the front, creating a positive shopping experience and inspiring others to deliver great service.
 • Build strong relationships with colleagues and customers, creating a supportive and collaborative team environment.

 • Make confident decisions and respond positively in a busy, fast-moving retail environment.

You'll Also Bring

 • Experience managing cash processes and ensuring accuracy and compliance.
 • A passion for delivering exceptional customer service.

 • A positive, hands-on approach with the ability to motivate and engage teams.
 • Flexibility to work across days, evenings and weekends.

Why Join B&M?

 • Competitive salary plus bonus opportunity
 • Up to 33 days' holiday
 • 10% discount at B&M and Heron Foods
 • Extensive training and development opportunities
 • Clear career progression within a growing business
 • Exclusive retail and hospitality discounts
 • Wellbeing support through our Employee Assistance Programme

Ready to Take the Next Step?

Ready to take the next step in your retail leadership career and make a real impact on the shop floor?
We're looking for a driven and hands-on Floor Manager to join our Colchester store. This is an exciting opportunity for an experienced retail leader who thrives in a fast-paced environment, enjoys developing people and takes pride in delivering outstanding standards and customer experiences.
As a key member of the store management team, you'll play an important role in the day-to-day success of the store. Working closely with colleagues and fellow managers, you'll help drive sales, maintain excellent standards and create an environment where both customers and colleagues can thrive.
At B&M, no two days are the same. Whether you're leading a team, supporting a major delivery, driving availability or ensuring the shop floor is ready for trade, you'll be at the heart of the action, setting the standard and leading by example.
With over 800 stores across the UK and ambitious growth plans, there's never been a better time to join a growing business that's investing in its people, supporting career development and creating exciting opportunities for growth.
What You'll Be Doing

 • Leading and supporting colleagues to deliver exceptional standards across the shop floor.
 • Driving sales performance by ensuring products are available, well-presented and easy for customers to shop.
 • Maintaining high standards of merchandising, availability and store presentation.
 • Planning and prioritising workloads to ensure the store is ready to trade.
 • Coaching and developing colleagues to build confidence, capability and performance.
 • Responding quickly to changing priorities and supporting the wider management team where needed.

What We're Looking For
We're keen to hear from leaders who can:

 • Lead from the front, demonstrating high standards and a strong work ethic.
 • Build positive relationships and create a collaborative team environment.
 • Take ownership of their area and make decisions that support store performance.
 • Adapt quickly in a fast-moving retail environment and maintain focus under pressure.
 • Support and develop colleagues, helping them perform at their best.
 • Deliver an excellent shopping experience by maintaining outstanding operational standards.

You'll Also Bring

 • Experience leading a team within a fast-paced retail, hospitality or customer-focused environment.
 • Strong communication and people leadership skills.
 • Commercial awareness and an understanding of how to drive store performance.
 • A passion for delivering high standards and operational excellence.
 • Confidence managing priorities and making decisions in a busy environment.
 • A hands-on approach and willingness to get involved wherever needed.
 • Flexibility to work across days, evenings and weekends.

Why Join B&M?

 • Competitive salary plus bonus opportunity
 • Up to 33 days' holiday
 • 10% discount at B&M and Heron Foods
 • Extensive training and development opportunities
 • Clear career progression within a growing business
 • Exclusive retail and hospitality discounts
 • Wellbeing support through our Employee Assistance Programme

Ready to Take the Next Step?
If you're an ambitious retail leader who enjoys being hands-on, developing people and delivering great results, we'd love to hear from you. Apply today!

**Duties & Responsibilities** 
Key responsibilities include being responsible for the efficient management of service charge debts owed, overseeing the various operations required to resolve debt repayment and introducing systems and procedures to enable the efficient collection of outstanding service charge and ground rent debts.

- Using professional judgement to determine when to commence legal action against a debtor.
- Develop relationships and processes with 3rd party dept collection agencies to assist in dept collection. Manage these relationships and ensure all reporting is compiled to give a collective view to business.

- Posting and allocation of cash receipts to Propman system

job_title: Software Engineering Team Lead Core (API & UI), RTGS Technology
job_description:
Software Engineering Team Lead Core (API & UI), RTGS Technology
Permanent
Full Time
Leeds or London
Job Description
Most great engineers don’t set out to manage people. They set out to build something good. At some point, the best of them realise that building something good at scale means more than writing great code yourself — it means shaping the team, the standards, and what “good” means for everyone around you. If that’s the point you’re at, this role is built for you.
As Software Engineering Team Lead for the Core (API & UI) team, you'll own the technical health of the services through which users and systems interact with RTGS. The team is responsible for APIs, user interfaces and access services that enable participants and connected systems to interact with RTGS securely and reliably. Every standard you set, every call you make about what's good enough, happens at a scale most engineers never get near.
You stay in the code, retaining the ability to engage directly with complex implementation and production issues where required. You decide what good looks like for your team, and you build the conditions for it. You’re the technical counterpart to the Product Owner - together you decide what gets built next, and when to fix what’s broken, simplify what’s overcomplicated, and make the whole thing better.
You’ll also be investing in the engineers around you - the people doing this work alongside you are as much your responsibility as the systems they build. Helping them grow, and building a team people want to be part of, is not separate from the job. It is the job, just as much as the code is. This team follows a you “build it, you own it” model. What you ship is yours - including how it behaves once it’s live. And as you grow into the role, so does it: more influence over the domain’s direction, more say in how the team works, more of a hand in what comes next. Flexible Working Options 
This role is open to flexible working patterns, which may include:
• Flexible start and end times to each day
• A 50% in-office attendance requirement that can be spread across the month, with flexibility to reflect operational commitments such as on-call activity
• There will be occasional out-of-hours activity to support production releases and change testing, which may include limited weekend or non-core hours working
Opportunities in Leeds:
We’re excited to be growing our presence in Leeds, a city we’ve been connected to for nearly 200 years! Our modern, accessible office in the City Centre offers a supportive, flexible working environment. The majority of roles, including this one, are now available in Leeds, giving you the chance to build a meaningful career outside of London while contributing to our mission from a dynamic and growing location. You’ll work collaboratively with London-based colleagues in a hybrid model, with regular opportunities to travel into the London office to meet and connect together in person.
A day in the role:
Your day might begin with the team stand-up - a short sprint check-in where you cut through the noise, surface what actually matters, and make sure the team is pointed in the right direction. You know the codebase and domain well enough to judge what is hard, what is risky, and where focus is required.
You may spend much of your morning in the code itself - reviewing pull requests with rigour, pairing on complex service behaviour, API capabilities, user-facing functionality or production issues that require technical depth and sound engineering judgement. Your experience allows you to engage meaningfully, not just oversee. How much time you spend here depends on your team: if your team is experienced and self-sufficient, you may have more space to contribute directly to design and implementation; if the team needs more guidance and support, more of your time may go into coaching, unblocking and strengthening engineering practices. Both are normal and valuable version of this role.
Mid-morning, you may be in a design session with the Solution Designer, reviewing a new API capability, user-facing feature, or service interaction, stress-testing it against production realities and ensuring failure scenarios, operational considerations and recovery paths are understood before development begins.
After lunch, you could be in a roadmap conversation with the Product Owner - working through what comes next together, making sure there’s room for the technical debt, resilience, and improvement work that keeps the domain healthy, alongside the features that matter to the business.
Later, you may have a 1:1 with an engineer - providing direct feedback, supporting their development, and helping them grow into stronger engineers over time. No two days are the same, but the thread is consistent: keeping the team clear, supported, and moving. Sometimes that means writing code. Sometimes removing blockers. Sometimes asking the right question before a bad commitment is made. And sometimes leading a calm, effective response when something goes wrong in production.
Role Requirements:
As Software Engineering Team Lead within Core (API & UI), you will own the engineering quality, technical direction, and delivery outcomes of a team responsible for the services through which users and systems access RTGS capabilities.
This isn’t a role where you step back from the work to coordinate it. Your technical judgement directly shapes what gets built, how it is built, and how the team grows — which is exactly why people who care about the craft tend to find this rewarding.
You will:
• Stay in the code - taking on complex, high-impact work alongside your team, not just reviewing what others build. The balance between coding and leading shifts with your team's maturity: when the team is performing well, it largely runs itself and you have more room to go deep technically; when it's still developing, your energy goes into coaching & building the conditions for the team to reach that point.
• Lead by example in code reviews and implementation decisions, holding end-to-end accountability for the quality, resilience, and operability of the services your team builds and runs
• Own how your services behave in production - monitoring, alerting, reliability, and operational health - ensuring they meet the auditability, traceability, and recoverability expectations of a high-value, regulated environment
• Work closely with the Solution Designer to pressure-test technical approaches and translate designs into clear, buildable components
• Define, adopt, and enforce engineering standards across the team, including:
• Testing discipline and coverage
• Code quality and review practices
• Deployment safety and release readiness
• Incident response and operational learning
• Security by Design
• Act as technical counterpart to the Product Owner and co-own the roadmap - making room for technical debt, efficiencies, and continuous improvement alongside features, and forecasting what your team can realistically deliver
• Line-manage your engineers - performance, development, progression, and promotion and build a team environment where people are supported, challenged, and growing
• Take an active role in hiring for your team, including interviewing and assessing candidates
• Track engineering health metrics (e.g. deployment frequency, lead time, change failure rate, recovery time) to guide investment, and work with peer Team Leads across RTGS Technology to share patterns, solve cross-team problems, and raise standards more broadly
• Participate in on-call as a senior escalation point - leading calm, effective incident response and fostering a blameless culture of thorough post-incident learning
Minimum Criteria • A strong software engineering background, with experience building, operating and evolving production systems of meaningful complexity.
• Working knowledge of Java, React/Redux and API-based architectures, sufficient to engage meaningfully in technical discussions, review engineering approaches and provide direction across the team.
• Experience working within delivery teams and understanding how technical decisions affect delivery pace, quality and long-term sustainability.
• A solid understanding of distributed systems, data flows and event-driven architectures, including common failure modes and recovery patterns.
• Experience delivering and supporting live services, including troubleshooting, debugging, incident response and ongoing operational ownership.
• Experience mentoring, supporting or providing technical guidance to other engineers.
Essential Criteria
We are particularly interested in candidates ready to step into technical leadership, even if they have not previously held a formal line-management or team-leadership role. If you are an experienced engineer who is technically credible and ready to take the next step, this role is very much for you. These criteria describe the experience, judgement and leadership potential we are looking for, rather than a checklist of previous job titles.
• Proven experience as a Senior Software Engineer, Technical Lead or in an equivalent role within a complex production environment.
• Strong technical leadership and engineering judgement, with the ability to establish standards, challenge technical decisions and navigate trade-offs across quality, pace, resilience, security and cost.
• The ability to lead across different technical disciplines, drawing on the deeper specialist expertise of individual engineers while remaining accountable for the team’s overall engineering quality and direction.
• A track record of improving engineering standards through areas such as code review, testing, implementation practices, deployment safety or technical decision-making.
• Experience contributing an engineering perspective to roadmap, planning and prioritisation decisions, including making space for technical debt, resilience and continuous improvement.
• Demonstrated ability or strong potential to lead, support and develop engineers, creating an environment in which people are challenged, supported and able to grow.
• Calm and credible leadership during incidents or operational challenges, with evidence of turning operational learning into meaningful improvements.
• Clear and direct communication with technical and non-technical stakeholders, including the ability to explain risks, trade-offs and recommendations.
• Experience of, or willingness to participate in, recruiting and assessing engineers.
Desirable Criteria
It would also be beneficial, though not essential, to have some of the following:
• Experience working with Apigee or another API management platform.
• Experience with CI/CD pipelines and associated tooling, such as Jenkins and Gradle.
• Experience with messaging and streaming platforms, such as Kafka or IBM MQ.
• Experience with Oracle-backed applications or other data-intensive, high-volume systems.
• Experience in financial services, payments or another highly available or regulated environment.
Don’t hesitate to apply if you don’t meet all of the criteria. We value diverse perspectives and believe different experiences lead to stronger teams and better outcomes.
How this role fits into the wider Bank:
RTGS Technology is moving to a product engineering model, with teams aligned to business and platform domains. The Core (API & UI) team owns the services through which users and systems interact with RTGS, including APIs, user interfaces and access capabilities. Working closely with Core (Backend Services), the team provides secure, reliable and observable access to RTGS functionality.
As Software Engineering Team Lead, you are the technical heartbeat of the team - the person who holds the engineering bar and makes sure delivery stays coherent from design through to production, working alongside a Product Owner, Solution Designer, and Scrum Master who each bring their own part of the picture.
As the team and your capability grow, so will your influence over the domain’s technical direction - architecture, tooling, and the long-term evolution of the platform
Our Approach to Inclusion
The Bank values diversity, equity and inclusion. We play a key role in maintaining monetary and financial stability, and to do that effectively, we believe we need a workforce that reflects the society we serve. At the Bank of England, we want all colleagues to feel valued and respected, so we're working hard to build an inclusive culture which supports people from all backgrounds and communities to be at their best at work. We celebrate all forms of diversity, including (but not limited to) age, disability, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, race, religion, sexual orientation and socioeconomic status. We believe that it’s by drawing on different perspectives and experiences that we’ll continue to make the best decisions for the public.
We welcome applications from individuals who work flexibly, including job shares and part time working patterns. We've also partnered with external organisations to support us in making adjustments for candidates and employees in the recruitment process where they're needed.
From 1st October 2026, we expect all our colleagues to spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office per month. This is to capitalise on the benefits of working together in person across teams, while maintaining the flexibility offered by home working. Subject to that minimum requirement, individuals and managers should work together to find what works best for them and their team.
Finally, we're proud to be a member of the Disability Confident Scheme. If you wish to apply under this scheme, you should check the box in the ‘Candidate Personal Information’ under the ‘Disability Confident Scheme’ section of the application.
Salary and Benefits Information
We encourage flexible working, part time working and job share arrangements. Part time salary and benefits will be on a pro-rated basis as appropriate.
London: £71,680 - £80,640
Leeds: £64,480 - £72,540 In addition, we also offer a comprehensive benefits package as detailed below:
• Currently a non-contributory, career average pension giving you a guaranteed retirement benefit of 1/80th of your annual salary for every year worked. There is the option to increase your pension (to 1/65th) or decrease (to 1/105th) in exchange for salary through our flexible benefits programme each year. The Bank has the discretion to vary standard accrual rates and dial up and dial down rates at any time and to withdraw dial up and dial down options at any time.
• A discretionary performance award based on a current award pool.
• An 8% benefits allowance with the option to take as salary or purchase a wide range of flexible benefits. • 26 days’ annual leave with option to buy up to 12 additional days through flexible benefits. • Private medical insurance and income protection.
National Security Vetting Process

Further information regarding the vetting and security clearance requirements for the role will be provided to the successful applicant, and information about how the Bank processes personal data for these purposes, is set out in the Bank's Privacy Notice.
The Bank of England welcomes applications from all candidates, but as a UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) approved sponsor, we have a responsibility to comply with the Immigration Rules and guidance. As such, our ability to employ individuals who require sponsorship for immigration purposes is limited. The Bank cannot guarantee that you and / or the role you are applying for will be eligible for sponsorship and that any application made to UKVI will be successful. Eligibility will therefore be considered on a case by case basis.

Important: Please ensure that you complete the ‘work history’ section and answer ALL the application questions fully. All candidate applications are anonymised to ensure that our hiring managers will not be able to see your personal information, including your CV, when reviewing your application details at the screening stage. It’s therefore really important that you fill out the work history and application form questions, as your answers will form a critical part of the initial selection process.

As a Level 6 Journalism Apprentice, you'll develop your skills within a fast-paced, innovative newsroom. You'll gain hands-on experience creating quality news and current affairs content for the BBC. We offer gold standard training for people already demonstrating their journalistic potential and looking to develop advanced journalism skills.     ## **YOUR KEY RESPONSIBILITIES AND IMPACT** As a Journalist apprentice, this is a brilliant opportunity to learn, grow and contribute. On this apprenticeship you can expect to:  - Play a key role in creating trusted, high-quality news content for BBC audiences. - Grow your storytelling expertise through hands-on experience researching, writing and producing stories on subjects ranging from current affairs and business to sport, culture and politics. - Learn from experienced journalists, contribute to stories which matter to the public, collaborate with expert teams and develop your career at the world's leading public service media organisation. This involves weekly virtual Webinars and in-person bootcamps at PA Media Academy in London.  You’ll study modules such as: Media Law, Advanced Newsgathering, Advanced Storytelling and Advanced Audience, and work towards the National Qualification in Journalism (NQJ). The NQJ is assessed through 2 exams and a logbook of work.   For more information on what you will study during the scheme, please see the [Journalism Apprenticeship Standard](https://skillsengland.education.gov.uk/apprenticeships/st1490-v2-0) and the [NCTJ](https://www.nctj.com/qualifications-courses/qualifications/national-qualification-in-journalism/). ## **YOUR SKILLS AND ELIGIBILITY** We’re interested in your passion for working at the BBC and your enthusiasm for delivering world-class content and operational excellence to our audiences. We’re not focused on your qualifications; instead, we look for potential and offer you the opportunity to apply your transferable strengths and experience to work in different ways. If you can bring some of these skills and experiences, along with transferable strengths, we’d love to hear from you and encourage you to apply:   - Demonstrate strong journalistic skills and a passion for storytelling. - Actively follow sports news across a range of platforms. - Show a fascination with people, communities and the issues shaping the world around us. - Bring fresh, creative ideas for engaging and reaching new audiences. - Demonstrate motivation, adaptability and resilience in a fast-paced environment. This scheme is aimed at people who are already demonstrating their journalistic potential. You may have gained experience through a community or student newspaper, radio station, blog, vlog, podcast or social media content creation. We welcome applicants from a range of backgrounds and experiences, including those who have completed the NCTJ Diploma, a Level 5 Journalist Apprenticeship, or another journalism qualification.  ## **ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA** To be eligible for an apprenticeship at the BBC, you must: - Be 18 years old or over by the time the apprenticeship begins in September 2027.  - Have lived in the UK continuously for the last three years prior to the start of the apprenticeship.  - Be legally eligible to work full-time in the UK for the entire duration of the apprenticeship. - Not currently be enrolled in another apprenticeship programme, whether with the BBC or another organisation. - Not have completed or hold qualifications in the apprenticeship subject at the same or higher level. - Identify as disabled under the Equality Act (2010) or the Disabilty Discrimination Act (1995) if applying in Northern Ireland.  To apply for this scheme, you must also:  •    Not previously have completed any elements of the National Qualification in Journalism (NQJ)  •    Have achieved English GCSE at Grade 4/C or above; or National 5 (Scotland) at C or Functional Skills Level 2; or equivalent qualification.   Candidates under the age of 19 at the start of the apprenticeship must have achieved Maths and English GCSE at Grade 4/C or above or National 5 (Scotland) at C or Functional Skills Level 2 or equivalent qualification. Depending on your placement area, you could be working behind the scenes on exciting productions, from gripping dramas to the thrill of live radio, and gain a recognised qualification while learning on the job. This is your opportunity to broaden your production knowledge while working on content that matters to millions.  **Want to find out more?** Watch recordings from our webinar series on our [Life at the BBC YouTube playlist](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLQirbxfWHEPimmLiTI-yrGoMNMV1FRfWK) to learn more about this scheme and other opportunities we offer, and hear from current apprentices about their experiences. Places on the Production Assistant Apprenticeship are available across a range of teams at this location, as well as in other locations. You can find details on other placements in this location on the [BBC Early Careers website.](https://www.bbc.co.uk/careers/work/early-careers/production/#productionassistantlevel3) ## **WHY JOIN THE TEAM?** This is a unique opportunity to work with one of the world's most inspiring content catalogues, the **BBC Archive**. You’ll help transform it, for modern audiences. You'll be part of a supportive team that combines creativity, storytelling, production and digital innovation. As an apprentice, you'll contribute to stories that appear across YouTube, social channels, Bitesize, News and Radio, reaching millions every day. You’ll develop practical production skills, working alongside experienced colleagues, who love their jobs and who want to learn from you too! You'll gain exposure to different parts of the BBC, build a strong professional network, and see the direct impact of your work every day. As a Production Assistant Apprentice at the BBC, you'll gain hands-on experience across a range of projects, from supporting high-profile productions to contributing to content enjoyed by audiences across the UK. You'll work alongside experienced professionals, develop practical skills and play an active role in bringing creative ideas to life. This apprenticeship could lead to job opportunities as a: - Junior Researcher - Runner - Content or Edit Assistant ## **YOUR KEY RESPONSIBILITIES AND IMPACT** As a Production Assistant Apprentice within **BBC Archive Content**, this is a brilliant opportunity to learn, grow, and contribute. You could be: - Helping to develop ideas and stories by researching content and finding guests and participants. - Gaining real-life experience by assisting your team on location, in the studio, or in a TV gallery and helping out on the studio floor. - Learning to use technical equipment and specialist software by supporting teams with cameras, sound, lighting, and editing. - Creating content for multiple platforms, including social media, under the guidance of experienced professionals. You’ll study for your industry recognised apprenticeship qualification, learning both on and off the job.  This means that as well as learning on your placement at the BBC, you’ll also attend learning blocks (up to a week at a time) with our learning provider, working towards an industry recognised apprenticeship qualification - Level 3 Production Assistant. This hands-on, immersive programme combines practical workshops, interactive sessions, assignments and collaborative group projects. You’ll gain experience in creating, recording and editing video and audio content, while developing your planning, presentation and pitching skills. The scheme also provides a foundation in photography and imaging, social media and search engine optimisation (SEO), and website creation, giving you a broad understanding of modern digital content production.

The TV social team run promotional social media campaigns for some of the BBC’s biggest shows like The Traitors, Gladiators and Line of Duty. Our goal is to engage younger audiences and encourage them to watch our programmes on BBC iPlayer. We do this by making a range of content including editing video clips, filming on location, creating image carousels, and working with influencers and online creators.
## **YOUR KEY RESPONSIBILITIES AND IMPACT**
As a Content Creator apprentice, this is brilliant opportunity to learn, grow, and contribute – you could expect to:  
- Play a part in creating trusted, high-quality content for BBC audiences. 
- Grow your storytelling skills through hands-on experience researching, writing, producing and editing content on a range of subjects. 
- Develop your digital content skills by monitoring audience trends and creating content for social media platforms, including selecting and editing clips from programmes for use on social media platforms.  
- Spot opportunities for digital content, including short clips, behind-the-scenes moments, interviews and talent‑led extras. 
- Learn from experienced professionals, collaborate with expert teams and develop your career at the world's largest public service broadcaster. 
You’ll study for your industry recognised apprenticeship qualification, learning both on and off the job.  This means that as well as learning on your placement at the BBC, you’ll also attend learning blocks (up to a week at a time) with our learning provider, working towards an industry recognised apprenticeship qualification - Level 3 Content Creator.  
Learning blocks will be a mixture of in-person and virtual delivery, including attending instructor-led workships, tutorial sessions, presentations and group work.
For more information on what you will study during the scheme, please see the [Content Creator apprenticeship standard.](https://skillsengland.education.gov.uk/apprenticeships/st0105-v2-0)

If you can bring some of these skills and experiences, along with transferable strengths, we’d love to hear from you and encourage you to apply:
- Bring fresh, creative ideas for engaging and reaching new audiences.   
- A genuine consumer of content who follows what is happening across platforms like TikTok, YouTube and Instagram. 
- Adaptable and versatile, able to switch between serious, issue‑based content and fun, high-energy entertainment. 
- A collaborative team player who is organised, motivated, adaptable and thrive in a fast-paced environment. 
- Passionate about your own self-development, showing the discipline and commitment required to complete the apprenticeship. 
This scheme is aimed at **non-graduates.** If you have a degree and you’re interested in similar roles at the BBC, we recommend applying for jobs at the [BBC careers site](https://careers.bbc.co.uk/) or having a look at our other apprenticeship schemes. 
## **ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA**
To be eligible for an apprenticeship at the BBC, you must: 
- Be 18 years old or over by the time the apprenticeship begins in September 2027.
- Have lived in the UK continuously for the last three years prior to the start of the apprenticeship.
- Be legally eligible to work full-time in the UK for the entire duration of the apprenticeship. 
- Not currently be enrolled in another apprenticeship programme, whether with the BBC or another organisation.
- No prior learning is required to apply.
- If you already have relevant experience or qualifications, your individual learning plan may be adjusted to reflect this – meaning you could complete your apprenticeship in less time.
For candidates under the age of 19 years at 8th September 2027: To complete the apprenticeship, you must have achieved Maths and English GCSE at Grade 4/C or above or National 5 (Scotland) at C or Functional Skills Level 2 or equivalent qualification. If you have not achieved these qualifications by the start of your apprenticeship, you will be required to achieve Functional Skills Level 2 before the end of your apprenticeship when you take your end-point assessment.   
## **READY TO APPLY?**
Don’t leave yourself wondering “what if?” this could be your chance to be part of something exciting. See yourself thriving in this role? Just click ‘Apply Now’! 
You’ll create a candidate profile and answer a few questions - **no CV or cover letter needed.** 
If you're eligible, we’ll guide you through the next steps of the process and what to expect. 
You’ll need to live within a commutable distance of where this role is based. Interested in a different location? Check out our other adverts - but please only apply to one. 
The BBC recognises that you may need to relocate to a new location to take up a BBC Apprenticeship scheme. The cost of relocating can be a barrier for some applicants and where that is a barrier to participation, we want to help where we can. To help ensure our apprenticeship opportunities are accessible to people from a wide range of backgrounds, a limited number of relocation support awards are available each year for those who meet our financial eligibility criteria.  Relocation financial support is available for this role, subject to meeting the financial eligibility criteria. Further information will be shared with applicants during the recruitment process. ## **WHY JOIN THIS SCHEME?**
The Junior Journalist Apprenticeship (JRA27) is perfect for curious and creative individuals with a passion for storytelling. Whether you're finishing school, college, or exploring an alternative to university, this programme offers an exciting opportunity to kick-start your journalism career with the world's leading public service media organisation.
You'll gain hands-on experience covering stories that matter to audiences, learning from experienced journalists and developing the skills needed to create trusted journalism.  
Alongside this, you’ll work towards both the NCTJ Diploma in Journalism and a Level 5 apprenticeship qualification.
**Want to find out more?** Watch recordings from our webinar series on our [Life at the BBC YouTube playlist](https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PLQirbxfWHEPimmLiTI-yrGoMNMV1FRfWK&si=zN5oW9PAy2C6nmDQ) to learn more about this scheme and other opportunities we offer, and hear from current apprentices about their experiences.
## **YOUR KEY RESPONSIBILITIES AND IMPACT**
 As a Junior Journalist apprentice, this is a brilliant opportunity to learn, grow and contribute. On this team you can expect to: 
- Work alongside experienced journalists developing your skills while creating high-quality content.
- Get hands on experience including researching stories, booking guests and writing briefs.  
- Discover and develop compelling stories, assisting with interviews that bring important issues to life for diverse audiences.
- Learn from industry experts at the world's largest public service broadcaster.
You’ll study for your industry-recognised apprenticeship qualification, learning both on and off the job. 
This involves weekly virtual webinars + in-person bootcamps at PA Media Academy in London. 
You’ll cover a range of modules for the NCTJ Diploma including: 
- Media Law
- Essential Journalism
- Broadcast Journalism
- Journalism for a Digital Audience
- Video Journalism
Modules will be assessed through exams, coursework and a portfolio of work.

We’re interested in your passion for working at the BBC and your enthusiasm for delivering world-class content and operational excellence to our audiences. We’re not focused on your qualifications; instead, we look for potential and offer you the opportunity to apply your transferable strengths and experience to work in different ways.

- You're naturally curious about people and what’s happening in the world around you, with a keen interest in news.
- You’re full of creative ideas and enjoy finding innovative ways to tell engaging stories.
- You love finding things out, asking questions and getting to the heart of a story.
- You have a real enthusiasm for writing and enjoy communicating complex ideas in a clear, compelling way.

- Have lived in the UK continuously for the last three years prior to the start of the apprenticeship.
- Be legally eligible to work full-time in the UK for the entire duration of the apprenticeship. 
- Not currently be enrolled in another apprenticeship programme, whether with the BBC or another organisation.
- Not already hold a qualification in the same subject area at the same or a higher level than this apprenticeship.

- Not have completed or be studying for the NCTJ diploma or a journalism qualification at the same level or higher.
- Have achieved English GCSE at Grade 4/C or above, or National 5 (Scotland) at C or Functional Skills Level 2 or equivalent qualification.
