Job Closing Date:  24 November 2026
Glasgow, GBR, G511DA **Contract Type:** Fixed-Term Apprenticeship, Full-time for 36 months
**Department:** Business Operations & Technology Operations
**Location:** Glasgow - Pacific Quay
**Salary:** £24,650 
## **COULD A BBC APPRENTICESHIP BE THE NEXT ROLE FOR YOU?**
Join us as an apprentice at the BBC to give yourself the opportunity to kick-start your career in a job you'll love. We’re committed to your skills and talent development. ## **WHY JOIN THIS SCHEME?**
Engineering in the BBC develops, supports and maintains the systems and infrastructure that keeps the BBC on air. This is a fantastic opportunity to be part of the next generation of media systems engineers helping the BBC to deliver content for TV, radio, online and other digital services. You’ll be working on unique challenges, hand in hand with the best creative minds in the UK.
Learn about technologies and systems for TV, radio and digital channels, and how they produce high-quality content that’s distributed around the world.  Also learn the industry standards for the set-up of broadcast communication systems, media content systems and IP networks.   
Develop the specialised skills to design, build and maintain the media production and broadcasting technologies and systems that will take the BBC into the future.
**Want to find out more?** Watch recordings from our webinar series on our [Life at the BBC YouTube playlist](https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PLQirbxfWHEPimmLiTI-yrGoMNMV1FRfWK&si=eCgNZuWfnZICtWz1) to learn more about this scheme and other opportunities we offer, and hear from current apprentices about their experiences.
## **WHY JOIN THE TEAM?**
Depending on where you are based, you will work on the front line, supporting TV and Radio Production networks, systems and devices that are behind our flagship services such as Radio 1, 1xtra, 2, 3, 4 and 5, BBC ONE, SIX and TEN News, BBC Breakfast, BBC Sport, BBC Children’s, World TV News, our 40 World Service Radio services, BBC London, and Arabic and Persian TV services. The teams are also responsible for our master control rooms and telecommunication network systems. You will be trained and developed to support our TV & Radio studios and infrastructure and our master control rooms. 
## **YOUR KEY RESPONSIBILITIES AND IMPACT**
As a Broadcast Engineering apprentice (EAS27), this is brilliant opportunity to learn, grow, and contribute – you will:
- Develop your understanding of how live content is acquired and presented to studios, recording areas, playout facilities and distribution platforms in the formats they each require. You will learn how we manipulate audio and video and grow to understand the challenges faced in servicing a large broadcasting organisation. 
- Develop operational and engineering skills, learning how to use a variety of tools and systems, as well as how they work and what we do when things go wrong. 
- Develop teamworking and communication skills, working as part of a varied team providing services, and talking directly to other departments across the BBC. 
You’ll study for your industry recognised apprenticeship qualification, learning both on and off the job.  This means undertaking blended learning through a series of online and face to face teaching blocks at Birmingham City University, including: 
- Audio and Vision Engineering  
- Electrical and Electronic Engineering    
- IP Networks  
- Computer Science    
- Broadcast Technology  
- Database Technology   
- Engineering Mathematics  
 For more information on what you will study during the scheme, please see the [Broadcast & Media Systems Engineer standard](https://occupational-maps.skillsengland.education.gov.uk/maps/occupation/OCC0426).
## **YOUR SKILLS AND ELIGIBILITY**
We’re interested in your passion for working at the BBC and your enthusiasm for delivering world-class content and operational excellence to our audiences. We’re not focused on your qualifications; instead, we look for potential and offer you the opportunity to apply your transferable strengths and experience to work in different ways. 
If you can bring some of these skills and experiences, along with transferable strengths, we’d love to hear from you and encourage you to apply:
- Are fascinated by how things work  
- Love solving technical problems  
- Have a passion for media technology  
- Can manage multiple deadlines and demands on your time    
- Have a calm and focused approach to changing circumstances    
- Are an enthusiastic self-starter, flexible and adaptable to out-of-hours working 
## **ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA**
To be eligible for an apprenticeship at the BBC, you must: 
- Be 18 years old or over by the time the apprenticeship begins in September 2027 
- Have lived in the UK continuously for the last 3 years prior to the start of the apprenticeship 
- Be legally eligible to work full-time in the UK for the entire duration of the apprenticeship 
- Not currently be enrolled in another apprenticeship programme, whether with the BBC or another organisation 
- Not already hold a qualification in the same subject area at the same or a higher level than this apprenticeship. 
 To apply for this scheme, you must also: 
- Have achieved Maths and English GCSE at Grade 4/C or above or National 5 (Scotland) at C or equivalent qualification. 
- Have achieved, or expected to achieve, by the start of the scheme, a minimum of 112 UCAS points (300 if before 2017).   
- Have achieved A Level/Higher Maths, or an extended BTEC in Engineering with Engineering Maths, or an equivalent qualification.  
- Not have completed or hold qualifications in the apprenticeship subject, music technology, engineering or similar at Level 6 (undergraduate degree) or higher.
## **READY TO APPLY?**
Don’t leave yourself wondering “what if?” this could be your chance to be part of something exciting. See yourself thriving in this role? Just click ‘Apply Now’! 
You’ll create a candidate profile and answer a few questions - **no CV or cover letter needed.** 
If you're eligible, we’ll guide you through the next steps of the process and what to expect. 
You’ll need to live within a commutable distance of where this role is based. Interested in a different location? Check out our other adverts - **but please** **only apply to one.** 
The BBC recognises that you may need to relocate to a new location to take up a BBC Apprenticeship scheme. The cost of relocating can be a barrier for some applicants and where that is a barrier to participation, we want to help where we can. To help ensure our apprenticeship opportunities are accessible to people from a wide range of backgrounds, a limited number of relocation support awards are available each year for those who meet our financial eligibility criteria.  Relocation financial support is available for this role, subject to meeting the financial eligibility criteria. Further information will be shared with applicants during the recruitment process. Details on the wider support, initiatives and networks available at the BBC can be found on [our careers site.](https://www.bbc.co.uk/careers/bbc-life/inclusion/sed/)

You’ll be supported with career development, employability training, and networking opportunities to help you take your next step.
For apprenticeship opportunities, disabled applicants who choose to apply under the Disability Confident Scheme and who meet the minimum criteria for the role will normally be progressed to the next stage of the recruitment process. Job Description
Job Requisition ID:  55422
Job Closing Date:  24 November 2026
Salford, MAN, GBR, M50 2QH **Contract Type:** Fixed-Term Apprenticeship, Full-time for 36 months
**Department:** Technology Operations
**Location:** Salford - Quay House
**Salary:** £24,650 
## **COULD A BBC APPRENTICESHIP BE THE NEXT ROLE FOR YOU?**
Join us as an apprentice at the BBC to give yourself the opportunity to kick-start your career in a job you'll love. We’re committed to your skills and talent development. You’ll learn on-the-job, developing your knowledge and skills in an area that interests you, whilst working towards your apprenticeship qualification with one of our learning providers. 
## **WHY JOIN THIS SCHEME?**
Engineering in the BBC develops, supports and maintains the systems and infrastructure that keeps the BBC on air. This is a fantastic opportunity to be part of the next generation of media systems engineers helping the BBC to deliver content for TV, radio, online and other digital services. You’ll be working on unique challenges, hand in hand with the best creative minds in the UK.
Learn about technologies and systems for TV, radio and digital channels, and how they produce high-quality content that’s distributed around the world.  Also learn the industry standards for the set-up of broadcast communication systems, media content systems and IP networks. 
Develop the specialised skills to design, build and maintain the media production and broadcasting technologies and systems that will take the BBC into the future.
**Want to find out more?** Watch recordings from our webinar series on our [Life at the BBC YouTube playlist](https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PLQirbxfWHEPimmLiTI-yrGoMNMV1FRfWK&si=eCgNZuWfnZICtWz1) to learn more about this scheme and other opportunities we offer, and hear from current apprentices about their experiences.
## **WHY JOIN THE TEAM?**
Depending on where you are based, you will work on the front line, supporting TV and Radio Production networks, systems and devices that are behind our flagship services such as Radio 1, 1xtra, 2, 3, 4 and 5, BBC ONE, SIX and TEN News, BBC Breakfast, BBC Sport, BBC Children’s, World TV News, our 40 World Service Radio services, BBC London, and Arabic and Persian TV services. The teams are also responsible for our master control rooms and telecommunication network systems. You will be trained and developed to support our TV & Radio studios and infrastructure and our master control rooms. 
## **YOUR KEY RESPONSIBILITIES AND IMPACT**
As a Broadcast Engineering apprentice (EAS27), this is brilliant opportunity to learn, grow, and contribute – you will:
- Develop your understanding of how live content is acquired and presented to studios, recording areas, playout facilities and distribution platforms in the formats they each require. You will learn how we manipulate audio and video and grow to understand the challenges faced in servicing a large broadcasting organisation. 
- Develop operational and engineering skills, learning how to use a variety of tools and systems, as well as how they work and what we do when things go wrong. 
- Develop teamworking and communication skills, working as part of a varied team providing services, and talking directly to other departments across the BBC. 
You’ll study for your industry recognised apprenticeship qualification, learning both on and off the job.  This means undertaking blended learning through a series of online and face to face teaching blocks at Birmingham City University, including: 
- Audio and Vision Engineering  
- Electrical and Electronic Engineering    
- IP Networks  
- Computer Science    
- Broadcast Technology  
- Database Technology  
- Engineering Mathematics  
For more information on what you will study during the scheme, please see the [Broadcast & Media Systems Engineer standard](https://occupational-maps.skillsengland.education.gov.uk/maps/occupation/OCC0426).
## **YOUR SKILLS AND ELIGIBILITY**
We’re interested in your passion for working at the BBC and your enthusiasm for delivering world-class content and operational excellence to our audiences. We’re not focused on your qualifications; instead, we look for potential and offer you the opportunity to apply your transferable strengths and experience to work in different ways. 
If you can bring some of these skills and experiences, along with transferable strengths, we’d love to hear from you and encourage you to apply:
- Are fascinated by how things work  
- Love solving technical problems  
- Have a passion for media technology  
- Can manage multiple deadlines and demands on your time    
- Have a calm and focused approach to changing circumstances    
- Are an enthusiastic self-starter, flexible and adaptable to out-of-hours working 
## **ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA**
To be eligible for an apprenticeship at the BBC, you must: 
- Be 18 years old or over by the time the apprenticeship begins in September 2027 
- Have lived in the UK continuously for the last 3 years prior to the start of the apprenticeship 
- Be legally eligible to work full-time in the UK for the entire duration of the apprenticeship 
- Not currently be enrolled in another apprenticeship programme, whether with the BBC or another organisation 
- Not already hold a qualification in the same subject area at the same or a higher level than this apprenticeship. 
 To apply for this scheme, you must also: 
- Have achieved Maths and English GCSE at Grade 4/C or above or National 5 (Scotland) at C or equivalent qualification.   
- Have achieved, or expected to achieve, by the start of the scheme, a minimum of 112 UCAS points (300 if before 2017).   
- Have achieved A Level/Higher Maths, or an extended BTEC in Engineering with Engineering Maths, or an equivalent qualification.  
- Not have completed or hold qualifications in the apprenticeship subject, music technology, engineering or similar at level 6 (undergraduate degree) or higher.
## **READY TO APPLY?**
Don’t leave yourself wondering “what if?” this could be your chance to be part of something exciting. See yourself thriving in this role? Just click ‘Apply Now’! 
You’ll create a candidate profile and answer a few questions - **no CV or cover letter needed.** 
If you're eligible, we’ll guide you through the next steps of the process and what to expect. 
You’ll need to live within a commutable distance of where this role is based. Interested in a different location? Check out our other adverts - **but please** **only apply to one.** 
The BBC recognises that you may need to relocate to a new location to take up a BBC Apprenticeship scheme. The cost of relocating can be a barrier for some applicants and where that is a barrier to participation, we want to help where we can. To help ensure our apprenticeship opportunities are accessible to people from a wide range of backgrounds, a limited number of relocation support awards are available each year for those who meet our financial eligibility criteria.  Relocation financial support is available for this role, subject to meeting the financial eligibility criteria. Further information will be shared with applicants during the recruitment process. Details on the wider support, initiatives and networks available at the BBC can be found on [our careers site.](https://www.bbc.co.uk/careers/bbc-life/inclusion/sed/)
This is a fixed-term apprenticeship - your contract lasts for the duration of the scheme. Once you have completed your apprenticeship, you will be able to apply for any suitable open vacancies at the BBC or outside in the wider creative industry. You’ll be supported with career development, employability training, and networking opportunities to help you take your next step.
For apprenticeship opportunities, disabled applicants who choose to apply under the Disability Confident Scheme and who meet the minimum criteria for the role will normally be progressed to the next stage of the recruitment process. For most of our campaigns, this would be an online assessment designed to assess your skills, motivations and suitability for the role.  Further details can be found in the [FAQs section of our careers site.](https://www.bbc.co.uk/careers/work/early-careers/faqs/#applicationguidance)
## Disclaimer
This job description is a written statement of the essential characteristics of the job, with its principal accountabilities, incorporating a note of the skills, knowledge and experience required for a satisfactory level of performance. This is not intended to be a complete, detailed account of all aspects of the duties involved.
Our apprenticeship roles are also subject to you having the require qualifications that we have deemed to be necessary for your role and the requirement of the training provider for your scheme.  The offer would be subject to you undergoing and meeting the requirements of a skill scan process with the BBC nominated training provider to determine your eligibility.
Please note: If you were to be offered this role, the BBC will conduct Employment screening checks which include Reference checks; Eligibility to work checks; and if applicable to the role, Safeguarding and Adverse media/Social media checks. Any offer made is conditional on these checks being satisfactory.
Before your start date, you may need to disclose any unspent convictions or police charges, in line with our Recruitment policy. This allows us to discuss any support you may need and assess any risks. Failure to disclose may result in the withdrawal of your offer.
We are unable to accept applications via CV and only applications made online will be considered. Please click on the APPLY NOW button to proceed with your application.

We’re committed to your skills and talent development. You’ll learn on-the-job, developing your knowledge and skills in an area that interests you, whilst working towards your apprenticeship qualification with one of our learning providers.  ## **WHY JOIN THIS SCHEME?** The Content Creator apprenticeship is designed to equip you with the skills to create engaging, impactful content across a range of platforms. You’ll learn how to plan and develop creative ideas, research target audiences, and produce audio, visual and written content suitable for different channels.  This hands-on, immersive programme combines practical workshops, interactive sessions, assignments and collaborative group projects. You’ll gain experience in creating, recording and editing video and audio content, while developing your planning, presentation and pitching skills. The scheme also provides a foundation in photography and imaging, social media and search engine optimisation (SEO), and website creation, giving you a broad understanding of modern digital content production. **Want to find out more?** Watch recordings from our webinar series on our [Life at the BBC YouTube playlist](https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PLQirbxfWHEPimmLiTI-yrGoMNMV1FRfWK&si=eCgNZuWfnZICtWz1) to learn more about this scheme and other opportunities we offer, and hear from current apprentices about their experiences. ## **WHY JOIN THE TEAM?** [BBC Radio Cambridgeshire](https://www.bbc.co.uk/sounds/play/live/bbc_radio_cambridge) operates a network of radio stations across England and the Channel Islands. From Truro to Newcastle, we are at the heart of the local community. Our services offer a trusted source of local news and information but we also celebrate everything that is great about where we live. Whilst our shows will primarily be studio-based, we are all about getting into the heart of the communities that we serve. We have a unique connection with our audience and love finding and sharing their stories. We’re also passionate about local sport, plus our ‘Make A Difference’ initiative is all about celebrating the people and organisations that make the areas we broadcast to, a great place to live. ## **YOUR KEY RESPONSIBILITIES AND IMPACT** As a Content Creator apprentice, this is brilliant opportunity to learn, grow, and contribute – you could expect to:   - Play a part in creating trusted, high-quality content for BBC audiences.  - Grow your storytelling skills through hands-on experience researching, writing, producing and editing content on a range of subjects.  - Develop your digital content skills by monitoring audience trends and creating content for social media platforms, including selecting and editing clips from programmes for use on social media platforms.   - Spot opportunities for digital content, including short clips, behind-the-scenes moments, interviews and talent‑led extras.  - Learn from experienced professionals, collaborate with expert teams and develop your career at the world's largest public service broadcaster.  You’ll study for your industry recognised apprenticeship qualification, learning both on and off the job.  This means that as well as learning on your placement at the BBC, you’ll also attend learning blocks (up to a week at a time) with our learning provider, working towards an industry recognised apprenticeship qualification - Level 3 Content Creator.   Learning blocks will be a mixture of in-person and virtual delivery, including attending instructor-led workships, tutorial sessions, presentations and group work. - Runner

- Gaining real-life experience by assisting your team on location, in the studio, or in a TV gallery and helping out on the studio floor.
- Learning to use technical equipment and specialist software by supporting teams with cameras, sound, lighting, and editing.
- Creating content for multiple platforms, including social media, under the guidance of experienced professionals.
You’ll study for your industry recognised apprenticeship qualification, learning both on and off the job.  This means that as well as learning on your placement at the BBC, you’ll also attend learning blocks (up to a week at a time) with our learning provider, working towards an industry recognised apprenticeship qualification - Level 3 Production Assistant. As part of the programme, you will be required to travel to attend in-person learning blocks and other apprenticeship-related activities where necessary.

- Passionate and curious about content, and the production process at the BBC  
- Brimming with new ideas and fresh perspectives for BBC content
- A great team player who can deal with unexpected challenges  
- Flexible and have an adaptable approach to work to help enable our content to be delivered.
This scheme is aimed at **non-graduates.** If you have a degree and you’re interested in similar roles at the BBC, we recommend applying for jobs at the [BBC careers site](https://www.bbc.co.uk/careers/) or having a look at our other apprenticeship schemes.

- Be 18 years old or over by the time the apprenticeship begins in September 2027

- Be legally eligible to work full-time in the UK for the entire duration of the apprenticeship
- Not currently be enrolled in another apprenticeship programme, whether with the BBC or another organisation

- Junior Researcher
- Runner
- Content or Edit Assistant

Data Science is evolving the way the BBC operates. Our data scientists help us to better understand the customers we serve, and the content served to them, turning raw data into valuable insights and products to better serve audience needs. Whether audiences are watching on BBC iPlayer, listening on BBC Sounds, reading BBC News and BBC Sport articles or learning on BBC Bitesize, behind the scenes data scientists are at work...fancy being one of them?!  
Want to find out more? ## **WHY JOIN THE TEAM?**
As a Data Scientist Apprentice at the BBC, you’ll join a supportive, forward-thinking community where your work has real impact. You’ll grow through a mix of hands-on projects and dedicated study, earning an industry-recognised qualification. You’ll be part of a culture that values curiosity, creativity, and collaboration, helping to shape the future of media while building a strong foundation for your data science career.  
The BBC’s Media Tech Group builds the apps and products that bring incredible BBC content to millions of audience members across the UK and beyond. Increasingly machine learning and artificial intelligence play a crucial part in delivering these services effectively and efficiently.
We are looking for individuals intrigued by how we use maths and code to deliver real-world impact, collaborating with hundreds of amazing colleagues to create the BBC’s digital future. You’ll get on-the-job experience with our brilliant teams of data experts while also studying towards a degree. A fantastic opportunity to kick-start your career, building the world’s most in-demand skillset!
## **YOUR KEY RESPONSIBILITIES AND IMPACT**
As a Data Scientist (DSD27) apprentice, this is brilliant opportunity to learn, grow, and contribute – you will:   
- Learn about the value of data to organisations like the BBC. 
- Discover how the BBC uses data to both improve its connection with audiences and improve internal tooling and workflows. 
-  Be part of a team using data to enhance the way the BBC operates, using AI and machine learning approaches to deliver valuable audience insights and products. 
- Learn about and contribute to all aspects of the Data Science lifecycle from inception to production deployment and beyond, including aspects such as cleansing and validating data and building and evaluating predictive models.   
You’ll study for your industry recognised apprenticeship qualification, learning both on and off the job. This means you’ll spend at least one day a week studying for a BSc (Hons) in Data Science with BPP University remotely studying topics including:   
- Artificial Intelligence and Deep Learning   
- Machine Learning  
- Data Infrastructure & Tools 
- Data Visualisation & Dashboards   
For more information on what you will study during the scheme, please see the [Data Scientist degree apprenticeship standard.](https://skillsengland.education.gov.uk/apprenticeships/st0585-v1-1)

- Have a love of maths  and a passion for data, machine learning and AI 
- An excitement to embrace the latest AI and Machine Learning Technologies responsibly to transform working practices 
- Have brilliant non-technical skills such as problem-solving, organisation and negotiation 
- Flexibility and adaptability including a calm and focused approach to working within an evolving technical landscape and workplace.   
- Can manage multiple deadlines and demands on your time  
- Bursting with fresh ideas to introduce new perspectives with a keen interest in the BBC, it’s public service mission and values. 
This scheme is aimed at **non-graduates**. If you have a degree and you’re interested in similar roles at the BBC, we recommend applying for jobs at the [BBC careers site](https://careers.bbc.co.uk/) or having a look at our other apprenticeship schemes. 
## **ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA**
To be eligible for an apprenticeship at the BBC, you must: 
- Be 18 years old or over by the time the apprenticeship begins in September 2027.
- Have lived in the UK continuously for the last three years prior to the start of the apprenticeship.
- Be legally eligible to work full-time in the UK for the entire duration of the apprenticeship.

- Not already hold a qualification in the same subject area at the same or a higher level than this apprenticeship. 
 To apply for this scheme, you must also:
- Have maths and English GCSE at Grade 4/C or above or National 5 (Scotland) at C or equivalent qualification  
- Have achieved, or expected to achieve, by the start of the scheme, a minimum of 104 UCAS points. 
- This must include A Level/Higher Maths, or an extended BTEC in Engineering with Engineering Maths, or an equivalent qualification.

You’ll create a candidate profile and answer a few questions - **no CV or cover letter needed.** 
If you're eligible, we’ll guide you through the next steps of the process and what to expect.

**Department:** BBC Introducing
**Location:** Glasgow - Pacific Quay
**Salary:** £24,650 
## **COULD A BBC APPRENTICESHIP BE THE NEXT ROLE FOR YOU?**
Join us as an apprentice at the BBC to give yourself the opportunity to kick-start your career in a job you'll love. We’re committed to your skills and talent development. You’ll learn on-the-job, developing your knowledge and skills in an area that interests you, whilst working towards your apprenticeship qualification with one of our learning providers. 
## **WHY JOIN THIS SCHEME?**
The Content Creator apprenticeship is designed to equip you with the skills to create engaging, impactful content across a range of platforms. You’ll learn how to plan and develop creative ideas, research target audiences, and produce audio, visual and written content suitable for different channels. 
This hands-on, immersive programme combines practical workshops, interactive sessions, assignments and collaborative group projects. You’ll gain experience in creating, recording and editing video and audio content, while developing your planning, presentation and pitching skills. The scheme also provides a foundation in photography and imaging, social media and search engine optimisation (SEO), and website creation, giving you a broad understanding of modern digital content production.
**Want to find out more?** Watch recordings from our webinar series on our [Life at the BBC YouTube playlist](https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PLQirbxfWHEPimmLiTI-yrGoMNMV1FRfWK&si=eCgNZuWfnZICtWz1) to learn more about this scheme and other opportunities we offer, and hear from current apprentices about their experiences.
## **WHY JOIN THE TEAM?**
[BBC Introducing](https://www.bbc.co.uk/introducing) supports exciting new music from across the UK. Working within [BBC Radio Scotland](https://www.bbc.co.uk/sounds/play/live/bbc_radio_scotland_fm), you’ll listen to new music, carry out research, edit audio, support programme teams, create content and may help deliver live events and sessions. We’re looking for someone really passionate about music, radio and social media. You'll need to be organised, creative and confident working under pressure in a busy, fast-moving broadcasting environment. You must live in the area you’re applying for.
## **YOUR KEY RESPONSIBILITIES AND IMPACT**
As a Content Creator apprentice, this is brilliant opportunity to learn, grow, and contribute – you could expect to:  
- Play a part in creating trusted, high-quality content for BBC audiences. 
- Grow your storytelling skills through hands-on experience researching, writing, producing and editing content on a range of subjects. 
- Develop your digital content skills by monitoring audience trends and creating content for social media platforms, including selecting and editing clips from programmes for use on social media platforms.  
- Spot opportunities for digital content, including short clips, behind-the-scenes moments, interviews and talent‑led extras. 
- Learn from experienced professionals, collaborate with expert teams and develop your career at the world's largest public service broadcaster. 
You’ll study for your industry recognised apprenticeship qualification, learning both on and off the job.  This means that as well as learning on your placement at the BBC, you’ll also attend learning blocks (up to a week at a time) with our learning provider, working towards an industry recognised apprenticeship qualification - Level 3 Content Creator.  
Learning blocks will be a mixture of in-person and virtual delivery, including attending instructor-led workships, tutorial sessions, presentations and group work.
For more information on what you will study during the scheme, please see the [Content Creator apprenticeship standard.](https://skillsengland.education.gov.uk/apprenticeships/st0105-v2-0) 
As part of the programme, you will be required to travel to attend in-person learning blocks and other apprenticeship-related activities where necessary. 
## **YOUR SKILLS AND ELIGIBILITY**
We’re interested in your passion for working at the BBC and your enthusiasm for delivering world-class content and operational excellence to our audiences. We’re not focused on your qualifications; instead, we look for potential and offer you the opportunity to apply your transferable strengths and experience to work in different ways. 
If you can bring some of these skills and experiences, along with transferable strengths, we’d love to hear from you and encourage you to apply:
- Bring fresh, creative ideas for engaging and reaching new audiences.   
- A genuine consumer of content who follows what is happening across platforms like TikTok, YouTube and Instagram. 
- Adaptable and versatile, able to switch between serious, issue‑based content and fun, high-energy entertainment. 
- A collaborative team player who is organised, motivated, adaptable and thrive in a fast-paced environment. 
- Passionate about your own self-development, showing the discipline and commitment required to complete the apprenticeship. 
This scheme is aimed at **non-graduates.** If you have a degree and you’re interested in similar roles at the BBC, we recommend applying for jobs at the [BBC careers site](https://careers.bbc.co.uk/) or having a look at our other apprenticeship schemes. 
## **ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA**
To be eligible for an apprenticeship at the BBC, you must: 
- Be 18 years old or over by the time the apprenticeship begins in September 2027.
- Have lived in the UK continuously for the last three years prior to the start of the apprenticeship.
- Be legally eligible to work full-time in the UK for the entire duration of the apprenticeship. 
- Not currently be enrolled in another apprenticeship programme, whether with the BBC or another organisation.
- No prior learning is required to apply.
- If you already have relevant experience or qualifications, your individual learning plan may be adjusted to reflect this – meaning you could complete your apprenticeship in less time.
For candidates under the age of 19 years at 8th September 2027: To complete the apprenticeship, you must have achieved Maths and English GCSE at Grade 4/C or above or National 5 (Scotland) at C or Functional Skills Level 2 or equivalent qualification. If you have not achieved these qualifications by the start of your apprenticeship, you will be required to achieve Functional Skills Level 2 before the end of your apprenticeship when you take your end-point assessment.   
## **READY TO APPLY?**
Don’t leave yourself wondering “what if?” this could be your chance to be part of something exciting. See yourself thriving in this role? Just click ‘Apply Now’! 
You’ll create a candidate profile and answer a few questions - **no CV or cover letter needed.** 
If you're eligible, we’ll guide you through the next steps of the process and what to expect. 
You’ll need to live within a commutable distance of where this role is based. Interested in a different location? Check out our other adverts - but please only apply to one. 
The BBC recognises that you may need to relocate to a new location to take up a BBC Apprenticeship scheme. The cost of relocating can be a barrier for some applicants and where that is a barrier to participation, we want to help where we can. To help ensure our apprenticeship opportunities are accessible to people from a wide range of backgrounds, a limited number of relocation support awards are available each year for those who meet our financial eligibility criteria.  Relocation financial support is available for this role, subject to meeting the financial eligibility criteria. Further information will be shared with applicants during the recruitment process. Details on the wider support, initiatives and networks available at the BBC can be found on [our careers site.](https://www.bbc.co.uk/careers/bbc-life/inclusion/sed/)
This is a fixed-term apprenticeship - your contract lasts for the duration of the scheme. Once you have completed your apprenticeship, you will be able to apply for any suitable open vacancies at the BBC or outside in the wider creative industry. You’ll be supported with career development, employability training, and networking opportunities to help you take your next step.
For apprenticeship opportunities, disabled applicants who choose to apply under the Disability Confident Scheme and who meet the minimum criteria for the role will normally be progressed to the next stage of the recruitment process. For most of our campaigns, this would be an online assessment designed to assess your skills, motivations and suitability for the role.  Further details can be found in the [FAQs section of our careers site.](https://www.bbc.co.uk/careers/work/early-careers/faqs/#applicationguidance)

Job Description
Job Requisition ID:  56066
Job Closing Date:  24 November 2026
Glasgow, GBR, G511DA **CONTRACT TYPE:** Fixed-term Apprenticeship, Full-time for 17 months **DEPARTMENT:** BBC Scotland **LOCATION**: Glasgow - Pacific Quay **SALARY:** £24,650 
## **COULD A BBC APPRENTICESHIP BE THE NEXT ROLE FOR YOU?**
Join us as an apprentice at the BBC to give yourself the opportunity to kick-start your career in a job you'll love. We’re committed to your skills and talent development. You’ll learn on-the-job, developing your knowledge and skills in an area that interests you, whilst working towards your apprenticeship qualification with one of our learning providers. 
## **WHY JOIN THIS SCHEME?**
Are you a natural organiser with a passion for media? The Junior Production Coordinator Apprenticeship at the BBC could be your perfect start. You may help with the set-up of filming on location or in the studio for one of our programmes like The One Show or schedule crews and freelancers for Women’s Hour. No media experience or qualifications needed - just enthusiasm and problem-solving skills. Whether you're finishing school or changing careers, this hands-on role offers a pathway into production management at one of the world’s leading broadcasters.
**Want to find out more?** Watch recordings from our webinar series on our [Life at the BBC YouTube playlist](https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PLQirbxfWHEPimmLiTI-yrGoMNMV1FRfWK&si=eCgNZuWfnZICtWz1)  to learn more about this scheme and other opportunities we offer, and hear from current apprentices about their experiences.
Places on the Junior Production Coordinator Apprenticeship are available across a range of teams at this location, as well as in other locations. You can find details on other placements in this location on the [BBC Early Careers website.](https://www.bbc.co.uk/careers/work/early-careers/production/#juniorproductioncoordinatorlevel4)
## **WHY JOIN THE TEAM?**
Start your career in Production Management. As a Junior Production Coordinator apprentice, you'll work alongside experienced Production Managers and Production Coordinators, helping to create high-quality content for TV, audio, online and digital platforms.
**BBC Scotland’s Music, Entertainment & Events, Sport, and Impact teams** create a wide range of content that connects with audiences across TV, radio, and digital platforms. From live music and major sporting events to powerful documentaries and entertainment shows, our work reflects life in Scotland and beyond. As an apprentice, you’ll support the production teams by helping with logistics, coordination, and on-the-ground activity that brings our content to life.
This apprenticeship could lead to job opportunities as a:
- Production Coordinator
- Production Secretary
- Production Manager
## **YOUR KEY RESPONSIBILITIES AND IMPACT**
As a Junior Production Coordinator Apprentice this is a brilliant opportunity within **BBC Scotland** to learn, grow, and contribute – you may: 
- Assist with shoots, studio setups, crew bookings, and call sheets 
- Booking transport and accommodation
- Support budget management, raising payments for suppliers and broadcasters
- Applying for accreditations/permits/visas
- Learn best practices in health & safety, and compliance
By the end of the apprenticeship, you'll have the skills and confidence to take the next step in your career, applying for roles such as Junior Production Coordinator or Production Management Assistant. To find out what it's like to work in a Production Management team, please take a look at the following links;
- Learn what [BBC Production Management](https://www.bbc.com/academy-guides/is-tv-production-management-for-me/#:~:text=TV%20production%20management%20is%20the,on%20budget%20and%20on%20time) is and how it helps bring programmes to life
- Watch this video to learn about the day-to-day responsibilities of a [Production Coordinator at BBC Radio Ulster](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Dr8dEqNMucs&t=3s)
This apprenticeship will give you a thorough knowledge and understanding of what it is like to work within a Production Management team and the media industry, which you can then utilise during your time at the BBC and afterwards in the wider industry.  
You’ll study for your industry recognised apprenticeship qualification, learning both on the job at the BBC and off the job with our chosen education provider. The academic study involves;
- Attending instructor-led workshops
- Tutorial sessions
- Presentations
- Group work
Throughout your apprenticeship, you will be asked to gather a portfolio of evidence and work on an apprenticeship assessment that demonstrates your learning, while working towards a SCQF7 diploma apprenticeship qualification.
For more information on this apprenticeship framework you will be studying, please visit detail on the [Creative Media SCQF level 7 - SQA.](https://www.sqa.org.uk/sqa/69546.html)
## **YOUR SKILLS AND ELIGIBILITY**
We’re interested in your passion for working at the BBC and your enthusiasm for delivering world-class content and operational excellence to our audiences. We’re not focused on your qualifications; instead, we look for potential and offer you the opportunity to apply your transferable strengths and experience to work in different ways. 
If you can bring some of these skills and experiences, along with transferable strengths, we’d love to hear from you and encourage you to apply:
- Have brilliant organisational skills and are great at problem-solving and negotiating
- Great at working with people; a team player and great communicator
- Resilient, responsible and have a calm focused approach to challenging situations
- Flexible, motivated and have an adaptable approach to the pace of work
- Can manage multiple deadlines and demands on your time
- Are an enthusiastic and motivated self-starter, flexible and adaptable to out-of-hours working
This scheme is aimed at **non-graduates.** If you have a degree and you’re interested in similar roles at the BBC, we recommend applying for jobs at the [BBC careers site](https://www.bbc.co.uk/careers/) or having a look at our other apprenticeship schemes. 
## **ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA**
To be eligible for an apprenticeship at the BBC, you must: 
- Be 18 years old or over by the time the apprenticeship begins in September 2027.
- Have lived in the UK continuously for the last three years prior to the start of the apprenticeship.
- Be legally eligible to work full-time in the UK for the entire duration of the apprenticeship. 
- Not currently be enrolled in another apprenticeship programme, whether with the BBC or another organisation.
- Not already hold a qualification in the same subject area at the same or a higher level than this apprenticeship. 
 To apply for this scheme, you must also:
- To complete the apprenticeship, you must have achieved Core Skills (Scotland) at SCQF Level 5 or 6 in Communication and Numeracy. If you have not achieved these qualifications by the start of your apprenticeship, core skills will be embedded into learning.
- Must be passionate about the production management side of making content. If it’s the ‘coming up with ideas for content’ side you like about producing content, then the [Level 3 Production Assistant Apprenticeship](https://www.bbc.co.uk/careers/work/early-careers/production/#productionassistantlevel3) will be more suitable for you.  ## **READY TO APPLY?**
Don’t leave yourself wondering “what if?” this could be your chance to be part of something exciting. See yourself thriving in this role? Just click ‘Apply Now’! 
You’ll create a candidate profile and answer a few questions - **no CV or cover letter needed.** 
If you're eligible, we’ll guide you through the next steps of the process and what to expect. 
You’ll need to live within a commutable distance of where this role is based. Interested in a different location? Check out our other adverts - but please only apply to one. The BBC recognises that you may need to relocate to a new location to take up a BBC Apprenticeship scheme. The cost of relocating can be a barrier for some applicants and where that is a barrier to participation, we want to help where we can. To help ensure our apprenticeship opportunities are accessible to people from a wide range of backgrounds, a limited number of relocation support awards are available each year for those who meet our financial eligibility criteria.  Relocation financial support is available for this role, subject to meeting the financial eligibility criteria. Further information will be shared with applicants during the recruitment process. Details on the wider support, initiatives and networks available at the BBC can be found on [our careers site.](https://www.bbc.co.uk/careers/bbc-life/inclusion/sed/)
This is a fixed-term apprenticeship - your contract lasts for the duration of the scheme. Once you have completed your apprenticeship, you will be able to apply for any suitable open vacancies at the BBC or outside in the wider creative industry. You’ll be supported with career development, employability training, and networking opportunities to help you take your next step.
For apprenticeship opportunities, disabled applicants who choose to apply under the Disability Confident Scheme and who meet the minimum criteria for the role will normally be progressed to the next stage of the recruitment process. For most of our campaigns, this would be an online assessment designed to assess your skills, motivations and suitability for the role.  Further details can be found in the [FAQs section of our careers site.](https://www.bbc.co.uk/careers/work/early-careers/faqs/#applicationguidance)
(JPC27)

## **WE ARE BBC STUDIOS**
A globally renowned media company borne of the BBC. We make and distribute the world’s most sought-after TV, audio and digital content. Our ambition is to be the home of the most powerful, entertaining, and inspiring stories for people all around the world.

Join us as an apprentice at the BBC to give yourself the opportunity to kick-start your career in a job you'll love. We’re committed to your skills and talent development. You’ll learn on-the-job, developing your knowledge and skills in an area that interests you, while working towards your apprenticeship qualification with one of our learning providers. 
## **WHY JOIN THIS SCHEME?**
Are you a natural organiser with a passion for media? The Junior Production Coordinator Apprenticeship at the BBC could be your perfect start. You may help with the set-up of filming on location or in the studio for one of our programmes like The One Show or schedule crews and freelancers for Women’s Hour. No media experience or qualifications needed - just enthusiasm and problem-solving skills. Whether you're finishing school or changing careers, this hands-on role offers a pathway into production management at one of the world’s leading broadcasters.

Places on the Junior Production Coordinator Apprenticeship are available across a range of teams at this location, as well as in other locations. You can find details on other placements in this location on the [BBC Early Careers Website.](https://www.bbc.co.uk/careers/earlycareers)

Start your career in Production Management. As a Junior Production Coordinator apprentice, you'll work alongside experienced Production Managers and Production Coordinators, helping to create high-quality content for TV, audio, online and digital platforms.
BBC Studios is the most awarded production company and the biggest independent producer in the UK. **Kids & Family Productions** produces a wide breadth of content for children in the UK, including Unscripted shows, Blue Peter, CBeebies Specials and Playtime Towers. Our Live Action Unit, produces shows such as The Dumping Ground, Odd Squad and Crookhaven. In Animation, we create My Friend Maisy, Rafi the Wishing Wizard and an all new 7+ series called Vanishing Point. At Kids & Family, we cover every genre! 
This apprenticeship could lead to job opportunities as a:
- Production Coordinator
- Production Management Assistant / Production Secretary

As a Junior Production Coordinator Apprentice this is a brilliant opportunity within **Specialist Factual** to learn, grow, and contribute – you may: 
- Assist with shoots, studio setups, crew bookings, and call sheets 
- Booking transport and accommodation
- Support budget management, raising payments for suppliers and broadcasters
- Applying for accreditations/permits/visas
- Learn best practices in health & safety, and compliance
By the end of the apprenticeship, you'll have the skills and confidence to take the next step in your career, applying for roles such as Junior Production Coordinator or Production Management Assistant.

- Learn what [BBC Production Management](https://www.bbc.com/academy-guides/is-tv-production-management-for-me/#:~:text=TV%20production%20management%20is%20the,on%20budget%20and%20on%20time) is and how it helps bring programmes to life
- Watch this video to learn about the day-to-day responsibilities of a [Production Coordinator at BBC Radio Ulster](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Dr8dEqNMucs&t=3s)
This apprenticeship will give you a thorough knowledge and understanding of what it is like to work within a Production Management team and the media industry, which you can then utilise during your time at the BBC and afterwards in the wider industry.   You’ll study for your industry recognised apprenticeship qualification, learning both on the job at the BBC and off the job with our chosen education provider. The academic study involves;
- Attending instructor-led workshops
- Tutorial sessions
- Presentations
- Group work
Throughout your apprenticeship, you will be asked to gather a portfolio of evidence and work on an apprenticeship assessment that demonstrates your learning, while working towards a Level 4 apprenticeship qualification. For more information on this apprenticeship framework you will be studying, please visit detail on the [Junior Production Coordinator Standard.](https://skillsengland.education.gov.uk/apprenticeships/st0792-v1-2)   ## **YOUR SKILLS AND ELIGIBILITY**
We’re interested in your passion for working at the BBC and your enthusiasm for delivering world-class content and operational excellence to our audiences. We’re not focused on your qualifications; instead, we look for potential and offer you the opportunity to apply your transferable strengths and experience to work in different ways. 
If you can bring some of these skills and experiences, along with transferable strengths, we’d love to hear from you and encourage you to apply:
- Have brilliant organisational skills and are great at problem-solving and negotiating
- Great at working with people; a team player and great communicator
- Resilient, responsible and have a calm focused approach to challenging situations
- Flexible, motivated and have an adaptable approach to the pace of work
- Can manage multiple deadlines and demands on your time
- Are an enthusiastic and motivated self-starter, flexible and adaptable to out-of-hours working This scheme is aimed at non-graduates. If you have a degree and you’re interested in similar roles at the BBC, we recommend applying for jobs at the [BBC careers site](https://www.bbc.co.uk/careers/) or having a look at our other apprenticeship schemes. 
## **ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA**
To be eligible for an apprenticeship at the BBC, you must:
- Be 18 years old or over by the time the apprenticeship begins in September 2027. 
- Have lived in the UK continuously for the last three years prior to the start of the apprenticeship. 
- Be legally eligible to work full-time in the UK for the entire duration of the apprenticeship.
- Not currently be enrolled in another apprenticeship programme, whether with the BBC or another organisation.
- Not have completed or hold qualifications in the apprenticeship subject at the same or higher level.
- Identify as disabled under the Equality Act (2010).
To apply for this scheme, you must also:
- For candidates under the age of 19 years on 7 September 2027: To complete the apprenticeship, you must have achieved Maths and English GCSE at Grade 4/C or above or National 5 (Scotland) at C or Functional Skills Level 2 or equivalent qualification. If you have not achieved these qualifications by the start of your apprenticeship, you will be required to achieve Functional Skills Level 2 before the apprenticeship assessment when you take your end-point assessment.
- Must be passionate about the production management side of making content. If it’s the ‘coming up with ideas for content’ side you like about producing content, then the [Level 3 Production Assistant apprenticeship.](https://www.bbc.co.uk/careers/work/early-careers/production/#productionassistantlevel3) will be more suitable for you.

Renowned for innovation, creativity, and world-class storytelling, the NHU brings the wonders of the natural world to audiences through cutting-edge technology, science, and exceptional filmmaking. From landmark series such as Planet Earth 3, Blue Planet 3, Big Cat 24/7, Springwatch and Deadly 60 to live productions and children’s content, the NHU sets the global standard for quality and craft You will learn to complete Production Management duties across a variety of productions and be an integral part of our programme-making teams.   This apprenticeship could lead to job opportunities as a: - Production Coordinator - Production Management Assistant / Production Secretary ## **YOUR KEY RESPONSIBILITIES AND IMPACT** As a Junior Production Coordinator Apprentice this is a brilliant opportunity within **The Natural History Unit (NHU)** to learn, grow, and contribute – you may:  - Assist with shoots, studio setups, crew bookings, and call sheets  - Booking transport and accommodation - Support budget management, raising payments for suppliers and broadcasters - Applying for accreditations/permits/visas - Learn best practices in health & safety, and compliance By the end of the apprenticeship, you'll have the skills and confidence to take the next step in your career, applying for roles such as Junior Production Coordinator or Production Management Assistant. job_description:
Job Description
Job Requisition ID:  55560
Job Closing Date:  24 November 2026
Leicester, GBR, LE1 5LB **Contract Type:** Fixed-Term Apprenticeship, Full-time for 24 months
**Department:** BBC East Midlands News
**Location:** Leicester - Radio Leicester
**Salary:** £26,000 
## **COULD A BBC APPRENTICESHIP BE THE NEXT ROLE FOR YOU?**
Join us as an apprentice at the BBC to give yourself the opportunity to kick-start your career in a job you'll love. We’re committed to your skills and talent development. You’ll learn on-the-job, developing your knowledge and skills in an area that interests you, whilst working towards your apprenticeship qualification with one of our learning providers. 
## **WHY JOIN THIS SCHEME?**
The BBC Level 6 Journalist Apprenticeship (JOA27) offers emerging journalists the opportunity to advance their skills through industry-leading training and hands-on experience. 
Working with industry experts, you’ll contribute to trusted and impactful journalism, telling stories that inform, educate and engage audiences. Alongside this, you’ll work towards a Level 6 apprenticeship and the industry-recognised NCTJ National Qualification in Journalism (NQJ).
**Want to find out more?** Watch recordings from our webinar series on our [Life at the BBC YouTube playlist](https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PLQirbxfWHEPimmLiTI-yrGoMNMV1FRfWK&si=zN5oW9PAy2C6nmDQ) to learn more about this scheme and other opportunities we offer, and hear from current apprentices about their experiences.
## **YOUR KEY RESPONSIBILITIES AND IMPACT**
As a Journalist apprentice, this is a brilliant opportunity to learn, grow and contribute. On this apprenticeship you can expect to: 
- Play a key role in creating trusted, high-quality news content for BBC audiences.
- Grow your storytelling expertise through hands-on experience researching, writing and producing stories on subjects ranging from current affairs and business to sport, culture and politics.
- Learn from experienced journalists, contribute to stories which matter to the public, collaborate with expert teams and develop your career at the world's leading public service media organisation.
You’ll study for your industry recognised apprenticeship qualification, learning both on and off the job.  
This involves weekly virtual webinars and in- person bootcamps at PA Media Academy in London. 
You’ll cover modules such as: Media Law, Advanced Newsgathering, Advanced Storytelling and Advanced Audience, and work towards the National Qualification in Journalism (NQJ). 
 The NQJ is assessed through two exams and a logbook of work.
For more information on what you will study during the scheme, please see the [Journalism Apprenticeship Standard](https://skillsengland.education.gov.uk/apprenticeships/st1490-v2-0) and the [NCTJ](https://www.nctj.com/qualifications-courses/qualifications/national-qualification-in-journalism/) 
## **YOUR SKILLS AND ELIGIBILITY**
We’re interested in your passion for working at the BBC and your enthusiasm for delivering world-class content and operational excellence to our audiences. We’re not focused on your qualifications; instead, we look for potential and offer you the opportunity to apply your transferable strengths and experience to work in different ways.
If you can bring some of these skills and experiences, along with transferable strengths, we’d love to hear from you and encourage you to apply:
- Demonstrate strong journalistic skills and a passion for storytelling.
- Actively follow sports news across a range of platforms.
- Show a fascination with people, communities and the issues shaping the world around us.
- Bring fresh, creative ideas for engaging and reaching new audiences.
- Demonstrate motivation, adaptability and resilience in a fast-paced environment.
This scheme is aimed at people who are already demonstrating their journalistic potential. You may have gained experience through a community or student newspaper, radio station, blog, vlog, podcast or social media content creation. 
We welcome applicants from a range of backgrounds and experiences, including those who have completed the NCTJ Diploma, a Level 5 Journalist Apprenticeship, or another journalism qualification. 
## **ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA**
To be eligible for an apprenticeship at the BBC, you must: 
- Be 18 years old or over by the time the apprenticeship begins in September 2027.
- Have lived in the UK continuously for the last three years prior to the start of the apprenticeship.
- Be legally eligible to work full-time in the UK for the entire duration of the apprenticeship. 
- Not currently be enrolled in another apprenticeship programme, whether with the BBC or another organisation.
- Not already hold a qualification in the same subject area at the same or a higher level than this apprenticeship. 
 To apply for this scheme, you must also:
- Not have previously completed any elements of the National Qualification in Journalism (NQJ).
- Have achieved English GCSE at Grade 4/C or above; or National 5 (Scotland) at C or Functional Skills Level 2; or equivalent qualification.  
Candidates under the age of 19 at the start of the apprenticeship must have achieved Maths and English GCSE at Grade 4/C or above or National 5 (Scotland) at C or Functional Skills Level 2 or equivalent qualification.  If you have not achieved these qualifications by the start of your apprenticeship, you will be required to achieve Functional Skills Level 2 before the end of your apprenticeship. 
## **READY TO APPLY?**
Don’t leave yourself wondering “what if?” this could be your chance to be part of something exciting. See yourself thriving in this role? Just click ‘Apply Now’! 
You’ll create a candidate profile and answer a few questions - **no CV or cover letter needed.** 
If you're eligible, we’ll guide you through the next steps of the process and what to expect. 
You’ll need to live within a commutable distance of where this role is based. Interested in a different location? Check out our other adverts - but please only apply to one. The BBC recognises that you may need to relocate to a new location to take up a BBC Apprenticeship scheme. The cost of relocating can be a barrier for some applicants and where that is a barrier to participation, we want to help where we can. To help ensure our apprenticeship opportunities are accessible to people from a wide range of backgrounds, a limited number of relocation support awards are available each year for those who meet our financial eligibility criteria.  Relocation financial support is available for this role, subject to meeting the financial eligibility criteria. Further information will be shared with applicants during the recruitment process. Details on the wider support, initiatives and networks available at the BBC can be found on [our careers site.](https://www.bbc.co.uk/careers/bbc-life/inclusion/sed/)
This is a fixed-term apprenticeship - your contract lasts for the duration of the scheme. Once you have completed your apprenticeship, you will be able to apply for any suitable open vacancies at the BBC or outside in the wider creative industry. You’ll be supported with career development, employability training, and networking opportunities to help you take your next step.
For apprenticeship opportunities, disabled applicants who choose to apply under the Disability Confident Scheme and who meet the minimum criteria for the role will normally be progressed to the next stage of the recruitment process. For most of our campaigns, this would be an online assessment designed to assess your skills, motivations and suitability for the role.  Further details can be found in the [FAQs section of our careers site.](https://www.bbc.co.uk/careers/work/early-careers/faqs/#applicationguidance)

This job description is a written statement of the essential characteristics of the job, with its principal accountabilities, incorporating a note of the skills, knowledge and experience required for a satisfactory level of performance. This is not intended to be a complete, detailed account of all aspects of the duties involved.
Our apprenticeship roles are also subject to you having the require qualifications that we have deemed to be necessary for your role and the requirement of the training provider for your scheme.  The offer would be subject to you undergoing and meeting the requirements of a skill scan process with the BBC nominated training provider to determine your eligibility.
Please note: If you were to be offered this role, the BBC will conduct Employment screening checks which include Reference checks; Eligibility to work checks; and if applicable to the role, Safeguarding and Adverse media/Social media checks. Any offer made is conditional on these checks being satisfactory.
Before your start date, you may need to disclose any unspent convictions or police charges, in line with our Recruitment policy. This allows us to discuss any support you may need and assess any risks. Failure to disclose may result in the withdrawal of your offer.
We are unable to accept applications via CV and only applications made online will be considered. Please click on the APPLY NOW button to proceed with your application.

Here you will benefit from: •  Excellent career and professional development. •  Fair pay and flexible benefits including a competitive salary package, a 35-hour working week, 25 days annual leave (26 days for BBC Studios), a range of policies to support your work/life balance, a defined pension scheme and discounted dental, health care and gym. •  A values-based organisation where the way we do things is important as what we do.
As an Apprentice you will also receive: •  An industry recognised qualification. •  Industry-leading training through the BBC Academy and our learning providers (this may involve travel to locations across the UK). •  A dedicated Team Manager and Scheme Specialist to help with your development. •  Training and Mentoring by industry professionals.  •  A bespoke BBC apprenticeship experience including apprenticeship development days and membership of the BBC Apprenticeship community. •  Employability and networking training and support to help you secure your next role. •  The opportunity to apply for financial support for relocation subject to eligibility.

AI & Automation Practitioner - Level 4 - London Job Description Job Requisition ID:  55551 Job Closing Date:  24 November 2026 London, GBR, W12 7TP | London, GBR, W1A 1AA **Contract Type:** Fixed-Term Apprenticeship, Full-time for 18 months **Department:** London Operations & HQ Operations  **Location:** London - Broadcast Centre, London - London Broadcasting House **Salary:** £24,650 (+ £5,441 London weighting)  ## **COULD A BBC APPRENTICESHIP BE THE NEXT ROLE FOR YOU?** Join us as an apprentice at the BBC to give yourself the opportunity to kick-start your career in a job you'll love. We’re committed to your skills and talent development. You’ll learn on-the-job, developing your knowledge and skills in an area that interests you, whilst working towards your apprenticeship qualification with one of our learning providers.  ## **WHY JOIN THIS SCHEME?** Join the BBC as an AI & Automation Practitioner and help shape the future of the world's leading public service broadcaster in the digital and AI age. Work on real projects, develop sought-after skills in artificial intelligence, automation, and emerging technologies, and gain hands-on experience delivering innovative solutions that improve how we work and create content. With gold-standard training and a supportive team, you'll play a key role in driving digital transformation across the BBC. Ready to make an impact?   **Want to find out more?** Watch recordings from our webinar series on our [Life at the BBC YouTube playlist](https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PLQirbxfWHEPimmLiTI-yrGoMNMV1FRfWK&si=eCgNZuWfnZICtWz1) to learn more about this scheme and other opportunities we offer, and hear from current apprentices about their experiences. ## **WHY JOIN THE TEAM?** **Media Operations Team:** BBC Media Operations is at the heart of teams delivering incredible content across all our platforms for all audiences. Comprising around nine hundred people, it manages the craft and production operations for the BBC’s news, radio, and some sport services across London, Salford, and Birmingham - capturing, editing, and producing our output 24x7 for TV, radio, and digital platforms. Join us as you develop your AI and Automation Practitioner skills, to help advance operations in our tech spaces and to plan our exciting delivery schedules. **Head Quarter Operations Team:**  Corporate Affairs is a unique department in the BBC that is able to offer several career routes and experiences as well as exposure to a variety of internal and external stakeholders that provides unparalleled access and development opportunities to an Early Careers Apprentice. Your placement may be working with a number of teams including, HQ Team with experience in support roles across the Division; External Comms covering proactive and reactive publicity and corporate support across all genres (News; Content; Press Office); Internal Comms & Engagement providing tailored staff engagement (Staff Survey and DG and Senior Leader Events); Group Partnerships (external stakeholder engagement and events with key BBC partners) and the Policy & Public Affairs team (front line engagement and activity with the UK Government; Public Policy and Regulation as well as the BBC Charter) Our experienced teams are playing a key role in the Charter Renewal process, so we are right at the heart of this and in addition to the opportunities above, will also offer an unprecedented insight to this process from several viewpoints. We are also at the heart of trialing and rolling our AI capabilities throughout our teams, tailoring benefits to each area to upskill our colleagues and deliver improved processes and creativity. ## **YOUR KEY RESPONSIBILITIES AND IMPACT** As an AI & Automation Practitioner (AAP27) apprentice, this is brilliant opportunity to learn, grow, and contribute – you will:   - Gain hands-on experience designing, developing and implementing AI and automation solutions that improve processes, enhance efficiency and support innovation across the BBC.  - Develop your understanding of how emerging technologies, automation tools and artificial intelligence can be applied to solve business challenges and create value for teams and audiences.  - Build technical and analytical skills by working with data, identifying opportunities for automation, testing solutions and measuring their impact on business performance.  - Explore how technology, organisational strategy, data, people and processes work together and learn how AI and automation can drive digital transformation across a complex and dynamic organisation.  You’ll study for your industry recognised apprenticeship qualification, learning both on and off the job.The course blends applied academic and work-based learning to your role, complementing skills, focused on discussion and group work.       For more information on what you will study during the scheme, please see the [AI & Automation Practitioner apprenticeship standard](https://skillsengland.education.gov.uk/apprenticeships/st1512-v2-1). ## **YOUR SKILLS AND ELIGIBILITY** We’re interested in your passion for working at the BBC and your enthusiasm for delivering world-class content and operational excellence to our audiences. We’re not focused on your qualifications; instead, we look for potential and offer you the opportunity to apply your transferable strengths and experience to work in different ways.  If you can bring some of these skills and experiences, along with transferable strengths, we’d love to hear from you and encourage you to apply: - Enjoy identifying opportunities to improve workflow efficiency and productivity using digital tools.   - Has an enquiring mindset ready to evaluate how current systems and processes could be improved by the introduction of low-or no-code solutions including AI-driven automations to make workflows more efficient.  - Support other users to adopt AI, facilitating the responsible, safe and ethical use of AI, automation and digital solutions, ensuring they align with BBC policies.  - Are motivated and self-driven.    This scheme is aimed at **non-graduates.** If you have a degree and you’re interested in similar roles at the BBC, we recommend applying for jobs at the [BBC careers site](https://careers.bbc.co.uk/) or having a look at our other apprenticeship schemes.  ## **ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA** To be eligible for an apprenticeship at the BBC, you must:  - Be 18 years old or over by the time the apprenticeship begins in September 2027. - Have lived in the UK continuously for the last three years prior to the start of the apprenticeship. - Be legally eligible to work full-time in the UK for the entire duration of the apprenticeship.  - Not currently be enrolled in another apprenticeship programme, whether with the BBC or another organisation. - Not already hold a qualification in the same subject area at the same or a higher level than this apprenticeship.   To apply for this scheme, you must also: - Have maths and English GCSE at Grade 4/C or above or National 5 (Scotland) at C or equivalent qualification   ## **READY TO APPLY?** Don’t leave yourself wondering “what if?” this could be your chance to be part of something exciting. See yourself thriving in this role? Just click ‘Apply Now’!  You’ll create a candidate profile and answer a few questions - **no CV or cover letter needed.**  If you're eligible, we’ll guide you through the next steps of the process and what to expect.  You’ll need to live within a commutable distance of where this role is based. Interested in a different location? Check out our other adverts - but please only apply to one.  This is a fixed-term apprenticeship - your contract lasts for the duration of the scheme. Once you have completed your apprenticeship, you will be able to apply for any suitable open vacancies at the BBC or outside in the wider creative industry. You’ll be supported with career development, employability training, and networking opportunities to help you take your next step. For apprenticeship opportunities, disabled applicants who choose to apply under the Disability Confident Scheme and who meet the minimum criteria for the role will normally be progressed to the next stage of the recruitment process. For most of our campaigns, this would be an online assessment designed to assess your skills, motivations and suitability for the role.  Further details can be found in the [FAQs section of our careers site.](https://www.bbc.co.uk/careers/work/early-careers/faqs/#applicationguidance) #LI-DNI ## Disclaimer This job description is a written statement of the essential characteristics of the job, with its principal accountabilities, incorporating a note of the skills, knowledge and experience required for a satisfactory level of performance. This is not intended to be a complete, detailed account of all aspects of the duties involved. Our apprenticeship roles are also subject to you having the require qualifications that we have deemed to be necessary for your role and the requirement of the training provider for your scheme.  The offer would be subject to you undergoing and meeting the requirements of a skill scan process with the BBC nominated training provider to determine your eligibility. Please note: If you were to be offered this role, the BBC will conduct Employment screening checks which include Reference checks; Eligibility to work checks; and if applicable to the role, Safeguarding and Adverse media/Social media checks. Any offer made is conditional on these checks being satisfactory. Before your start date, you may need to disclose any unspent convictions or police charges, in line with our Recruitment policy. This allows us to discuss any support you may need and assess any risks. Failure to disclose may result in the withdrawal of your offer. We are unable to accept applications via CV and only applications made online will be considered. Please click on the APPLY NOW button to proceed with your application. Information at a Glance ## This is your BBC At the BBC you can create and innovate in an inclusive environment while contributing to some of the world’s best loved content, and the BBC’s mission to inform, educate and entertain. [Find out more about the BBC](https://careers.bbc.co.uk/) ## Life at BBC Here you will benefit from: •  Excellent career and professional development. •  Fair pay and flexible benefits including a competitive salary package, a 35-hour working week, 25 days annual leave (26 days for BBC Studios), a range of policies to support your work/life balance, a defined pension scheme and discounted dental, health care and gym. •  A values-based organisation where the way we do things is important as what we do. As an Apprentice you will also receive: •  An industry recognised qualification. •  Industry-leading training through the BBC Academy and our learning providers (this may involve travel to locations across the UK). •  A dedicated Team Manager and Scheme Specialist to help with your development. •  Training and Mentoring by industry professionals.  •  A bespoke BBC apprenticeship experience including apprenticeship development days and membership of the BBC Apprenticeship community. •  Employability and networking training and support to help you secure your next role. •  The opportunity to apply for financial support for relocation subject to eligibility. [Candidate pack](https://www.bbc.co.uk/academy/courses/ec-application/#/) ## You belong We have a working environment where we value and respect every individual's unique contribution, so all our employees feel that they can belong, thrive and achieve their full potential. We want to attract the broadest range of talented people to join us. The more diverse our workforce, the better able we are to respond to and reflect our audiences in all their diversity. We welcome applications from individuals, regardless of age, gender, ethnicity, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, socio-economic background, religion and/or belief. Find out more about diversity, inclusion and belonging in our strategy below. [Diversity, inclusion & belonging strategy](https://www.bbc.co.uk/diversity/) ## Disability confident We take inclusivity seriously and want to ensure all candidates who are disabled or have long-term health conditions receive the support and adjustments they need. If you need to discuss adjustments or access requirements for the recruitment process, or to carry out this role, please contact us via the [Early Careers Recruitment contact form](https://app.smartsheet.com/b/form/fb9285d0c9bb4ebaa7dc7d22615d8305?) and we’d be happy to discuss how we can support you through the process.
