We make and distribute the world’s most sought-after TV, audio and digital content. Our ambition is to be the home of the most powerful, entertaining, and inspiring stories for people around the world. ## **COULD A BBC APPRENTICESHIP BE THE NEXT ROLE FOR YOU?** Join us as an apprentice at the BBC to give yourself the opportunity to kick-start your career in a job you'll love. We’re committed to your skills and talent development. You’ll learn on the job, developing your knowledge and skills in an area that interests you, while working towards your apprenticeship qualification with one of our learning providers.  ## **WHY JOIN THIS SCHEME?** The BBC isn’t just about what you see on screen! Behind every one of our programmes, there is a team that keeps the business running like clockwork. We’re looking for people to be part of this, and contribute to the second to none efficiency of our business operations. If you’re organised, proactive, and can spot the small details that make a big difference, look no further; our Administration Assistant Level 2 Apprenticeship could be your perfect next step!  **Want to find out more?** Watch recordings from our webinar series on our [Life at the BBC YouTube playlist](https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PLQirbxfWHEPimmLiTI-yrGoMNMV1FRfWK&si=eCgNZuWfnZICtWz1) to learn more about this scheme and other opportunities we offer, and hear from current apprentices about their experiences. ## **WHY JOIN THE TEAM?** **Content Sales EMEA (Europe, the Middle East, and Africa): **This is an excellent entry-level opportunity for someone looking to begin their career in media, working in a high-paced, but exciting environment, learning about the television industry alongside being able to develop valuable administrative and organisational skills. Working across multiple teams, responsibilities will include assisting with availability reports and checks, creating PowerPoint presentations, managing diaries, supporting contract administration, and liaising with other teams around the business to support the end-to-end sales process. The successful candidate will be proactive, detail-oriented, eager to learn and confident communicating with colleagues across the business. **Regulatory Affairs:** The Regulatory Affairs Team consists of specialist subject matter experts who advise on compliance with the BBC Code of Conduct, Editorial Standards, Data Protection, Ethical Policy, Sustainability, and Competition and Market separation matters in accordance with the criteria set out in the BBC’s Charter & Agreement. This role offers a great starting point for someone looking to build a career in the media industry. Working in a dynamic and fast-moving environment, the position provides the opportunity to gain valuable experience while strengthening essential administrative, organisational and professional skills. **Content Brand Protection Team:** The Content Protection team works within the Legal functions of BBC Studios to protect any programmes distributed, or produced, by BBC Studios. Utilising various tools we operate on major social media platforms and the wider web to remove BBC Studios content or, in select cases, monetise that content. The Administration Assistant apprentice can expect to be involved in the day to day tasks of the team, making decisions on user-uploaded infringing videos of BBC Studios programming, assisting the team in workflow management, cataloguing incoming reports and performing billing and invoicing tasks.  ## **YOUR KEY RESPONSIBILITIES AND IMPACT** As a Level 2 Administration Assistant (ADA27) apprentice, this is a brilliant opportunity to learn, grow, and contribute – you will:   - Work directly in a BBC team and pull back the curtain on the world’s leading public service broadcaster.  - Provide critical administrative support that keeps the heart of the team beating. - Keep the team on track and ensure deadlines are met, working at pace to solve problems on the job. - Communicate with colleagues across departments, building relationships and networks. - Learn the systems, processes and skills that keep a major global organisation running smoothly. You’ll study for your industry recognised apprenticeship qualification, learning both on and off the job.  This means you’ll spend at least one day a week studying for a Level 2 Administration Assistant apprenticeship with our learning provider, using its virtual delivery platform.       For more information on what you will study during the scheme, please see the [Administration Assisstant apprenticeship standard](https://skillsengland.education.gov.uk/apprenticeships/st1472-v2-0). ## **YOUR SKILLS AND ELIGIBILITY** We’re interested in your passion for working at the BBC and your enthusiasm for delivering world-class content and operational excellence to our audiences. We’re not focused on your qualifications; instead, we look for potential and offer you the opportunity to apply your transferable strengths and experience to work in different ways.  If you can bring some of these skills and experiences, along with transferable strengths, we’d love to hear from you and encourage you to apply:  - **Collaboration** – we want to hear about your ability to work well with others and stakeholders across the organisation, to reach a common goal. - **Organisation** – Hopefully you have a sharp eye for detail and are able to keep your team’s work organised/running efficiently to meet tight deadlines. - **Adaptability** – We’re looking for candidates with an ability to adapt to changing circumstances and working in uncertain situations. - **Motivation for the BBC** – We’re keen to hear about why you want to work at the BBC specifically, and your motivation around pursuing a role in the broadcasting industry.  The Administration Assistant Level 2 apprenticeship is designed to help individuals build the essential skills, confidence and knowledge needed to succeed in an entry-level administration or business support role.  The scheme is therefore not suitable for anyone who has significant qualifications or experience in administration or business support roles. As part of our commitment to building a workforce that reflects all of the audiences we serve, we want to open up more routes into the BBC for people at the very start of their working lives, a group that is currently under-represented across our teams. This scheme is one of the ways we are doing that. See yourself thriving in this role? Just click ‘Apply Now’!  You’ll create a candidate profile and answer a few questions - no CV or cover letter needed.  If you're eligible, we’ll guide you through the next steps of the process and what to expect.  This is a fixed-term apprenticeship - your contract lasts for the duration of the scheme. Once you have completed your apprenticeship, you will be able to apply for any suitable open vacancies at the BBC or outside in the wider creative industry. You’ll be supported with career development, employability training, and networking opportunities to help you take your next step. As an Apprentice you will also receive: •  An industry recognised qualification. •  Industry-leading training through the BBC Academy and our learning providers (this may involve travel to locations across the UK). •  A dedicated Team Manager and Scheme Specialist to help with your development. •  Training and Mentoring by industry professionals.  •  A bespoke BBC apprenticeship experience including apprenticeship development days and membership of the BBC Apprenticeship community. •  Employability and networking training and support to help you secure your next role. •  The opportunity to apply for financial support for relocation subject to eligibility. Job Description
Job Requisition ID:  55840
Job Closing Date:  24 November 2026
London, GBR, W1A 1AA **Contract Type:** Fixed-Term Apprenticeship, Full-time for 15 months
**Department:**  BBC Introducing
**Location:** London - London Broadcasting House
**Salary:** £24,650 (+£5,441 London weighting)
## **COULD A BBC APPRENTICESHIP BE THE NEXT ROLE FOR YOU?**
Join us as an apprentice at the BBC to give yourself the opportunity to kick-start your career in a job you'll love. We’re committed to your skills and talent development. You’ll learn on-the-job, developing your knowledge and skills in an area that interests you, whilst working towards your apprenticeship qualification with one of our learning providers. 
## **WHY JOIN THIS SCHEME?**
The Content Creator apprenticeship is designed to equip you with the skills to create engaging, impactful content across a range of platforms. You’ll learn how to plan and develop creative ideas, research target audiences, and produce audio, visual and written content suitable for different channels. 
This hands-on, immersive programme combines practical workshops, interactive sessions, assignments and collaborative group projects. You’ll gain experience in creating, recording and editing video and audio content, while developing your planning, presentation and pitching skills. The scheme also provides a foundation in photography and imaging, social media and search engine optimisation (SEO), and website creation, giving you a broad understanding of modern digital content production.
**Want to find out more?** Watch recordings from our webinar series on our [Life at the BBC YouTube playlist](https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PLQirbxfWHEPimmLiTI-yrGoMNMV1FRfWK&si=eCgNZuWfnZICtWz1) to learn more about this scheme and other opportunities we offer, and hear from current apprentices about their experiences.
## **WHY JOIN THE TEAM?**
[BBC Introducing](https://www.bbc.co.uk/introducing) supports exciting new music from across the UK. Working within BBC Broadcasting House in London, you’ll listen to new music, carry out research, edit audio, support the management team, create content and will work on live events from Radio 1’s Big Weekend to Glastonbury. We’re looking for someone really passionate about music, events and radio. You'll need to be organised, creative and confident working under pressure in a busy, fast-moving broadcasting environment.  
## **YOUR KEY RESPONSIBILITIES AND IMPACT**
As a Content Creator apprentice, this is brilliant opportunity to learn, grow, and contribute – you could expect to:  
- Play a part in creating trusted, high-quality content for BBC audiences. 
- Grow your storytelling skills through hands-on experience researching, writing, producing and editing content on a range of subjects. 
- Develop your digital content skills by monitoring audience trends and creating content for social media platforms, including selecting and editing clips from programmes for use on social media platforms.  
- Spot opportunities for digital content, including short clips, behind-the-scenes moments, interviews and talent‑led extras. 
- Learn from experienced professionals, collaborate with expert teams and develop your career at the world's largest public service broadcaster. 
You’ll study for your industry recognised apprenticeship qualification, learning both on and off the job.  This means that as well as learning on your placement at the BBC, you’ll also attend learning blocks (up to a week at a time) with our learning provider, working towards an industry recognised apprenticeship qualification - Level 3 Content Creator.  
Learning blocks will be a mixture of in-person and virtual delivery, including attending instructor-led workships, tutorial sessions, presentations and group work.
For more information on what you will study during the scheme, please see the [Content Creator apprenticeship standard.](https://skillsengland.education.gov.uk/apprenticeships/st0105-v2-0) 
As part of the programme, you will be required to travel to attend in-person learning blocks and other apprenticeship-related activities where necessary. 
## **YOUR SKILLS AND ELIGIBILITY**
We’re interested in your passion for working at the BBC and your enthusiasm for delivering world-class content and operational excellence to our audiences. We’re not focused on your qualifications; instead, we look for potential and offer you the opportunity to apply your transferable strengths and experience to work in different ways. 
If you can bring some of these skills and experiences, along with transferable strengths, we’d love to hear from you and encourage you to apply:
- Bring fresh, creative ideas for engaging and reaching new audiences.   
- A genuine consumer of content who follows what is happening across platforms like TikTok, YouTube and Instagram. 
- Adaptable and versatile, able to switch between serious, issue‑based content and fun, high-energy entertainment. 
- A collaborative team player who is organised, motivated, adaptable and thrive in a fast-paced environment. 
- Passionate about your own self-development, showing the discipline and commitment required to complete the apprenticeship. 
This scheme is aimed at **non-graduates.** If you have a degree and you’re interested in similar roles at the BBC, we recommend applying for jobs at the [BBC careers site](https://careers.bbc.co.uk/) or having a look at our other apprenticeship schemes. 
## **ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA**
To be eligible for an apprenticeship at the BBC, you must: 
- Be 18 years old or over by the time the apprenticeship begins in September 2027.
- Have lived in the UK continuously for the last three years prior to the start of the apprenticeship.
- Be legally eligible to work full-time in the UK for the entire duration of the apprenticeship. 
- Not currently be enrolled in another apprenticeship programme, whether with the BBC or another organisation.
- No prior learning is required to apply.
- If you already have relevant experience or qualifications, your individual learning plan may be adjusted to reflect this – meaning you could complete your apprenticeship in less time.
For candidates under the age of 19 years at 8th September 2027: To complete the apprenticeship, you must have achieved Maths and English GCSE at Grade 4/C or above or National 5 (Scotland) at C or Functional Skills Level 2 or equivalent qualification. If you have not achieved these qualifications by the start of your apprenticeship, you will be required to achieve Functional Skills Level 2 before the end of your apprenticeship when you take your end-point assessment.   
## **READY TO APPLY?**
Don’t leave yourself wondering “what if?” this could be your chance to be part of something exciting. See yourself thriving in this role? Just click ‘Apply Now’! 
You’ll create a candidate profile and answer a few questions - **no CV or cover letter needed.** 
If you're eligible, we’ll guide you through the next steps of the process and what to expect. 
You’ll need to live within a commutable distance of where this role is based. Interested in a different location? Check out our other adverts - but please only apply to one. 
This is a fixed-term apprenticeship - your contract lasts for the duration of the scheme. Once you have completed your apprenticeship, you will be able to apply for any suitable open vacancies at the BBC or outside in the wider creative industry. You’ll be supported with career development, employability training, and networking opportunities to help you take your next step.
For apprenticeship opportunities, disabled applicants who choose to apply under the Disability Confident Scheme and who meet the minimum criteria for the role will normally be progressed to the next stage of the recruitment process. For most of our campaigns, this would be an online assessment designed to assess your skills, motivations and suitability for the role.  Further details can be found in the [FAQs section of our careers site.](https://www.bbc.co.uk/careers/work/early-careers/faqs/#applicationguidance)

## **COULD A BBC APPRENTICESHIP BE THE NEXT ROLE FOR YOU?**
Join us as an apprentice at the BBC Studios to give yourself the opportunity to kick-start your career in a job you'll love. We’re committed to your skills and talent development. You’ll learn on-the-job, developing your knowledge and skills in an area that interests you, while working towards your apprenticeship qualification with one of our learning providers. 
## **WHY JOIN THIS SCHEME?**
The Content Creator apprenticeship is designed to equip you with the skills to create engaging, impactful content across a range of platforms. You’ll learn how to plan and develop creative ideas, research target audiences, and produce audio, visual and written content suitable for different channels. 
This hands-on, immersive programme combines practical workshops, interactive sessions, assignments and collaborative group projects. You’ll gain experience in creating, recording and editing video and audio content, while developing your planning, presentation and pitching skills. The scheme also provides a foundation in photography and imaging, social media and search engine optimisation (SEO), and website creation, giving you a broad understanding of modern digital content production.
**Want to find out more?** Watch recordings from our webinar series on our [Life at the BBC YouTube playlist](https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PLQirbxfWHEPimmLiTI-yrGoMNMV1FRfWK&si=eCgNZuWfnZICtWz1) to learn more about this scheme and other opportunities we offer, and hear from current apprentices about their experiences.
## **WHY JOIN THE TEAM?**
BBC Studios Digital are a content creation and publishing team, who manage the digital accounts of some of the world’s best loved entertainment brands including Bluey, Top Gear, Doctor Who and BBC Earth. This role would sit within the Digital Content team, who are responsible for content development and production across all digital platforms. We commission original pieces, respond to commercial branded briefs, and produce over 12,000 pieces of written, graphic, and video content per year.
## **YOUR KEY RESPONSIBILITIES AND IMPACT**
As a Content Creator apprentice, this is brilliant opportunity to learn, grow, and contribute – you could expect to:  
- Play a part in creating trusted, high-quality content for BBC audiences.
- Grow your storytelling skills through hands-on experience researching, writing, producing and editing content on a range of subjects.
- Develop your digital content skills by monitoring audience trends and creating content for social media platforms, including selecting and editing clips from programmes for use on social media platforms.  
- Spot opportunities for digital content, including short clips, behind-the-scenes moments, interviews and talent‑led extras.
- Learn from experienced professionals, collaborate with expert teams and develop your career at the world's largest public service broadcaster. 
You’ll study for your industry recognised apprenticeship qualification, learning both on and off the job. This means that as well as learning on your placement at the BBC, you’ll also attend learning blocks (up to a week at a time) with our learning provider, working towards an industry recognised apprenticeship qualification - Level 3 Content Creator.
Learning blocks will be a mixture of in-person and virtual delivery, including attending instructor-led workships, tutorial sessions, presentations and group work.
For more information on what you will study during the scheme, please see the [Content Creator apprenticeship standard.](https://skillsengland.education.gov.uk/apprenticeships/st0105-v2-0)
## **YOUR SKILLS AND ELIGIBILITY**
We’re interested in your passion for working at the BBC and your enthusiasm for delivering world-class content and operational excellence to our audiences. We’re not focused on your qualifications; instead, we look for potential and offer you the opportunity to apply your transferable strengths and experience to work in different ways. 
If you can bring some of these skills and experiences, along with transferable strengths, we’d love to hear from you and encourage you to apply:  
- Bring fresh, creative ideas for engaging and reaching new audiences.  
- A genuine consumer of content who follows what is happening across platforms like TikTok, YouTube and Instagram.
- Adaptable and versatile, able to switch between serious, issue‑based content and fun, high-energy entertainment.
- A collaborative team player who is organised, motivated, adaptable and thrive in a fast-paced environment.
- Passionate about your own self-development, showing the discipline and commitment required to complete the apprenticeship. 
This scheme is aimed at **non-graduates.** If you have a degree and you’re interested in similar roles at the BBC, we recommend applying for jobs at the [BBC careers site](https://careers.bbc.co.uk/) or having a look at our other apprenticeship schemes. 
## **ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA**
To be eligible for an apprenticeship at the BBC, you must:
- Identify as disabled under the Equality Act (2010).
- Be 18 years old or over by the time the apprenticeship begins in September 2027.
- Have lived in the UK continuously for the last three years prior to the start of the apprenticeship.
- Be legally eligible to work full-time in the UK for the entire duration of the apprenticeship.
- Not currently be enrolled in another apprenticeship programme, whether with the BBC or another organisation.
- No prior learning is required to apply.
- If you already have relevant experience or qualifications, your individual learning plan may be adjusted to reflect this – meaning you could complete your apprenticeship in less time. For candidates under the age of 19 years at 8th September 2027: To complete the apprenticeship, you must have achieved Maths and English GCSE at Grade 4/C or above or National 5 (Scotland) at C or Functional Skills Level 2 or equivalent qualification. If you have not achieved these qualifications by the start of your apprenticeship, you will be required to achieve Functional Skills Level 2 before the end of your apprenticeship when you take your end-point assessment.

You’ll create a candidate profile and answer a few questions - **no CV or cover letter needed.** 
If you're eligible, we’ll guide you through the next steps of the process and what to expect. 
You’ll need to live within a commutable distance of where this role is based. Interested in a different location? Check out our other adverts - but please only apply to one. This is a fixed-term apprenticeship - your contract lasts for the duration of the scheme.  Once you have completed your apprenticeship you will be able to apply for any suitable open vacancies at the BBC or outside in the wider creative industry. Join us as an apprentice at BBC Studios to give yourself the opportunity to kick-start your career in a job you'll love. We’re committed to your skills and talent development. The Content Creator apprenticeship is designed to equip you with the skills to create engaging, impactful content across a range of platforms. You’ll learn how to plan and develop creative ideas, research target audiences, and produce audio, visual and written content suitable for different channels. 
This hands-on, immersive programme combines practical workshops, interactive sessions, assignments and collaborative group projects. You’ll gain experience in creating, recording and editing video and audio content, while developing your planning, presentation and pitching skills. The scheme also provides a foundation in photography and imaging, social media and search engine optimisation (SEO), and website creation, giving you a broad understanding of modern digital content production.

## **WHY JOIN THE TEAM?**
BBC Studios Audio produces an expansive portfolio including hit podcasts, vodcasts and iconic radio including Desert Island Discs, You’re Dead to Me, Strong Message Here, Things Fell Apart and In Our Time. With drama, factual and comedy and entertainment teams delivering world-class audio and digital content to audiences around the world, BBC Studios Audio produced over 600 hours of content in the last year - winning 33 awards internationally.

- Play a part in creating trusted, high-quality content for BBC audiences. 
- Grow your storytelling skills through hands-on experience researching, writing, producing and editing content on a range of subjects. 
-  Develop your digital content skills by monitoring audience trends and creating content for social media platforms, including selecting and editing clips from programmes for use on social media platforms.  
- Spot opportunities for digital content, including short clips, behind-the-scenes moments, interviews and talent‑led extras. 
- Learn from experienced professionals, collaborate with expert teams and develop your career at the world's largest public service broadcaster.

- Bring fresh, creative ideas for engaging and reaching new audiences.   
- A genuine consumer of content who follows what is happening across platforms like TikTok, YouTube and Instagram. 
- Adaptable and versatile, able to switch between serious, issue‑based content and fun, high-energy entertainment. 
- A collaborative team player who is organised, motivated, adaptable and thrive in a fast-paced environment. 
- Passionate about your own self-development, showing the discipline and commitment required to complete the apprenticeship.

- Be 18 years old or over by the time the apprenticeship begins in September 2027.
- Have lived in the UK continuously for the last three years prior to the start of the apprenticeship.
- Be legally eligible to work full-time in the UK for the entire duration of the apprenticeship. 
- Not currently be enrolled in another apprenticeship programme, whether with the BBC or another organisation.

You’ll create a candidate profile and answer a few questions - **no CV or cover letter needed.** 
If you're eligible, we’ll guide you through the next steps of the process and what to expect. 
You’ll need to live within a commutable distance of where this role is based. Interested in a different location? Check out our other adverts - but please only apply to one.

## **WHY JOIN THIS SCHEME?**
Do you enjoy maths, spotting patterns in data, or working with Excel? Kick-start your career with the BBC as a Data Analyst Apprentice. You'll work on real projects, learn from industry experts, and help shape a data-driven future. Best of all, we'll teach you Python coding from scratch, giving you valuable skills for the future. If you're curious, enjoy teamwork, and love solving problems, we'd love to hear from you. 
**Want to find out more?** Watch recordings from our webinar series on our  [Life at the BBC YouTube playlist](https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PLQirbxfWHEPimmLiTI-yrGoMNMV1FRfWK&si=eCgNZuWfnZICtWz1) to learn more about this scheme and other opportunities we offer, and hear from current apprentices about their experiences.
## **WHY JOIN THE TEAM?**
**Audience Team:** 
The Audiences team helps the BBC make better decisions by providing insight into audience behaviour, needs and perceptions. We combine audience research, data analysis, digital analytics and strategic insight to help teams across the BBC understand who our audiences are, how they use BBC services, and how we can better serve them.
As an Early Careers Apprentice, you'll gain experience across different areas of audience insight and analytics, working with research and data specialists to support projects that inform strategic and editorial decision-making. You'll develop practical skills in research, analysis, stakeholder engagement and project delivery while working on real business challenges.
As part of the Audiences department, apprentices will support the day-to-day delivery of audience insight, research and analytics projects. They will have opportunities to work with a range of teams and develop experience in both qualitative and quantitative research approaches, digital analytics, audience measurement and insight communication.
**Typical activities may include:**
- Supporting the production of regular audience reporting, insight updates and presentations.
- Assisting with qualitative and quantitative research projects, including questionnaire design, fieldwork preparation, analysis and reporting.
- Conducting desk research and gathering information from a variety of audience, industry and market intelligence sources.
- Supporting digital analytics and audience measurement activities, helping to identify trends and patterns in audience behaviour.
- Assisting with project coordination and administration across research, analytics and strategic insight projects.
- Contributing to the interpretation and communication of audience data and research findings to colleagues across the BBC.
- Working with stakeholders from different teams to understand business questions and support evidence-based decision making.
- Learning how audience insight, research and analytics are used to shape BBC products, content and services.
- Developing skills in data literacy, storytelling, presentation and professional communication.
We're looking for people who are curious about audiences, data, media and technology, and who are keen to learn in a professional environment.
## **YOUR KEY RESPONSIBILITIES AND IMPACT**
As a Data Analyst apprentice (DAA27), this is brilliant opportunity to learn, grow, and contribute – you will:   
- Work with real data to uncover trends, solve problems and support decision-making.  
- Learn how data helps shape services, projects and performance across the organisation.  
- Develop skills in collecting, analysing and presenting data, turning information into clear insights.  
- Create reports and visualisations that help colleagues understand and act on data.  
- Understand the importance of data privacy, ethics and responsible data use 
You’ll study for your industry recognised apprenticeship qualification, learning both on and off the job. This means you’ll spend at least one day a week studying for a Level 4 Data Analyst qualification with our learning provider Cambridge Spark using its virtual delivery platform.    
For more information on what you will study during the scheme, please see the [Data Analyst apprenticeship standard.](https://skillsengland.education.gov.uk/apprenticeships/st0118-v1-1)

If you can bring some of these skills and experiences, along with transferable strengths, we’d love to hear from you and encourage you to apply:
- Enjoy working with data, numbers and excel spreadsheets, with an interest in maths and logical thinking. 
- Have brilliant organisational skills and are great at problem-solving and negotiating     
- Can manage multiple deadlines and demands on your time     
- Have a calm and focused approach to changing circumstances     
- Have a keen interest in the BBC and how people consume content, bursting with fresh ideas to introduce new perspectives      
- Are an enthusiastic self-starter, flexible and adaptable to out-of-hours working   
This scheme is aimed at **non-graduates.** If you have a degree and you’re interested in similar roles at the BBC, we recommend applying for jobs at the [BBC careers site](https://careers.bbc.co.uk/) or having a look at our other apprenticeship schemes. 
## **ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA**
To be eligible for an apprenticeship at the BBC, you must: 
- Be 18 years old or over by the time the apprenticeship begins in September 2027.
- Have lived in the UK continuously for the last three years prior to the start of the apprenticeship.
- Be legally eligible to work full-time in the UK for the entire duration of the apprenticeship. 
- Not currently be enrolled in another apprenticeship programme, whether with the BBC or another organisation.
- Not already hold a qualification in the same subject area at the same or a higher level than this apprenticeship. 
 To apply for this scheme, you must also:
- Have maths and English GCSE at Grade 4/C or above or National 5 (Scotland) at C or equivalent qualification    
- Have achieved, or expected to achieve, by the start of the scheme A Level/Higher Maths

You’ll need to live within a commutable distance of where this role is based. Interested in a different location? Check out our other adverts - but please only apply to one.

The cost of relocating can be a barrier for some applicants and where that is a barrier to participation, we want to help where we can. To help ensure our apprenticeship opportunities are accessible to people from a wide range of backgrounds, a limited number of relocation support awards are available each year for those who meet our financial eligibility criteria.  Relocation financial support might be available for this role, subject to meeting the financial eligibility criteria. ## **COULD A BBC APPRENTICESHIP BE THE NEXT ROLE FOR YOU?**
Join us as an apprentice at the BBC to give yourself the opportunity to kick-start your career in a job you'll love. We’re committed to your skills and talent development. You’ll learn on-the-job, developing your knowledge and skills in an area that interests you, whilst working towards your apprenticeship qualification with one of our learning providers. 
## **WHY JOIN THIS SCHEME?**
Do you enjoy maths, spotting patterns in data, or working with Excel? Kick-start your career with the BBC as a Data Analyst Apprentice. You'll work on real projects, learn from industry experts, and help shape a data-driven future. Best of all, we'll teach you Python coding from scratch, giving you valuable skills for the future. If you're curious, enjoy teamwork, and love solving problems, we'd love to hear from you. 
**Want to find out more?** Watch recordings from our webinar series on our  [Life at the BBC YouTube playlist](https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PLQirbxfWHEPimmLiTI-yrGoMNMV1FRfWK&si=eCgNZuWfnZICtWz1) to learn more about this scheme and other opportunities we offer, and hear from current apprentices about their experiences.
## **WHY JOIN THE TEAM?**
The News Data and Payments Team are a small team supporting our 24/7 global News operation.
We design, build and maintain data solutions in Excel, Smartsheet, Power Query, Power Automate and Power BI.
Areas we manage include mandatory training; hostile environments training around the world; taxi usage, make-up usage; workforce utilisation, and Press Card requests.
This is a very exciting time to join our team, we look forward to meeting you! 
## **YOUR KEY RESPONSIBILITIES AND IMPACT**
As a Data Analyst apprentice (DAA27), this is brilliant opportunity to learn, grow, and contribute – you will:   
- Work with real data to uncover trends, solve problems and support decision-making.  
- Learn how data helps shape services, projects and performance across the organisation.  
- Develop skills in collecting, analysing and presenting data, turning information into clear insights.  
- Create reports and visualisations that help colleagues understand and act on data.  
- Understand the importance of data privacy, ethics and responsible data use 
You’ll study for your industry recognised apprenticeship qualification, learning both on and off the job. This means you’ll spend at least one day a week studying for a Level 4 Data Analyst qualification with our learning provider Cambridge Spark using its virtual delivery platform.    
For more information on what you will study during the scheme, please see the [Data Analyst apprenticeship standard.](https://skillsengland.education.gov.uk/apprenticeships/st0118-v1-1) 
## **YOUR SKILLS AND ELIGIBILITY**
We’re interested in your passion for working at the BBC and your enthusiasm for delivering world-class content and operational excellence to our audiences. We’re not focused on your qualifications; instead, we look for potential and offer you the opportunity to apply your transferable strengths and experience to work in different ways. 
If you can bring some of these skills and experiences, along with transferable strengths, we’d love to hear from you and encourage you to apply:
- Enjoy working with data, numbers and excel spreadsheets, with an interest in maths and logical thinking. 
- Have brilliant organisational skills and are great at problem-solving and negotiating     
- Can manage multiple deadlines and demands on your time     
- Have a calm and focused approach to changing circumstances     
- Have a keen interest in the BBC and how people consume content, bursting with fresh ideas to introduce new perspectives      
- Are an enthusiastic self-starter, flexible and adaptable to out-of-hours working   
This scheme is aimed at **non-graduates.** If you have a degree and you’re interested in similar roles at the BBC, we recommend applying for jobs at the [BBC careers site](https://careers.bbc.co.uk/) or having a look at our other apprenticeship schemes. 
## **ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA**
To be eligible for an apprenticeship at the BBC, you must: 
- Be 18 years old or over by the time the apprenticeship begins in September 2027.
- Have lived in the UK continuously for the last three years prior to the start of the apprenticeship.
- Be legally eligible to work full-time in the UK for the entire duration of the apprenticeship. 
- Not currently be enrolled in another apprenticeship programme, whether with the BBC or another organisation.
- Not already hold a qualification in the same subject area at the same or a higher level than this apprenticeship. 
 To apply for this scheme, you must also:
- Have maths and English GCSE at Grade 4/C or above or National 5 (Scotland) at C or equivalent qualification    
- Have achieved, or expected to achieve, by the start of the scheme A Level/Higher Maths   
## **READY TO APPLY?**
Don’t leave yourself wondering “what if?” this could be your chance to be part of something exciting. See yourself thriving in this role? Just click ‘Apply Now’! 
You’ll create a candidate profile and answer a few questions - **no CV or cover letter needed.** 
If you're eligible, we’ll guide you through the next steps of the process and what to expect. 
You’ll need to live within a commutable distance of where this role is based. Interested in a different location? Check out our other adverts - but please only apply to one. 
This is a fixed-term apprenticeship - your contract lasts for the duration of the scheme. Once you have completed your apprenticeship, you will be able to apply for any suitable open vacancies at the BBC or outside in the wider creative industry. We make and distribute the world’s most sought-after TV, audio and digital content. Our ambition is to be the home of the most powerful, entertaining, and inspiring stories for people all around the world. ## **COULD A BBC APPRENTICESHIP BE THE NEXT ROLE FOR YOU?** Join us as an apprentice at BBC Studios to give yourself the opportunity to kick-start your career in a job you'll love. We’re committed to your skills and talent development. You’ll learn on the job, developing your knowledge and skills in an area that interests you, while working towards your apprenticeship qualification with one of our learning providers.  ## **WHY JOIN THIS SCHEME?** Data Science is evolving the way the BBC operates. Our data scientists help us to better understand the customers we serve, and the content served to them, turning raw data into valuable insights and products to better serve audience needs. Whether audiences are watching on BBC iPlayer, listening on BBC Sounds, reading BBC News and BBC Sport articles or learning on BBC Bitesize, behind the scenes data scientists are at work...fancy being one of them?!   **Want to find out more?** Watch recordings from our webinar series on our [Life at the BBC YouTube playlist](https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PLQirbxfWHEPimmLiTI-yrGoMNMV1FRfWK&si=eCgNZuWfnZICtWz1) to learn more about this scheme and other opportunities we offer, and hear from current apprentices about their experiences. ## **WHY JOIN THE TEAM?** **Ad Sales Strategy & Business Intelligence Team:**  The BI Data Solutions team sits within BBC Studios’ Global Ad Sales Strategy & Business Intelligence function. We turn advertising and sales data into trusted information that helps teams understand performance, identify opportunities and make better commercial decisions. We develop the datasets, reporting tools and analytical capabilities that support our global advertising business. As a Data Science apprentice, you could help explore and analyse commercial data, investigate trends in advertising performance and turn findings into clear insights for colleagues. You could also support the development of dashboards, help check and improve data quality, and contribute to datasets and automated reporting on our Snowflake data platform.With support from experienced analysts and technical colleagues, you’ll develop practical skills in data analysis, coding and visualisation, while learning how to work with business teams to answer real commercial questions. As your skills grow, there may also be opportunities to contribute to forecasting and explore how AI-assisted analytics can support the team’s work. **Data Analystics & Data Science Team:**  The apprentice will move between the data analytics and the data science team in Studios. The analytics team focusses on preparing data from a wide range of sources, understanding the meaning behind it and making it available to stakeholders. The data scientists work with the same data, building statistical models or using AI to gain insights into the underlying structure or make predictions. The apprentice will start in the analytics team, learning the fundamentals about our data and its applications. They will then spend some time with the data scientists to gain experience with the different modelling and machine learning techniques. ## **YOUR KEY RESPONSIBILITIES AND IMPACT** As a Data Scientist (DSD27) apprentice, this is brilliant opportunity to learn, grow, and contribute – you will:    - Learn about the value of data to organisations like the BBC.   - Discover how the BBC uses data to both improve its connection with audiences and improve internal tooling and workflows.   -  Be part of a team using data to enhance the way the BBC operates, using AI and machine learning approaches to deliver valuable audience insights and products.   - Learn about and contribute to all aspects of the Data Science lifecycle from inception to production deployment and beyond, including aspects such as cleansing and validating data and building and evaluating predictive models.    You’ll study for your industry recognised apprenticeship qualification, learning both on and off the job. This means you’ll spend at least one day a week studying for a BSc (Hons) in Data Science with BPP University remotely studying topics including:    - Artificial Intelligence and Deep Learning     - Machine Learning    - Data Infrastructure & Tools   - Data Visualisation & Dashboards    For more information on what you will study during the scheme, please see the [Data Scientist degree apprenticeship standard.](https://skillsengland.education.gov.uk/apprenticeships/st0585-v1-1) ## **YOUR SKILLS AND ELIGIBILITY** We’re interested in your passion for working at the BBC and your enthusiasm for delivering world-class content and operational excellence to our audiences. We’re not focused on your qualifications; instead, we look for potential and offer you the opportunity to apply your transferable strengths and experience to work in different ways.  If you can bring some of these skills and experiences, along with transferable strengths, we’d love to hear from you and encourage you to apply: - Have a love of maths  and a passion for data, machine learning and AI   - An excitement to embrace the latest AI and Machine Learning Technologies responsibly to transform working practices   - Have brilliant non-technical skills such as problem-solving, organisation and negotiation   - Flexibility and adaptability including a calm and focused approach to working within an evolving technical landscape and workplace.     - Can manage multiple deadlines and demands on your time    - Bursting with fresh ideas to introduce new perspectives with a keen interest in the BBC, it’s public service mission and values.  This scheme is aimed at **non-graduates.** If you have a degree and you’re interested in similar roles at the BBC, we recommend applying for jobs at the [BBC careers site](https://careers.bbc.co.uk/) or having a look at our other apprenticeship schemes.  ## **ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA** To be eligible for an apprenticeship at the BBC, you must:  - Be 18 years old or over by the time the apprenticeship begins in September 2027. - Have lived in the UK continuously for the last three years prior to the start of the apprenticeship. - Be legally eligible to work full-time in the UK for the entire duration of the apprenticeship.  - Not currently be enrolled in another apprenticeship programme, whether with the BBC or another organisation. - Not already hold a qualification in the same subject area at the same or a higher level than this apprenticeship.   To apply for this scheme, you must also: - Have maths and English GCSE at Grade 4/C or above or National 5 (Scotland) at C or equivalent qualification     - Have achieved, or expected to achieve, by the start of the scheme, a minimum of 104 UCAS points.   - This must include A Level/Higher Maths, or an extended BTEC in Engineering with Engineering Maths, or an equivalent qualification.    ## **READY TO APPLY?** Don’t leave yourself wondering “what if?” this could be your chance to be part of something exciting. See yourself thriving in this role? Just click ‘Apply Now’!  You’ll create a candidate profile and answer a few questions - no CV or cover letter needed.  If you're eligible, we’ll guide you through the next steps of the process and what to expect.  This is a fixed-term apprenticeship - your contract lasts for the duration of the scheme. Once you have completed your apprenticeship, you will be able to apply for any suitable open vacancies at the BBC or outside in the wider creative industry. You’ll be supported with career development, employability training, and networking opportunities to help you take your next step. You’ll need to live within a commutable distance of where this role is based. Interested in a different location? Check out our other adverts - but please only apply to one. For apprenticeship opportunities, disabled applicants who choose to apply under the Disability Confident Scheme and who meet the minimum criteria for the role will normally be progressed to the next stage of the recruitment process. For most of our campaigns, this would be an online assessment designed to assess your skills, motivations and suitability for the role.  Further details can be found in the [FAQs section of our careers site.](https://www.bbc.co.uk/careers/work/early-careers/faqs/#applicationguidance) #LI-DNI  ## Disclaimer This job description is a written statement of the essential characteristics of the job, with its principal accountabilities, incorporating a note of the skills, knowledge and experience required for a satisfactory level of performance. This is not intended to be a complete, detailed account of all aspects of the duties involved. Our apprenticeship roles are also subject to you having the require qualifications that we have deemed to be necessary for your role and the requirement of the training provider for your scheme.  The offer would be subject to you undergoing and meeting the requirements of a skill scan process with the BBC nominated training provider to determine your eligibility. Any offer made is conditional on these checks being satisfactory. Before your start date, you may need to disclose any unspent convictions or police charges, in line with our Recruitment policy. This allows us to discuss any support you may need and assess any risks. Failure to disclose may result in the withdrawal of your offer. We are unable to accept applications via CV and only applications made online will be considered. Please click on the APPLY NOW button to proceed with your application. Information at a Glance ## This is your BBC At the BBC you can create and innovate in an inclusive environment while contributing to some of the world’s best loved content, and the BBC’s mission to inform, educate and entertain. [Find out more about the BBC](https://careers.bbc.co.uk/) ## Life at BBC Here you will benefit from: •  Excellent career and professional development. •  Fair pay and flexible benefits including a competitive salary package, a 35-hour working week, 25 days annual leave (26 days for BBC Studios), a range of policies to support your work/life balance, a defined pension scheme and discounted dental, health care and gym. •  A values-based organisation where the way we do things is important as what we do. As an Apprentice you will also receive: •  An industry recognised qualification. •  Industry-leading training through the BBC Academy and our learning providers (this may involve travel to locations across the UK). •  A dedicated Team Manager and Scheme Specialist to help with your development. •  Training and Mentoring by industry professionals.  •  A bespoke BBC apprenticeship experience including apprenticeship development days and membership of the BBC Apprenticeship community. •  Employability and networking training and support to help you secure your next role. •  The opportunity to apply for financial support for relocation subject to eligibility. [Candidate pack](https://www.bbc.co.uk/academy/courses/ec-application/#/) ## You belong We have a working environment where we value and respect every individual's unique contribution, so all our employees feel that they can belong, thrive and achieve their full potential. We want to attract the broadest range of talented people to join us. The more diverse our workforce, the better able we are to respond to and reflect our audiences in all their diversity. We welcome applications from individuals, regardless of age, gender, ethnicity, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, socio-economic background, religion and/or belief. Find out more about diversity, inclusion and belonging in our strategy below. [Diversity, inclusion & belonging strategy](https://www.bbc.co.uk/diversity/) ## Disability confident We take inclusivity seriously and want to ensure all candidates who are disabled or have long-term health conditions receive the support and adjustments they need. **Location:**  London - London Broadcasting House

## **COULD A BBC APPRENTICESHIP BE THE NEXT ROLE FOR YOU?**
Join us as an apprentice at the BBC to give yourself the opportunity to kick-start your career in a job you'll love. We’re committed to your skills and talent development. You’ll learn on-the-job, developing your knowledge and skills in an area that interests you, whilst working towards your apprenticeship qualification with one of our learning providers. 
## **WHY JOIN THIS SCHEME?**
The Junior Journalist Apprenticeship (JRA27) is perfect for curious and creative individuals with a passion for storytelling. Whether you're finishing school, college, or exploring an alternative to university, this programme offers an exciting opportunity to kick-start your journalism career with the world's leading public service media organisation.
You'll gain hands-on experience covering stories that matter to audiences, learning from experienced journalists and developing the skills needed to create trusted journalism.  
Alongside this, you’ll work towards both the NCTJ Diploma in Journalism and a Level 5 apprenticeship qualification.
**Want to find out more?** Watch recordings from our webinar series on our [Life at the BBC YouTube playlist](https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PLQirbxfWHEPimmLiTI-yrGoMNMV1FRfWK&si=zN5oW9PAy2C6nmDQ) to learn more about this scheme and other opportunities we offer, and hear from current apprentices about their experiences.
## **YOUR KEY RESPONSIBILITIES AND IMPACT**
 As a Junior Journalist apprentice, this is a brilliant opportunity to learn, grow and contribute. On this team you can expect to: 
- Work alongside experienced journalists developing your skills while creating high-quality content.
- Get hands on experience including researching stories, booking guests and writing briefs.  
- Discover and develop compelling stories, assisting with interviews that bring important issues to life for diverse audiences.
- Learn from industry experts at the world's largest public service broadcaster.
You’ll study for your industry-recognised apprenticeship qualification, learning both on and off the job. 
This involves weekly virtual webinars + in-person bootcamps at PA Media Academy in London. 
You’ll cover a range of modules for the NCTJ Diploma including: 
- Media Law
- Essential Journalism
- Broadcast Journalism
- Journalism for a Digital Audience
- Video Journalism
Modules will be assessed through exams, coursework and a portfolio of work.  
For more information on what you will study during the scheme, please see the [Journalism Apprenticeship Standard](https://skillsengland.education.gov.uk/apprenticeships/st1516-v1-0).
## **YOUR SKILLS AND ELIGIBILITY**
We’re interested in your passion for working at the BBC and your enthusiasm for delivering world-class content and operational excellence to our audiences. We’re not focused on your qualifications; instead, we look for potential and offer you the opportunity to apply your transferable strengths and experience to work in different ways. 
If you can bring some of these skills and experiences, along with transferable strengths, we’d love to hear from you and encourage you to apply:
- You're naturally curious about people and what’s happening in the world around you, with a keen interest in news.
- You’re full of creative ideas and enjoy finding innovative ways to tell engaging stories.
- You love finding things out, asking questions and getting to the heart of a story.
- You have a real enthusiasm for writing and enjoy communicating complex ideas in a clear, compelling way.
- You thrive in a fast-paced environment, bringing flexibility, motivation and a willingness to adapt as priorities change.
This scheme is aimed at **non-graduates**. If you have a degree and you’re interested in similar roles at the BBC, we recommend applying for jobs at the [BBC careers site](https://careers.bbc.co.uk/) or having a look at our other apprenticeship schemes. 
## **ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA**
To be eligible for an apprenticeship at the BBC, you must: 
- Be 18 years old or over by the time the apprenticeship begins in September 2027.
- Have lived in the UK continuously for the last three years prior to the start of the apprenticeship.
- Be legally eligible to work full-time in the UK for the entire duration of the apprenticeship. 
- Not currently be enrolled in another apprenticeship programme, whether with the BBC or another organisation.
- Not already hold a qualification in the same subject area at the same or a higher level than this apprenticeship. 
 To apply for this scheme, you must also:
- Not have completed or be studying for the NCTJ diploma or a journalism qualification at the same level or higher.
- Have achieved English GCSE at Grade 4/C or above, or National 5 (Scotland) at C or Functional Skills Level 2 or equivalent qualification.
For candidates under the age of 19 years at the start of the apprenticeship: To complete the apprenticeship, you must have achieved Maths and English GCSE at Grade 4/C or above or National 5 (Scotland) at C or Functional Skills Level 2 or equivalent qualification to pass the apprenticeship.

You’ll create a candidate profile and answer a few questions - **no CV or cover letter needed.** 
If you're eligible, we’ll guide you through the next steps of the process and what to expect. 
You’ll need to live within a commutable distance of where this role is based. Interested in a different location? Check out our other adverts - but please only apply to one. ## **WE ARE BBC STUDIOS**
A globally renowned media company borne of the BBC. We make and distribute the world’s most sought-after TV, audio and digital content. Our ambition is to be the home of the most powerful, entertaining, and inspiring stories for people all around the world. 
## **COULD A BBC APPRENTICESHIP BE THE NEXT ROLE FOR YOU?**
Join us as an apprentice at the BBC to give yourself the opportunity to kick-start your career in a job you'll love. We’re committed to your skills and talent development. You’ll learn on-the-job, developing your knowledge and skills in an area that interests you, whilst working towards your apprenticeship qualification with one of our learning providers. 
## **WHY JOIN THIS SCHEME?**
This is your chance to launch a career at the very heart of British broadcasting. We're looking for individuals with a passion to find out how we make content and bring ideas to life. Depending on your placement area, you could be working behind the scenes on exciting productions, from gripping dramas to the thrill of live radio, and gain a recognised qualification while learning on the job. This is your opportunity to broaden your production knowledge while working on content that matters to millions. 
**Want to find out more?** Watch recordings from our webinar series on our [Life at the BBC YouTube playlist](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLQirbxfWHEPimmLiTI-yrGoMNMV1FRfWK) to learn more about this scheme and other opportunities we offer, and hear from current apprentices about their experiences.
Places on the Production Assistant Apprenticeship are available across a range of teams at this location, as well as in other locations. You can find details on other placements in this location on the [BBC Early Careers website.](https://www.bbc.co.uk/careers/work/early-careers/production/#productionassistantlevel3)
## **WHY JOIN THE TEAM?**
Based in Elstree, you will be working on the long-running multi-award winning drama series, EastEnders.  Working in the Production Office, you’ll gain an understanding in all aspects of how the production works with a specific focus on the Editorial.  You will be given a broad range of tasks and experiences to equip you for a future career in an Editorial environment
As a Production Assistant Apprentice at the BBC, you'll gain hands-on experience across a range of projects, from supporting high-profile productions to contributing to content enjoyed by audiences across the UK. You'll work alongside experienced professionals, develop practical skills and play an active role in bringing creative ideas to life. This apprenticeship could lead to job opportunities as a:
- Junior Researcher
- Runner
- Content or Edit Assistant
## **YOUR KEY RESPONSIBILITIES AND IMPACT**
As a Production Assistant Apprentice within **BBC Studios - Scripted Drama - Editorial**, this is a brilliant opportunity to learn, grow, and contribute. You could be:
- Helping to develop ideas and stories by researching content and finding guests and participants.
- Gaining real-life experience by assisting your team on location, in the studio, or in a TV gallery and helping out on the studio floor.
- Learning to use technical equipment and specialist software by supporting teams with cameras, sound, lighting, and editing.
- Creating content for multiple platforms, including social media, under the guidance of experienced professionals.
You’ll study for your industry recognised apprenticeship qualification, learning both on and off the job.  This means that as well as learning on your placement at the BBC, you’ll also attend learning blocks (up to a week at a time) with our learning provider, working towards an industry recognised apprenticeship qualification - Level 3 Production Assistant. Learning blocks will be a mixture of in-person and virtual delivery including tutorial sessions, presentations and group work.
As part of the programme, you will be required to travel to attend in-person learning blocks and other apprenticeship-related activities where necessary.
For more information on this apprenticeship standard you will be studying, please see detail on the [Production Assistant apprenticeship standard](https://skillsengland.education.gov.uk/apprenticeships/st0341-v2-0).
## **YOUR SKILLS AND ELIGIBILITY**
We’re interested in your passion for working at the BBC and your enthusiasm for delivering world-class content and operational excellence to our audiences. We’re not focused on your qualifications; instead, we look for potential and offer you the opportunity to apply your transferable strengths and experience to work in different ways. 
If you can bring some of these skills and experiences, along with transferable strengths, we’d love to hear from you and encourage you to apply:
- Passionate and curious about content, and the production process at the BBC  
- Brimming with new ideas and fresh perspectives for BBC content
- A great team player who can deal with unexpected challenges  
- Flexible and have an adaptable approach to work to help enable our content to be delivered.
This scheme is aimed at **non-graduates.** If you have a degree and you’re interested in similar roles at the BBC, we recommend applying for jobs at the [BBC careers site](https://www.bbc.co.uk/careers/) or having a look at our other apprenticeship schemes. 
## **ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA**
To be eligible for an apprenticeship at the BBC, you must: 
- Be 18 years old or over by the time the apprenticeship begins in September 2027
- Have lived in the UK continuously for the last three years prior to the start of the apprenticeship
- Be legally eligible to work full-time in the UK for the entire duration of the apprenticeship
- Not currently be enrolled in another apprenticeship programme, whether with the BBC or another organisation
For candidates under the age of 19 years on 7 September 2027: To complete the apprenticeship, you must have achieved Maths and English GCSE at Grade 4/C or above or National 5 (Scotland) at C or Functional Skills Level 2 or equivalent qualification. If you have not achieved these qualifications by the start of your apprenticeship, you will be required to achieve Functional Skills Level 2 before the apprenticeship assessment when you take your end-point assessment.

Don’t leave yourself wondering “what if?” this could be your chance to be part of something exciting. See yourself thriving in this role? Just click ‘Apply Now’! 
You’ll create a candidate profile and answer a few questions - **no CV or cover letter needed.** 
If you're eligible, we’ll guide you through the next steps of the process and what to expect. 
You’ll need to live within a commutable distance of where this role is based. Interested in a different location? Check out our other adverts - but please only apply to one. This is a fixed-term apprenticeship - your contract lasts for the duration of the scheme. Once you have completed your apprenticeship, you will be able to apply for any suitable open vacancies at the BBC or outside in the wider creative industry. You’ll be supported with career development, employability training, and networking opportunities to help you take your next step.
For apprenticeship opportunities, disabled applicants who choose to apply under the Disability Confident Scheme and who meet the minimum criteria for the role will normally be progressed to the next stage of the recruitment process. For most of our campaigns, this would be an online assessment designed to assess your skills, motivations and suitability for the role.  Further details can be found in the [FAQs section of our careers site.](https://www.bbc.co.uk/careers/work/early-careers/faqs/#applicationguidance)

Job Description
Job Requisition ID:  55916
Job Closing Date:  24 November 2026
London, GBR, W12 7FA **CONTRACT TYPE:** Fixed-term Apprenticeship, Full-time for 13 months **DEPARTMENT:** Entertainment Development Team **LOCATION**: London - Television Centre **SALARY:** £24,650 \[+£5,441 London weighting\]
## **WE ARE BBC STUDIOS**
A globally renowned media company borne of the BBC. We make and distribute the world’s most sought-after TV, audio and digital content. Our ambition is to be the home of the most powerful, entertaining, and inspiring stories for people all around the world. 
## **COULD A BBC APPRENTICESHIP BE THE NEXT ROLE FOR YOU?**
Join us as an apprentice at the BBC to give yourself the opportunity to kick-start your career in a job you'll love. We’re committed to your skills and talent development. You’ll learn on-the-job, developing your knowledge and skills in an area that interests you, whilst working towards your apprenticeship qualification with one of our learning providers. 
## **WHY JOIN THIS SCHEME?**
This is your chance to launch a career at the very heart of British broadcasting. We're looking for individuals with a passion to find out how we make content and bring ideas to life. Depending on your placement area, you could be working behind the scenes on exciting productions, from gripping dramas to the thrill of live radio, and gain a recognised qualification while learning on the job. This is your opportunity to broaden your production knowledge while working on content that matters to millions. 
**Want to find out more?** Watch recordings from our webinar series on our [Life at the BBC YouTube playlist](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLQirbxfWHEPimmLiTI-yrGoMNMV1FRfWK) to learn more about this scheme and other opportunities we offer, and hear from current apprentices about their experiences.
Places on the Production Assistant Apprenticeship are available across a range of teams at this location, as well as in other locations. You can find details on other placements in this location on the [BBC Early Careers website.](https://www.bbc.co.uk/careers/work/early-careers/production/#productionassistantlevel3)
## **WHY JOIN THE TEAM?**
**BBC Studios TalentWorks** is the key unit within BBC Studios, dedicated to identifying and developing emerging and established creators through original commissioned content, digital-first series, and curated live events. We work to support our digital brands including Bluey, Doctor Who, BBC Earth and Funny Parts.
As a Production Assistant Apprentice at the BBC, you'll gain hands-on experience across a range of projects, from supporting high-profile productions to contributing to content enjoyed by audiences across the UK. You'll work alongside experienced professionals, develop practical skills and play an active role in bringing creative ideas to life. This apprenticeship could lead to job opportunities as a:
- Junior Researcher
- Runner
- Content or Edit Assistant
## **YOUR KEY RESPONSIBILITIES AND IMPACT**
As a Production Assistant Apprentice within **BBC Studios TalentWorks**, this is a brilliant opportunity to learn, grow, and contribute. You could be:
- Helping to develop ideas and stories by researching content and finding guests and participants.
- Gaining real-life experience by assisting your team on location, in the studio, or in a TV gallery and helping out on the studio floor.
- Learning to use technical equipment and specialist software by supporting teams with cameras, sound, lighting, and editing.
- Creating content for multiple platforms, including social media, under the guidance of experienced professionals.
You’ll study for your industry recognised apprenticeship qualification, learning both on and off the job.  This means that as well as learning on your placement at the BBC, you’ll also attend learning blocks (up to a week at a time) with our learning provider, working towards an industry recognised apprenticeship qualification - Level 3 Production Assistant. Learning blocks will be a mixture of in-person and virtual delivery including tutorial sessions, presentations and group work.
As part of the programme, you will be required to travel to attend in-person learning blocks and other apprenticeship-related activities where necessary.
For more information on this apprenticeship standard you will be studying, please see detail on the [Production Assistant apprenticeship standard](https://skillsengland.education.gov.uk/apprenticeships/st0341-v2-0).
## **YOUR SKILLS AND ELIGIBILITY**
We’re interested in your passion for working at the BBC and your enthusiasm for delivering world-class content and operational excellence to our audiences. We’re not focused on your qualifications; instead, we look for potential and offer you the opportunity to apply your transferable strengths and experience to work in different ways. 
If you can bring some of these skills and experiences, along with transferable strengths, we’d love to hear from you and encourage you to apply:
- Passionate and curious about content, and the production process at the BBC  
- Brimming with new ideas and fresh perspectives for BBC content
- A great team player who can deal with unexpected challenges  
- Flexible and have an adaptable approach to work to help enable our content to be delivered.
This scheme is aimed at **non-graduates.** If you have a degree and you’re interested in similar roles at the BBC, we recommend applying for jobs at the [BBC careers site](https://www.bbc.co.uk/careers/) or having a look at our other apprenticeship schemes. 
## **ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA**
To be eligible for an apprenticeship at the BBC, you must: 
- Be 18 years old or over by the time the apprenticeship begins in September 2027
- Have lived in the UK continuously for the last three years prior to the start of the apprenticeship
- Be legally eligible to work full-time in the UK for the entire duration of the apprenticeship
- Not currently be enrolled in another apprenticeship programme, whether with the BBC or another organisation
For candidates under the age of 19 years on 7 September 2027: To complete the apprenticeship, you must have achieved Maths and English GCSE at Grade 4/C or above or National 5 (Scotland) at C or Functional Skills Level 2 or equivalent qualification. If you have not achieved these qualifications by the start of your apprenticeship, you will be required to achieve Functional Skills Level 2 before the apprenticeship assessment when you take your end-point assessment.  
## **READY TO APPLY?**
Don’t leave yourself wondering “what if?” this could be your chance to be part of something exciting. See yourself thriving in this role? Just click ‘Apply Now’! 
You’ll create a candidate profile and answer a few questions - **no CV or cover letter needed.** 
If you're eligible, we’ll guide you through the next steps of the process and what to expect. 
You’ll need to live within a commutable distance of where this role is based. Interested in a different location? Check out our other adverts - but please only apply to one. This is a fixed-term apprenticeship - your contract lasts for the duration of the scheme. Once you have completed your apprenticeship, you will be able to apply for any suitable open vacancies at the BBC or outside in the wider creative industry. You’ll be supported with career development, employability training, and networking opportunities to help you take your next step.
For apprenticeship opportunities, disabled applicants who choose to apply under the Disability Confident Scheme and who meet the minimum criteria for the role will normally be progressed to the next stage of the recruitment process. For most of our campaigns, this would be an online assessment designed to assess your skills, motivations and suitability for the role.  Further details can be found in the [FAQs section of our careers site.](https://www.bbc.co.uk/careers/work/early-careers/faqs/#applicationguidance)

## JOB DETAILS
JOB TITLE: SAP Principal Systems Engineer JOB REF: 54761  JOB BAND: D CONTRACT TYPE: Permanent, Full-time DEPARTMENT: BBC Technology Group LOCATION: London or Cardiff; Hybrid 2 days per week in office PROPOSED SALARY RANGE: £70,000 - £80,000 depending on relevant skills, knowledge and experience. The expected salary range for this role reflects internal benchmarking and external market insights. CLOSING: 23:59 on Friday 6th of November 2026 PROPOSED INTERVIEWS: To commence the week of the 23rd November 2026_\*please note that this may subject to change_ We're happy to discuss flexible working. If you'd like to, please indicate your preference in the application – though there's no obligation to do so now. Flexible working will be part of the discussion at offer stage. 
**Interview Process**:
1 x 45 minute Values and Behaviours competency-based interview and technical questions
## PURPOSE OF THE ROLE
Join the BBC’s Technology & Media Operations team to help shape the future of our corporate systems. In this role, you’ll influence strategy and drive innovation across finance platforms, focusing on SAP and partner solutions. You’ll contribute to delivering and managing complex technical changes and optimising systems to maximise value and align with BBC business goals. If you’re passionate about using technology to create meaningful impact, this is your opportunity to support the evolution of the BBC’s financial systems.
WHY JOIN THE TEAM
You will be joining a small, established team that work well together in a rapidly developing and transformative space. You will have the opportunity to pick up new skills and Best Practice ways of working which help drive efficiency and Value for Money. The team are currently engaged in an exciting transformation in the Finance and Procurement space, which you will be a contributor to.
## YOUR KEY RESPONSIBILITIES AND IMPACT:
⦁    Contribute to a technical roadmap for systems and services within their scope ⦁    Acting as a Co-ordinator for Small/Medium technical changes, clarifying requirements submitted by BBC Business Users and managing a change process followed by an outsourced technology provider, including Documentation Review, Technical Build, Testing Cycles, Production Deployment and Post Go-Live support ⦁    Acting as a trusted team member for larger projects with technical change elements, working closely with Project Management and Project Stakeholders to deliver timely, high-quality outcomes ⦁    Building relationships with Internal and External stakeholders, offering support and influence focussed on best practice, achievable goals ⦁    Working with Outsourced Technology partners and Internal Stakeholders to support the resolution of Incidents at varied severity levels
## YOUR SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE
**ESSENTIAL CRITERIA:**
⦁     Extensive experience and specialist knowledge of the Finance modules within SAP ECC and SAP S/4HANA, with a strong focus on best-practice configurations, and their alignment with business requirements.  ⦁     Experienced in translating project, business, user and product requirements into effective technical and functional solutions, balancing multiple priorities and competing demands, guiding outcomes to ensure solutions are effectively designed, delivered, supported and improved.  ⦁     Strong technical expertise in SAP ECC6 and S/4HANA integrations across finance, sales, reporting, and third-party platforms, leveraging APIs, middleware, IDocs, web services, and event-driven architectures. Deep knowledge of SAP FI/CO, Project Systems, Intercompany, Tax, Fixed Assets and Banking, with extensive integration experience across MM, BW, SD and HR. ⦁     Demonstratable and relevant recent experience of working within a complex SAP landscape and in reviewing technical and functional documentation, identifying and revising based on SAP best practice, quality, clarity and completeness. ⦁     Strong stakeholder management and leadership skills, with the ability to engage, influence and build credibility with senior business leaders, product owners, architects, engineers, suppliers and delivery teams. Able to communicate complex technical concepts in a clear and audience-appropriate manner, lead requirement gathering, evaluate solution options and provide recommendations aligned to engineering standards and strategic objectives.
If you can bring some of these skills and experience, along with transferable strengths, we’d love to hear from you and encourage you to apply.
Before your start date, you may need to disclose any unspent convictions or police charges, in line with our Contracts of Employment policy. This allows us to discuss any support you may need and assess any risks. Failure to disclose may result in the withdrawal of your offer.
