Job Description
Job Requisition ID:  55691
Job Closing Date:  24 November 2026
Londonderry, GBR, BT48 7JD **CONTRACT TYPE:** Fixed-term Apprenticeship, Full-time for 13 months **DEPARTMENT:** Radio Ulster/Foyle  **LOCATION**: Londonderry - Radio Foyle **SALARY:** £24,650
## **COULD A BBC APPRENTICESHIP BE THE NEXT ROLE FOR YOU?**
Join us as an apprentice at the BBC to give yourself the opportunity to kick-start your career in a job you'll love. We’re committed to your skills and talent development. You’ll learn on-the-job, developing your knowledge and skills in an area that interests you, whilst working towards your apprenticeship qualification with one of our learning providers. 
## **WHY JOIN THIS SCHEME?**
This is your chance to launch a career at the very heart of British broadcasting. We're looking for individuals with a passion to find out how we make content and bring ideas to life. Depending on your placement area, you could be working behind the scenes on exciting productions, from gripping dramas to the thrill of live radio, and gain a recognised qualification while learning on the job. This is your opportunity to broaden your production knowledge while working on content that matters to millions. 
**Want to find out more?** Watch recordings from our webinar series on our [Life at the BBC YouTube playlist](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLQirbxfWHEPimmLiTI-yrGoMNMV1FRfWK) to learn more about this scheme and other opportunities we offer, and hear from current apprentices about their experiences.
Places on the Production Assistant Apprenticeship are available across a range of teams at this location, as well as in other locations. You can find details on other placements in this location on the [BBC Early Careers website.](https://www.bbc.co.uk/careers/work/early-careers/production/#productionassistantlevel3)
## **WHY JOIN THE TEAM?**
Your Place and Mine celebrates the people, places and communities that make Northern Ireland unique. Across Radio Ulster, Radio Foyle, BBC Sounds, podcasts, YouTube and social media, the team tells original stories that are often overlooked by traditional news coverage, giving a platform to underserved voices and positive community stories. As an apprentice, you'll work alongside experienced journalists and presenter, Eve Blair, helping to research, develop and produce content from idea to broadcast. You'll gain hands-on experience across radio, podcasting, digital and video production while building valuable storytelling skills and audience connections.
As a Production Assistant Apprentice at the BBC, you'll gain hands-on experience across a range of projects, from supporting high-profile productions to contributing to content enjoyed by audiences across the UK. You'll work alongside experienced professionals, develop practical skills and play an active role in bringing creative ideas to life. This apprenticeship could lead to job opportunities as a:
- Junior Researcher
- Runner
- Content or Edit Assistant
## **YOUR KEY RESPONSIBILITIES AND IMPACT**
As a Production Assistant Apprentice within **Radio Ulster/Foyle**, this is a brilliant opportunity to learn, grow, and contribute. You could be:
- Helping to develop ideas and stories by researching content and finding guests and participants.
- Gaining real-life experience by assisting your team on location, in the studio, or in a TV gallery and helping out on the studio floor.
- Learning to use technical equipment and specialist software by supporting teams with cameras, sound, lighting, and editing.
- Creating content for multiple platforms, including social media, under the guidance of experienced professionals.
You’ll study for your industry recognised apprenticeship qualification, learning both on and off the job.  This means that as well as learning on your placement at the BBC, you’ll also attend learning blocks (up to a week at a time) with our learning provider, working towards an industry recognised apprenticeship qualification - Level 3 Production Assistant. Learning blocks will be a mixture of in-person and virtual delivery including tutorial sessions, presentations and group work.
As part of the programme, you will be required to travel to attend in-person learning blocks and other apprenticeship-related activities where necessary.
For more information on this apprenticeship standard you will be studying, please see detail on the [Production Assistant Level 3 Standard.](https://skillsengland.education.gov.uk/apprenticeships/st0341-v2-0) 
## **YOUR SKILLS AND ELIGIBILITY**
We’re interested in your passion for working at the BBC and your enthusiasm for delivering world-class content and operational excellence to our audiences. We’re not focused on your qualifications; instead, we look for potential and offer you the opportunity to apply your transferable strengths and experience to work in different ways. 
If you can bring some of these skills and experiences, along with transferable strengths, we’d love to hear from you and encourage you to apply:
- Passionate and curious about content, and the production process at the BBC  
- Brimming with new ideas and fresh perspectives for BBC content
- A great team player who can deal with unexpected challenges  
- Flexible and have an adaptable approach to work to help enable our content to be delivered.
This scheme is aimed at **non-graduates.** If you have a degree and you’re interested in similar roles at the BBC, we recommend applying for jobs at the [BBC careers site](https://www.bbc.co.uk/careers/) or having a look at our other apprenticeship schemes. 
## **ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA**
To be eligible for an apprenticeship at the BBC, you must: 
- Be 18 years old or over by the time the apprenticeship begins in September 2027
- Have lived in the UK continuously for the last three years prior to the start of the apprenticeship
- Be legally eligible to work full-time in the UK for the entire duration of the apprenticeship
- Not currently be enrolled in another apprenticeship programme, whether with the BBC or another organisation
For candidates under the age of 19 years on 7 September 2027: To complete the apprenticeship, you must have achieved Maths and English GCSE at Grade 4/C or above or National 5 (Scotland) at C or Functional Skills Level 2 or equivalent qualification. If you have not achieved these qualifications by the start of your apprenticeship, you will be required to achieve Functional Skills Level 2 before the apprenticeship assessment when you take your end-point assessment.  
## **READY TO APPLY?**
Don’t leave yourself wondering “what if?” this could be your chance to be part of something exciting. See yourself thriving in this role? Just click ‘Apply Now’! 
You’ll create a candidate profile and answer a few questions - **no CV or cover letter needed.** 
If you're eligible, we’ll guide you through the next steps of the process and what to expect. 
You’ll need to live within a commutable distance of where this role is based. Interested in a different location? Check out our other adverts - but please only apply to one.
The BBC recognises that you may need to relocate to a new location to take up a BBC Apprenticeship scheme. The cost of relocating can be a barrier for some applicants and where that is a barrier to participation, we want to help where we can. To help ensure our apprenticeship opportunities are accessible to people from a wide range of backgrounds, a limited number of relocation support awards are available each year for those who meet our financial eligibility criteria.  Relocation financial support is available for this role, subject to meeting the financial eligibility criteria. Further information will be shared with applicants during the recruitment process. Details on the wider support, initiatives and networks available at the BBC can be found on [our careers site.](https://www.bbc.co.uk/careers/bbc-life/inclusion/sed/)
This is a fixed-term apprenticeship - your contract lasts for the duration of the scheme. Once you have completed your apprenticeship, you will be able to apply for any suitable open vacancies at the BBC or outside in the wider creative industry. You’ll be supported with career development, employability training, and networking opportunities to help you take your next step.
For apprenticeship opportunities, disabled applicants who choose to apply under the Disability Confident Scheme and who meet the minimum criteria for the role will normally be progressed to the next stage of the recruitment process. For most of our campaigns, this would be an online assessment designed to assess your skills, motivations and suitability for the role.  Further details can be found in the [FAQs section of our careers site.](https://www.bbc.co.uk/careers/work/early-careers/faqs/#applicationguidance)

The scheme also provides a foundation in photography and imaging, social media and search engine optimisation (SEO), and website creation, giving you a broad understanding of modern digital content production.

[BBC Introducing](https://www.bbc.co.uk/introducing) supports exciting new music from across the UK. Working within [BBC Radio Northampton](https://www.bbc.co.uk/sounds/play/live/bbc_radio_northampton), you’ll listen to new music, carry out research, edit audio, support programme teams, create content and may help deliver live events. You’ll work on the BBC Introducing in the Three Counties and Northamptonshire show and collaborate remotely with BBC Introducing in The Channel Islands. We’re looking for someone passionate about music, radio and social media. You'll need to be organised, creative and confident working under pressure in a busy, fast-moving broadcasting environment. You must live in the area you’re applying for.  
## **YOUR KEY RESPONSIBILITIES AND IMPACT**
As a Content Creator apprentice, this is brilliant opportunity to learn, grow, and contribute – you could expect to:  
- Play a part in creating trusted, high-quality content for BBC audiences. 
- Grow your storytelling skills through hands-on experience researching, writing, producing and editing content on a range of subjects. 
- Develop your digital content skills by monitoring audience trends and creating content for social media platforms, including selecting and editing clips from programmes for use on social media platforms.  
- Spot opportunities for digital content, including short clips, behind-the-scenes moments, interviews and talent‑led extras. 
- Learn from experienced professionals, collaborate with expert teams and develop your career at the world's largest public service broadcaster. 
You’ll study for your industry recognised apprenticeship qualification, learning both on and off the job.  This means that as well as learning on your placement at the BBC, you’ll also attend learning blocks (up to a week at a time) with our learning provider, working towards an industry recognised apprenticeship qualification - Level 3 Content Creator.  
Learning blocks will be a mixture of in-person and virtual delivery, including attending instructor-led workships, tutorial sessions, presentations and group work.
For more information on what you will study during the scheme, please see the [Content Creator apprenticeship standard.](https://skillsengland.education.gov.uk/apprenticeships/st0105-v2-0)

If you can bring some of these skills and experiences, along with transferable strengths, we’d love to hear from you and encourage you to apply:
- Bring fresh, creative ideas for engaging and reaching new audiences.   
- A genuine consumer of content who follows what is happening across platforms like TikTok, YouTube and Instagram. 
- Adaptable and versatile, able to switch between serious, issue‑based content and fun, high-energy entertainment. 
- A collaborative team player who is organised, motivated, adaptable and thrive in a fast-paced environment. 
- Passionate about your own self-development, showing the discipline and commitment required to complete the apprenticeship. 
This scheme is aimed at **non-graduates.** If you have a degree and you’re interested in similar roles at the BBC, we recommend applying for jobs at the [BBC careers site](https://careers.bbc.co.uk/) or having a look at our other apprenticeship schemes. 
## **ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA**
To be eligible for an apprenticeship at the BBC, you must: 
- Be 18 years old or over by the time the apprenticeship begins in September 2027.
- Have lived in the UK continuously for the last three years prior to the start of the apprenticeship.
- Be legally eligible to work full-time in the UK for the entire duration of the apprenticeship. 
- Not currently be enrolled in another apprenticeship programme, whether with the BBC or another organisation.
- No prior learning is required to apply.

For candidates under the age of 19 years at 8th September 2027: To complete the apprenticeship, you must have achieved Maths and English GCSE at Grade 4/C or above or National 5 (Scotland) at C or Functional Skills Level 2 or equivalent qualification. You’ll create a candidate profile and answer a few questions - **no CV or cover letter needed.** 
If you're eligible, we’ll guide you through the next steps of the process and what to expect. 
You’ll need to live within a commutable distance of where this role is based. Interested in a different location? Check out our other adverts - but please only apply to one.

Job Requisition ID: 55992
Job Closing Date: 24 November 2026
Norwich, GBR, NR2 1TF **Contract Type:** Fixed-Term Apprenticeship, Full-time for 25 months
**Department:** East Operations a0
**Location:** Norwich - The Forum
**Salary:** a324,650 a0
## **COULD A BBC APPRENTICESHIP BE THE NEXT ROLE FOR YOU?**
Join us as an apprentice at the BBC to give yourself the opportunity to kick-start your career in a job you'll love. We’re committed to your skills and talent development. You’ll learn on-the-job, developing your knowledge and skills in an area that interests you, whilst working towards your apprenticeship qualification with one of our learning providers. a0
## **WHY JOIN THIS SCHEME?**
Working alongside journalists and programme makers is a dedicated team of technical operators who make sure the broadcast equipment and technology side of our business runs smoothly. a0This apprenticeship is an exciting entry-level opportunity to join the BBC across the UK; working at the front end of technical operating in sound and/or vision in the newsroom ingest hubs, galleries, studios, post-production areas, and out on location. a0
**Want to find out more?** Watch recordings from our webinar series on our [Life at the BBC YouTube playlis](https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PLQirbxfWHEPimmLiTI-yrGoMNMV1FRfWK&si=eCgNZuWfnZICtWz1)t to learn more about this scheme and other opportunities we offer, and hear from current apprentices about their experiences.
## **WHY JOIN THE TEAM?**
The BBC’s broadcast services are at the heart of communities across the UK; telling stories that matter to people, on TV, radio, online and via our wider digital services. Through this apprenticeship opportunity, you could be part of the next generation of highly skilled Technical Operators.
## **YOUR KEY RESPONSIBILITIES AND IMPACT**
As a0a Broadcast Technical Operator apprentice (BOA27), this is a brilliant opportunity to learn, grow, and contribute you will: a0
- Gain practical experience across all aspects of live and recorded broadcasting, including camera operations on location, studio-based technical roles, directing, lighting, editing, and graphic design for regional and national BBC programmes
- Contribute to the delivery of high-quality content for BBC shows, using advanced broadcast technologies such as satellite trucks and IP systems for outside broadcasts
- Develop a strong understanding of how technical production, editorial decisions, and audience engagement work together to shape compelling content across TV, digital, and online platforms.
You’ll study for your industry recognised apprenticeship qualification, learning both on and off the job. a0 Your learning with the National Film and Television School will introduce you to a wide variety of skills across both TV and Radio, including: a0
- Camera Operations
- Floor Management a0
- TV Vision Mixing a0
- Sound Operations a0
- Technical Directing a0
- Shoot and Edit Multi-Skilled Operator a0
- Picture and Audio Editing a0
- Ingest and Library functions.
As part of the programme, you will be required to travel to attend in-person learning blocks and other apprenticeship-related activities where necessary. For more information on what you will study during the scheme, please see the [Broadcast & Media Systems Technical Operator standard](https://skillsengland.education.gov.uk/apprenticeships/st0424-v1-2). a0
## **YOUR SKILLS AND ELIGIBILITY**
We’re interested in your passion for working at the BBC and your enthusiasm for delivering world-class content and operational excellence to our audiences. We’re not focused on your qualifications; instead, we look for potential and offer you the opportunity to apply your transferable strengths and experience to work in different ways. a0
If you can bring some of these skills and experiences, along with transferable strengths, we’d love to hear from you and encourage you to apply:
- Passionate about media content and the technical production side of how that content reaches the audience
- Can work calmly under pressure
- Fascinated by how things work
- Brilliant organisational skills and are great at problem-solving
- Enthusiastic self-starter, flexible and adaptable to out-of-hours working.
This scheme is aimed at **non-graduates.** If you have a degree and you’re interested in similar roles at the BBC, we recommend applying for jobs at the [BBC careers site](https://careers.bbc.co.uk/) or having a look at our other apprenticeship schemes. a0
## **ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA**
To be eligible for an apprenticeship at the BBC, you must:
- Be 18 years old or over by the time the apprenticeship begins in September 2027
- Have lived in the UK continuously for the last three years prior to the start of the apprenticeship
- Be legally eligible to work full-time in the UK for the entire duration of the apprenticeship
- Not currently be enrolled in another apprenticeship programme, whether with the BBC or another organisation
- Not already hold a qualification in the same subject area at the same or a higher level than this apprenticeship. a0
a0To apply for this scheme, you must also:
- Not have completed or hold qualifications in the apprenticeship subject at level 3 or above
- Not have completed or hold an extended BTEC or degree in media, television, film, audio or radio production
- Have little or no work experience in the subject area
- For candidates under the age of 19 years on 7 September 2027: To complete the apprenticeship, you must have achieved Maths and English GCSE at Grade 4/C or above or National 5 (Scotland) at C or Functional Skills Level 2 or equivalent qualification. If you have not achieved these qualifications by the start of your apprenticeship, you will be required to achieve Functional Skills Level 2 before the apprenticeship assessment when you take your end-point assessment. a0
## **READY TO APPLY?**
Don’t leave yourself wondering what if?” this could be your chance to be part of something exciting. See yourself thriving in this role? Just click ‘Apply Now’!
You’ll create a candidate profile and answer a few questions - **no CV or cover letter needed.**
If you're eligible, we’ll guide you through the next steps of the process and what to expect.
You’ll need to live within a commutable distance of where this role is based. Interested in a different location? Check out our other adverts - but please only apply to one.
The BBC recognises that you may need to relocate to a new location to take up a BBC Apprenticeship scheme. The cost of relocating can be a barrier for some applicants and where that is a barrier to participation, we want to help where we can. To help ensure our apprenticeship opportunities are accessible to people from a wide range of backgrounds, a limited number of relocation support awards are available each year for those who meet our financial eligibility criteria. a0Relocation financial support is available for this role, subject to meeting the financial eligibility criteria. Further information will be shared with applicants during the recruitment process. Details on the wider support, initiatives and networks available at the BBC can be found on our [careers site.](https://www.bbc.co.uk/careers/bbc-life/inclusion/sed/)
This is a fixed-term apprenticeship - your contract lasts for the duration of the scheme. Once you have completed your apprenticeship, you will be able to apply for any suitable open vacancies at the BBC or outside in the wider creative industry. You’ll be supported with career development, employability training, and networking opportunities to help you take your next step.
For apprenticeship opportunities, disabled applicants who choose to apply under the Disability Confident Scheme and who meet the minimum criteria for the role will normally be progressed to the next stage of the recruitment process. For most of our campaigns, this would be an online assessment designed to assess your skills, motivations and suitability for the role. a0 Further details can be found in the [FAQs section of our careers site.](https://www.bbc.co.uk/careers/work/early-careers/faqs/#applicationguidance)
## Disclaimer
This job description is a written statement of the essential characteristics of the job, with its principal accountabilities, incorporating a note of the skills, knowledge and experience required for a satisfactory level of performance. This is not intended to be a complete, detailed account of all aspects of the duties involved.
Our apprenticeship roles are also subject to you having the require qualifications that we have deemed to be necessary for your role and the requirement of the training provider for your scheme. a0 The offer would be subject to you undergoing and meeting the requirements of a skill scan process with the BBC nominated training provider to determine your eligibility.
Please note: If you were to be offered this role, the BBC will conduct Employment screening checks which include Reference checks; Eligibility to work checks; and if applicable to the role, Safeguarding and Adverse media/Social media checks. Any offer made is conditional on these checks being satisfactory.
Before your start date, you may need to disclose any unspent convictions or police charges, in line with our Recruitment policy. This allows us to discuss any support you may need and assess any risks. Failure to disclose may result in the withdrawal of your offer.
We are unable to accept applications via CV and only applications made online will be considered. Please click on the APPLY NOW button to proceed with your application.

You'll gain hands-on experience covering stories that matter to audiences, learning from experienced journalists and developing the skills needed to create trusted journalism.   Alongside this, you’ll work towards a SCQF7 apprenticeship qualification. **Want to find out more?** Watch recordings from our webinar series on our [Life at the BBC YouTube playlist](https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PLQirbxfWHEPimmLiTI-yrGoMNMV1FRfWK&si=zN5oW9PAy2C6nmDQ) to learn more about this scheme and other opportunities we offer, and hear from current apprentices about their experiences. ## **YOUR KEY RESPONSIBILITIES AND IMPACT**  As a Junior Journalist apprentice, this is a brilliant opportunity to learn, grow and contribute. On this team you can expect to:  - Work alongside experienced journalists developing your skills while creating high-quality content. - Get hands on experience including researching stories, booking guests and writing briefs.   - Discover and develop compelling stories, assisting with interviews that bring important issues to life for diverse audiences. - Learn from industry experts at the world's largest public service broadcaster. You’ll study for your industry-recognised apprenticeship qualification, learning both on and off the job.  This involves weekly in-person classes at Glasgow Clyde College. For apprentices who aren’t based in Glasgow these sessions will be virtual.  You’ll cover a range of modules including:  - Media Law - Essential Journalism - Broadcast Journalism - Journalism for a Digital Audience - Video Journalism Modules will be assessed through exams, coursework and a portfolio of work.   For more information on what you will study during the scheme, please see the [SCQF 7 Standard.](https://scqf.org.uk/the-framework/) ## **YOUR SKILLS AND ELIGIBILITY** We’re interested in your passion for working at the BBC and your enthusiasm for delivering world-class content and operational excellence to our audiences. This scheme is aimed at **non-graduates**. If you have a degree and you’re interested in similar roles at the BBC, we recommend applying for jobs at the [BBC careers site](https://careers.bbc.co.uk/) or having a look at our other apprenticeship schemes.  ## **ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA** To be eligible for an apprenticeship at the BBC, you must:  - Be 18 years old or over by the time the apprenticeship begins in September 2027. - Have lived in the UK continuously for the last three years prior to the start of the apprenticeship. - Be legally eligible to work full-time in the UK for the entire duration of the apprenticeship.  - Not currently be enrolled in another apprenticeship programme, whether with the BBC or another organisation. - Not already hold a qualification in the same subject area at the same or a higher level than this apprenticeship.   To apply for this scheme, you must also: - Not have completed or be studying for the NCTJ diploma or a journalism qualification at the same level or higher. - Have achieved English GCSE at Grade 4/C or above, or National 5 (Scotland) at C or Functional Skills Level 2 or equivalent qualification. We make and distribute the world’s most sought-after TV, audio and digital content. Our ambition is to be the home of the most powerful, entertaining, and inspiring stories for people all around the world.  ## **COULD A BBC APPRENTICESHIP BE THE NEXT ROLE FOR YOU?** Join us as an apprentice at the BBC to give yourself the opportunity to kick-start your career in a job you'll love. We're looking for individuals with a passion to find out how we make content and bring ideas to life. Depending on your placement area, you could be working behind the scenes on exciting productions, from gripping dramas to the thrill of live radio, and gain a recognised qualification while learning on the job. This is your opportunity to broaden your production knowledge while working on content that matters to millions.  **Want to find out more?** Watch recordings from our webinar series on our [Life at the BBC YouTube playlist](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLQirbxfWHEPimmLiTI-yrGoMNMV1FRfWK) to learn more about this scheme and other opportunities we offer, and hear from current apprentices about their experiences. You can find details on other placements in this location on the [BBC Early Careers website.](https://www.bbc.co.uk/careers/work/early-careers/production/#productionassistantlevel3) ## **WHY JOIN THE TEAM?** Based in Elstree, you will be working on the long-running multi-award winning drama series, EastEnders.  Working in the Scenic Design department, you’ll gain an understanding in all aspects of how the production works with a focus on design and construction. As a Production Assistant Apprentice at the BBC, you'll gain hands-on experience across a range of projects, from supporting high-profile productions to contributing to content enjoyed by audiences across the UK. You'll work alongside experienced professionals, develop practical skills and play an active role in bringing creative ideas to life. This apprenticeship could lead to job opportunities as a: - Junior Researcher - Runner - Content or Edit Assistant ## **YOUR KEY RESPONSIBILITIES AND IMPACT** As a Production Assistant Apprentice within **BBC Studios - Scripted Drama - Scenic Design**, this is a brilliant opportunity to learn, grow, and contribute. Learning blocks will be a mixture of in-person and virtual delivery including tutorial sessions, presentations and group work. As part of the programme, you will be required to travel to attend in-person learning blocks and other apprenticeship-related activities where necessary. For more information on this apprenticeship standard you will be studying, please see detail on the [Production Assistant apprenticeship standard](https://skillsengland.education.gov.uk/apprenticeships/st0341-v2-0). ## **YOUR SKILLS AND ELIGIBILITY** We’re interested in your passion for working at the BBC and your enthusiasm for delivering world-class content and operational excellence to our audiences. This scheme is aimed at **non-graduates.** If you have a degree and you’re interested in similar roles at the BBC, we recommend applying for jobs at the [BBC careers site](https://www.bbc.co.uk/careers/) or having a look at our other apprenticeship schemes.  ## **ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA** To be eligible for an apprenticeship at the BBC, you must:  - Be 18 years old or over by the time the apprenticeship begins in September 2027 - Have lived in the UK continuously for the last three years prior to the start of the apprenticeship - Be legally eligible to work full-time in the UK for the entire duration of the apprenticeship - Not currently be enrolled in another apprenticeship programme, whether with the BBC or another organisation For candidates under the age of 19 years on 7 September 2027: To complete the apprenticeship, you must have achieved Maths and English GCSE at Grade 4/C or above or National 5 (Scotland) at C or Functional Skills Level 2 or equivalent qualification. See yourself thriving in this role? Just click ‘Apply Now’!  You’ll create a candidate profile and answer a few questions - **no CV or cover letter needed.**  If you're eligible, we’ll guide you through the next steps of the process and what to expect.  You’ll need to live within a commutable distance of where this role is based. Interested in a different location? Check out our other adverts - but please only apply to one.  This is a fixed-term apprenticeship - your contract lasts for the duration of the scheme. Once you have completed your apprenticeship, you will be able to apply for any suitable open vacancies at the BBC or outside in the wider creative industry. You’ll be supported with career development, employability training, and networking opportunities to help you take your next step. For apprenticeship opportunities, disabled applicants who choose to apply under the Disability Confident Scheme and who meet the minimum criteria for the role will normally be progressed to the next stage of the recruitment process. For most of our campaigns, this would be an online assessment designed to assess your skills, motivations and suitability for the role.  Further details can be found in the [FAQs section of our careers site.](https://www.bbc.co.uk/careers/work/early-careers/faqs/#applicationguidance) #LI-DNI PRA27 ## Disclaimer This job description is a written statement of the essential characteristics of the job, with its principal accountabilities, incorporating a note of the skills, knowledge and experience required for a satisfactory level of performance. This is not intended to be a complete, detailed account of all aspects of the duties involved. Our apprenticeship roles are also subject to you having the require qualifications that we have deemed to be necessary for your role and the requirement of the training provider for your scheme.  The offer would be subject to you undergoing and meeting the requirements of a skill scan process with the BBC nominated training provider to determine your eligibility. Please note: If you were to be offered this role, the BBC will conduct Employment screening checks which include Reference checks; Eligibility to work checks; and if applicable to the role, Safeguarding and Adverse media/Social media checks. Any offer made is conditional on these checks being satisfactory. Before your start date, you may need to disclose any unspent convictions or police charges, in line with our Recruitment policy. As an Apprentice you will also receive: •  An industry recognised qualification. •  Industry-leading training through the BBC Academy and our learning providers (this may involve travel to locations across the UK). •  A dedicated Team Manager and Scheme Specialist to help with your development. •  Training and Mentoring by industry professionals.  •  A bespoke BBC apprenticeship experience including apprenticeship development days and membership of the BBC Apprenticeship community. •  Employability and networking training and support to help you secure your next role. •  The opportunity to apply for financial support for relocation subject to eligibility. Journalist Apprenticeship - Level 6 - BBC South News - Reading Job Description Job Requisition ID:  55561 Job Closing Date:  24 November 2026 Reading, GBR, RG6 1PT **Contract Type:** Fixed-Term Apprenticeship, Full-time for 24 months **Department:** BBC South News **Location:** Reading - BBC Berkshire **Salary:** £26,000  ## **COULD A BBC APPRENTICESHIP BE THE NEXT ROLE FOR YOU?** Join us as an apprentice at the BBC to give yourself the opportunity to kick-start your career in a job you'll love. We’re committed to your skills and talent development. You’ll learn on-the-job, developing your knowledge and skills in an area that interests you, whilst working towards your apprenticeship qualification with one of our learning providers.  ## **WHY JOIN THIS SCHEME?** The BBC Level 6 Journalist Apprenticeship (JOA27) offers emerging journalists the opportunity to advance their skills through industry-leading training and hands-on experience.  Working with industry experts, you’ll contribute to trusted and impactful journalism, telling stories that inform, educate and engage audiences. Alongside this, you’ll work towards a Level 6 apprenticeship and the industry-recognised NCTJ National Qualification in Journalism (NQJ). **Want to find out more?** Watch recordings from our webinar series on our [Life at the BBC YouTube playlist](https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PLQirbxfWHEPimmLiTI-yrGoMNMV1FRfWK&si=zN5oW9PAy2C6nmDQ) to learn more about this scheme and other opportunities we offer, and hear from current apprentices about their experiences. ## **YOUR KEY RESPONSIBILITIES AND IMPACT** As a Journalist apprentice, this is a brilliant opportunity to learn, grow and contribute. On this apprenticeship you can expect to:  - Play a key role in creating trusted, high-quality news content for BBC audiences. - Grow your storytelling expertise through hands-on experience researching, writing and producing stories on subjects ranging from current affairs and business to sport, culture and politics. - Learn from experienced journalists, contribute to stories which matter to the public, collaborate with expert teams and develop your career at the world's leading public service media organisation. You’ll study for your industry recognised apprenticeship qualification, learning both on and off the job.   This involves weekly virtual webinars and in- person bootcamps at PA Media Academy in London.  You’ll cover modules such as: Media Law, Advanced Newsgathering, Advanced Storytelling and Advanced Audience, and work towards the National Qualification in Journalism (NQJ).   The NQJ is assessed through two exams and a logbook of work.    For more information on what you will study during the scheme, please see the [Journalism Apprenticeship Standard](https://skillsengland.education.gov.uk/apprenticeships/st1490-v2-0) and the  [NCTJ](https://www.nctj.com/qualifications-courses/qualifications/national-qualification-in-journalism/)  ## **YOUR SKILLS AND ELIGIBILITY** We’re interested in your passion for working at the BBC and your enthusiasm for delivering world-class content and operational excellence to our audiences. We’re not focused on your qualifications; instead, we look for potential and offer you the opportunity to apply your transferable strengths and experience to work in different ways. If you can bring some of these skills and experiences, along with transferable strengths, we’d love to hear from you and encourage you to apply: - Demonstrate strong journalistic skills and a passion for storytelling. - Actively follow sports news across a range of platforms. - Show a fascination with people, communities and the issues shaping the world around us. - Bring fresh, creative ideas for engaging and reaching new audiences. - Demonstrate motivation, adaptability and resilience in a fast-paced environment. This scheme is aimed at people who are already demonstrating their journalistic potential. You may have gained experience through a community or student newspaper, radio station, blog, vlog, podcast or social media content creation.  We welcome applicants from a range of backgrounds and experiences, including those who have completed the NCTJ Diploma, a Level 5 Journalist Apprenticeship, or another journalism qualification.  ## **ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA** To be eligible for an apprenticeship at the BBC, you must:  - Be 18 years old or over by the time the apprenticeship begins in September 2027. - Have lived in the UK continuously for the last three years prior to the start of the apprenticeship. - Be legally eligible to work full-time in the UK for the entire duration of the apprenticeship.  - Not currently be enrolled in another apprenticeship programme, whether with the BBC or another organisation. - Not already hold a qualification in the same subject area at the same or a higher level than this apprenticeship.   To apply for this scheme, you must also: - Not have previously completed any elements of the National Qualification in Journalism (NQJ). - Have achieved English GCSE at Grade 4/C or above; or National 5 (Scotland) at C or Functional Skills Level 2; or equivalent qualification.   Candidates under the age of 19 at the start of the apprenticeship must have achieved Maths and English GCSE at Grade 4/C or above or National 5 (Scotland) at C or Functional Skills Level 2 or equivalent qualification.  If you have not achieved these qualifications by the start of your apprenticeship, you will be required to achieve Functional Skills Level 2 before the end of your apprenticeship.  ## **READY TO APPLY?** Don’t leave yourself wondering “what if?” this could be your chance to be part of something exciting. See yourself thriving in this role? Just click ‘Apply Now’!  You’ll create a candidate profile and answer a few questions - **no CV or cover letter needed.**  If you're eligible, we’ll guide you through the next steps of the process and what to expect.  You’ll need to live within a commutable distance of where this role is based. Interested in a different location? Check out our other adverts - but please only apply to one. The BBC recognises that you may need to relocate to a new location to take up a BBC Apprenticeship scheme. The cost of relocating can be a barrier for some applicants and where that is a barrier to participation, we want to help where we can. To help ensure our apprenticeship opportunities are accessible to people from a wide range of backgrounds, a limited number of relocation support awards are available each year for those who meet our financial eligibility criteria.  Relocation financial support is available for this role, subject to meeting the financial eligibility criteria. Further information will be shared with applicants during the recruitment process. Details on the wider support, initiatives and networks available at the BBC can be found on [our careers site.](https://www.bbc.co.uk/careers/bbc-life/inclusion/sed/) This is a fixed-term apprenticeship - your contract lasts for the duration of the scheme. Once you have completed your apprenticeship, you will be able to apply for any suitable open vacancies at the BBC or outside in the wider creative industry. You’ll be supported with career development, employability training, and networking opportunities to help you take your next step. For apprenticeship opportunities, disabled applicants who choose to apply under the Disability Confident Scheme and who meet the minimum criteria for the role will normally be progressed to the next stage of the recruitment process. For most of our campaigns, this would be an online assessment designed to assess your skills, motivations and suitability for the role.  Further details can be found in the [FAQs section of our careers site.](https://www.bbc.co.uk/careers/work/early-careers/faqs/#applicationguidance) ## Disclaimer This job description is a written statement of the essential characteristics of the job, with its principal accountabilities, incorporating a note of the skills, knowledge and experience required for a satisfactory level of performance. This is not intended to be a complete, detailed account of all aspects of the duties involved. Our apprenticeship roles are also subject to you having the require qualifications that we have deemed to be necessary for your role and the requirement of the training provider for your scheme.  The offer would be subject to you undergoing and meeting the requirements of a skill scan process with the BBC nominated training provider to determine your eligibility. Please note: If you were to be offered this role, the BBC will conduct Employment screening checks which include Reference checks; Eligibility to work checks; and if applicable to the role, Safeguarding and Adverse media/Social media checks. Any offer made is conditional on these checks being satisfactory. Before your start date, you may need to disclose any unspent convictions or police charges, in line with our Recruitment policy. This allows us to discuss any support you may need and assess any risks. Failure to disclose may result in the withdrawal of your offer. Job Title:  SAP (S/4) - Principal Systems Engineer - Finance JOB REF: 56164 JOB BAND: D CONTRACT TYPE: Permanent, Full-time DEPARTMENT: BBC Technology Group LOCATION: London Televison Centre;  2 days per week in office PROPOSED SALARY RANGE: £70,000 - £80,000 depending on relevant skills, knowledge and experience. The expected salary range for this role reflects internal benchmarking and external market insights. CLOSING DATE: 23:59 on Monday the 16th November 2026 INTERVIEWS TO COMMENCE: Monday the 30th November\* this may be subject to change
We're happy to discuss flexible working. If you'd like to, please indicate your preference in the application – though there's no obligation to do so now. Flexible working will be part of the discussion at offer stage.  Interview Process:
1 x 45 minute Values and Behaviours competency-based interview with technical questions.
## PURPOSE OF THE ROLE
BBC Studios Bold. British. Creative: that’s BBC Studios. Combining the strengths of the UK’s most-awarded production company with a world-class distributor, we fund, create, distribute and commercialize world-class content for the BBC and other UK and international companies. Our aim is to inspire audiences around the globe with quality content that informs, educates and entertains and to strengthen the BBC, our partners and wider industry both creatively and financially. We seek to be the best British content company in the world; a first-choice partner and employer, where everyone can flourish and do their best work. BBC’s Media Tech team helps shape the future of our corporate systems. In this role, you’ll influence strategy and drive innovation across finance platforms, focusing on SAP (S4 HANA) and partner solutions. You’ll contribute to delivering and managing complex technical changes and optimising systems to maximise value and align with BBC business goals. If you’re passionate about using technology to create meaningful impact, this is your opportunity to support the evolution of the BBC’s financial systems.
WHY JOIN THE TEAM
You will be joining a small, established team that work well together in a rapidly developing and transformative space. You will have the opportunity to pick up new skills and Best Practice ways of working which help drive efficiency and Value for Money. The team are currently engaged in an exciting transformation in the Finance and Procurement space, which you will be a contributor to.
## YOUR KEY RESPONSIBILITIES AND IMPACT:
\- Contribute to a technical roadmap for systems and services within their scope \- Responsible and accountable for Small/Medium technical changes, clarifying requirements submitted by BBC Business Users and managing a change process followed by an outsourced technology provider, including Documentation creation / Review, Technical Build, Testing Cycles, Production Deployment and Post Go-Live support \- Acting as a trusted team member for larger projects with technical change elements, working closely with Project Management and Project Stakeholders to deliver timely, high-quality outcomes \- Building relationships with Internal and External stakeholders, offering support and influence focused on best practice, achievable goals \- Working with Outsourced Technology partners and Internal Stakeholders to support the resolution of Incidents at varied severity levels \-Coach colleagues and share good practice across modules
## YOUR SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE
ESSENTIAL CRITERIA:
    • Significant SAP functional experience, with depth expertise in SAP FI, Assets, Banking and CO-PA plus one other SD, MM or PS modules. Hands-on S/4HANA experience, including at least one full implementation or migration lifecycle and ongoing support     • Extensive experience and system specialist for Finance modules of SAP -S/4 and other Finance related systems, including understanding how best-practice configurations align with business processes and providing guidance to a wide range of technical and functional stakeholders, including expertise in translating project, user and product requirements into technical solutions     • Experience with the following software: SAP Finance and Controlling, SAP S/4, detailed SAP integration knowledge with SD, MM, FI-CO, PS, Intercompany, Tax, Financial Statement processes, E-invoicing and integration (SAP-BTP).     • Experience reviewing Technical and Functional Documentation, identifying and revising based on SAP best practice, quality, clarity and completeness. Experience integrating SAP with third-party applications      • Ability to engage and influence stakeholders at various levels, translating and imparting technical concepts into audience relevant information, including leading on requirements gathering with the business process owners and presenting solution options that align with BBC Engineering Strategies. Dealing with multiple priorities, managing conflict and using influencing skills to ensure that projects/assignments are properly commissioned and delivered into the business
DESIRED:
\- Experience with the following software: SAP S/4 Hana (FI/CO, SD, MM, PS), Treasury,  SAP Fiori, Concur, SAP Signavio, SAP Joule, SAP Walkme, Workiva, One Source, Kyriba, Taxually, Blackline, BTP (CPI, APIM, E-invoicing) \- Understanding of media specific processes relating to an organisation’s financial operation e.g. Production Accounting, Content Distribution, Media supply chain, Broadcasting or rights driven business. Familiarity with rights, royalties or content-cost processes \- Understanding the necessity of security, access control and segregation of duties in system design \- Ability to write and communicate complex technology solutions in a clear and coherent way
If you can bring some of these skills and experience, along with transferable strengths, we’d love to hear from you and encourage you to apply.

- Floor Management  
- TV Vision Mixing  
- Sound Operations  
- Technical Directing  
- Shoot and Edit Multi-Skilled Operator  
- Picture and Audio Editing

Join us as an apprentice at the BBC to give yourself the opportunity to kick-start your career in a job you'll love. We’re committed to your skills and talent development. ## **WHY JOIN THIS SCHEME?**
The Junior Journalist Apprenticeship (JRA27) is perfect for curious and creative individuals with a passion for storytelling. Whether you're finishing school, college, or exploring an alternative to university, this programme offers an exciting opportunity to kick-start your journalism career with the world's leading public service media organisation.
You'll gain hands-on experience covering stories that matter to audiences, learning from experienced journalists and developing the skills needed to create trusted journalism.  
Alongside this, you’ll work towards both the NCTJ Diploma in Journalism and a SCQF 7 apprenticeship qualification.
**Want to find out more?** Watch recordings from our webinar series on our [Life at the BBC YouTube playlist](https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PLQirbxfWHEPimmLiTI-yrGoMNMV1FRfWK&si=EY7BNqy8b4Y_X-hE) to learn more about this scheme and other opportunities we offer, and hear from current apprentices about their experiences.
## **WHY JOIN THE TEAM?**
BBC Sport is the largest sports website and app in the UK. It is the most popular service of its kind for audiences across the country, covering live sport and sports news, while also providing great entertainment for sports fans through content such as videos, quizzes and engaging interviews. The team also delivers sports news coverage on iPlayer and across national and global radio.
## **YOUR KEY RESPONSIBILITIES AND IMPACT**
 As a Junior Journalist apprentice, this is a brilliant opportunity to learn, grow and contribute. On this team you can expect to: 
- Work alongside experienced journalists developing your skills while creating high-quality content.
- Get hands on experience including researching stories, booking guests and writing briefs.  
- Discover and develop compelling stories, assisting with interviews that bring important issues to life for diverse audiences.
- Learn from industry experts at the world's largest public service broadcaster.
You’ll study for your industry-recognised apprenticeship qualification, learning both on and off the job. 
This involves weekly in-person classes at Glasgow Clyde College. For apprentices who aren’t based in Glasgow these sessions will be virtual. 
You’ll cover a range of modules for the NCTJ Diploma including: 
- Media Law
- Essential Journalism
- Broadcast Journalism
- Journalism for a Digital Audience
- Video Journalism
Modules will be assessed through exams, coursework and a portfolio of work.  
For more information on what you will study during the scheme, please see the [Journalism Apprenticeship Standard.](https://skillsengland.education.gov.uk/apprenticeships/st1516-v1-0)

We’re interested in your passion for working at the BBC and your enthusiasm for delivering world-class content and operational excellence to our audiences. We’re not focused on your qualifications; instead, we look for potential and offer you the opportunity to apply your transferable strengths and experience to work in different ways. 
If you can bring some of these skills and experiences, along with transferable strengths, we’d love to hear from you and encourage you to apply:
- You're naturally curious about people and what’s happening in the world around you, with a keen interest in news.
- You’re full of creative ideas and enjoy finding innovative ways to tell engaging stories.
- You love finding things out, asking questions and getting to the heart of a story.
- You have a real enthusiasm for writing and enjoy communicating complex ideas in a clear, compelling way.
- You thrive in a fast-paced environment, bringing flexibility, motivation and a willingness to adapt as priorities change.
This scheme is aimed at **non-graduates.** If you have a degree and you’re interested in similar roles at the BBC, we recommend applying for jobs at the [BBC careers site](https://careers.bbc.co.uk/) or having a look at our other apprenticeship schemes. 
## **ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA**
To be eligible for an apprenticeship at the BBC, you must: 
- Be 18 years old or over by the time the apprenticeship begins in September 2027.
- Have lived in the UK continuously for the last three years prior to the start of the apprenticeship.
- Be legally eligible to work full-time in the UK for the entire duration of the apprenticeship. 
- Not currently be enrolled in another apprenticeship programme, whether with the BBC or another organisation.
- Not already hold a qualification in the same subject area at the same or a higher level than this apprenticeship. 
 To apply for this scheme, you must also:
•    Not have completed or be studying for the NCTJ diploma or a journalism qualification at the same level or higher.  •    Have achieved English GCSE at Grade 4/C or above, or National 5 (Scotland) at C or Functional Skills Level 2 or equivalent qualification.
For candidates under the age of 19 years at the start of the apprenticeship: To complete the apprenticeship, you must have achieved Maths and English GCSE at Grade 4/C or above or National 5 (Scotland) at C or Functional Skills Level 2 or equivalent qualification to pass the apprenticeship.

You’ll create a candidate profile and answer a few questions - **no CV or cover letter needed.** 
If you're eligible, we’ll guide you through the next steps of the process and what to expect. 
You’ll need to live within a commutable distance of where this role is based. Interested in a different location? Check out our other adverts - but please only apply to one. 
The BBC recognises that you may need to relocate to a new location to take up a BBC Apprenticeship scheme. The cost of relocating can be a barrier for some applicants and where that is a barrier to participation, we want to help where we can. To help ensure our apprenticeship opportunities are accessible to people from a wide range of backgrounds, a limited number of relocation support awards are available each year for those who meet our financial eligibility criteria.  Relocation financial support is available for this role, subject to meeting the financial eligibility criteria. Further information will be shared with applicants during the recruitment process. Job Description
Job Requisition ID:  55676
Job Closing Date:  24 November 2026
Salford, GBR, M50 2QH | Salford, MAN, GBR, M50 2QH **Contract Type:** Fixed-Term Apprenticeship, Full-time for 40 months
**Department:** Media Technology
**Location:** Salford - Dock House, Salford - Quay House
**Salary:** £24,650 
## **COULD A BBC APPRENTICESHIP BE THE NEXT ROLE FOR YOU?**
Join us as an apprentice at the BBC to give yourself the opportunity to kick-start your career in a job you'll love. We’re committed to your skills and talent development. You’ll learn on-the-job, developing your knowledge and skills in an area that interests you, whilst working towards your apprenticeship qualification with one of our learning providers. 
## **WHY JOIN THIS SCHEME?**
As an apprentice within our team, you will be right at the heart of the BBC's digital first world, developing and maintaining the systems that audiences rely on every single day.  
Imagine this: The code you write helps deliver the suspense of EastEnders on iPlayer, the freshest tracks on Sounds, the minute-by-minute drama of a breaking news story, or the thrill of a live goal on Sport.   
Your Code, Millions of Users  
- Your work directly delights millions of people every week. When they tune in to a podcast, catch up on the news, or stream a live event, it's the platform you helped build that makes it happen.  
- You will learn to handle the massive digital challenge of running services that have to be fast, reliable, and available 24/7.  
- You will be working with world class software engineers to evolve the platform, ensuring the BBC remains at the forefront of digital media.  
You’ve got to be interested now, right? 
**Want to find out more?** Watch recordings from our webinar series on our [Life at the BBC YouTube playlist](https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PLQirbxfWHEPimmLiTI-yrGoMNMV1FRfWK&si=eCgNZuWfnZICtWz1) to learn more about this scheme and other opportunities we offer, and hear from current apprentices about their experiences.
## **WHY JOIN THE TEAM?**
**Partnerships Team:** 
We are the team behind iPlayer off product discovery. We work with a range of partners from Samsung, LG, Google, Amazon to surface the amazing BBC content that we have on their platforms. We power important services such as continue watching, promotional content, experimentation and we're responsible for providing iPlayer metadata to our partner platforms.
We maintain and create core services such as VOD catalogue (the content available for on demand playback), schedules (EPG data for upcoming programming), promotions (automated and manually curated sets of themed content), continue watching (continue watching your last programme from off product).
We create services which are used by millions on a wide variety of devices, so no day is never the same! We're the gateway to BBC iPlayer and drive over 20% of traffic directly to the BBC. We are a huge growth area for the BBC, so come join us on an exciting journey!
**Iplayer & S TV Engineering Team:**
BBC Search plays a vital role in helping millions of people discover the content they love across BBC iPlayer, Sounds, News, Sport and the wider BBC. Our search platform handles millions of requests every day, and we're passionate about making search smarter, faster and more relevant for our audiences.
Our engineering team is organised into three squads: Search Catalogue, Search Intent & Retrieval, and Search Ranking, working together to deliver an intelligent, scalable and innovative search experience.
As an apprentice, you'll have the opportunity to work with modern technologies, including Apache Solr, OpenSearch, AWS, Python and Java, while gaining hands-on experience in building and improving large-scale search systems.
You'll also get exposure to some of the most exciting developments in search technology, including Artificial Intelligence (AI), Large Language Models (LLMs), Natural Language Processing (NLP), semantic search and machine learning. We're exploring innovative ways to understand what audiences are searching for, recognise their intent, handle misspelt queries and deliver more meaningful results.
**Search Team:** 
We are TV Client and we build iPlayer on TV, serving over 20 million people every month. We have 6 teams in our space that look after a wide variety of different problem spaces.
They split them into two types, platform teams who build the interface with TV devices directly and experience teams who use that platform to rapidly experiment on and deliver audience features every day.
We use a wide range of technologies but with any new joiner we start small and build up, coaching and supporting every step of the way. If you are interested to learn how TVs work and how we manage to deliver experiences on them come and join us.
## **YOUR KEY RESPONSIBILITIES AND IMPACT**
As a Software Engineer apprentice (SED27), this is a brilliant opportunity to learn, grow, and contribute – you will:   
- Gain hands-on experience in the beating heart of the BBC’s software engineering teams responsible for TV, audio, online, and digital platforms.  
- Develop your understanding of how the BBC’s existing apps and websites are fit for purpose, ranging from analysis, design, code, build, test, implementation, and support.  
- Develop your knowledge and skills on how to apply software engineering principles to all stages of the solution development life cycle, from gathering code and data requirements and ensuring they are secure.  
- You will gain a new understanding on how to ensure the quality and reliability of software through rigorous testing and quality control practices.  
- You will explore considerations and how to tackle troubleshooting concerns, guided by your team.  
- You will play a part in ground-breaking complex projects, in alignment with the BBC’s Digital First strategy, from inception to delivery.  
You’ll study for your industry recognised apprenticeship qualification, learning both on-and-off-the-job. This means on successful completion of the apprenticeship, you will be awarded with an Undergraduate Degree (Bachelor of Science with Honours) in Digital and Technology Solutions Professional (Software Engineer pathway) from a UK University, and you will be supported to find a job role within the BBC’s Technology or Product delivery teams.   
For more information on what you will study during the scheme, please see the [Software Engineering degree apprenticeship standard](https://skillsengland.education.gov.uk/apprenticeships/st0119-v1-2).
## **YOUR SKILLS AND ELIGIBILITY**
We’re interested in your passion for working at the BBC and your enthusiasm for delivering world-class content and operational excellence to our audiences. We’re not focused on your qualifications; instead, we look for potential and offer you the opportunity to apply your transferable strengths and experience to work in different ways. 
If you can bring some of these skills and experiences, along with transferable strengths, we’d love to hear from you and encourage you to apply:
- Have a love of maths and a passion for coding.  
- You're excited about embracing the latest AI and Machine Learning technologies to transform working practices.   
- Have brilliant organisational skills and are great at problem -solving and negotiating.  
- You can manage multiple deadlines and demands on your time, and have a calm and focused approach to changing circumstances.  
- Have a keen interest in the BBC and how people consume content, bursting with fresh ideas to introduce new perspectives.  
This scheme is aimed at **non-graduates.** If you have a degree and you’re interested in similar roles at the BBC, we recommend applying for jobs at the [BBC careers site](https://careers.bbc.co.uk/) or having a look at our other apprenticeship schemes. 
## **ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA**
To be eligible for an apprenticeship at the BBC, you must: 
- Be 18 years old or over by the time the apprenticeship begins in September 2027.
- Have lived in the UK continuously for the last three years prior to the start of the apprenticeship.
- Be legally eligible to work full-time in the UK for the entire duration of the apprenticeship. 
- Not currently be enrolled in another apprenticeship programme, whether with the BBC or another organisation.
- Not already hold a qualification in the same subject area at the same or a higher level than this apprenticeship. 
 To apply for this scheme, you must also:
- Have maths and English GCSE at Grade 4/C or above or National 5 (Scotland) at C or equivalent qualification.  
- Have some experience of coding and/or software engineering. Whether that is from an A Level/BTEC course, coding boot camp or personal projects. A basic coding test will form part of the assessment for this scheme.
## **READY TO APPLY?**
Don’t leave yourself wondering “what if?” this could be your chance to be part of something exciting. See yourself thriving in this role? Just click ‘Apply Now’! 
You’ll create a candidate profile and answer a few questions - **no CV or cover letter needed.** 
If you're eligible, we’ll guide you through the next steps of the process and what to expect. 
You’ll need to live within a commutable distance of where this role is based. Interested in a different location? Check out our other adverts - but please only apply to one. 
The BBC recognises that you may need to relocate to a new location to take up a BBC Apprenticeship scheme. The cost of relocating can be a barrier for some applicants and where that is a barrier to participation, we want to help where we can. To help ensure our apprenticeship opportunities are accessible to people from a wide range of backgrounds, a limited number of relocation support awards are available each year for those who meet our financial eligibility criteria.  Relocation financial support is available for this role, subject to meeting the financial eligibility criteria. Further information will be shared with applicants during the recruitment process. job_description:
Job Requisition ID:  55633
Job Closing Date:  24 November 2026
Stoke-on-Trent, GBR, ST1 1JJ **Contract Type:** Fixed-Term Apprenticeship, Full-time for 15 months
**Department:** BBC Local Radio
**Location:** Stoke-on-Trent - Radio Stoke
**Salary:** £24,650 
## **COULD A BBC APPRENTICESHIP BE THE NEXT ROLE FOR YOU?**
Join us as an apprentice at the BBC to give yourself the opportunity to kick-start your career in a job you'll love. We’re committed to your skills and talent development. You’ll learn on-the-job, developing your knowledge and skills in an area that interests you, whilst working towards your apprenticeship qualification with one of our learning providers. 
## **WHY JOIN THIS SCHEME?**
The Content Creator apprenticeship is designed to equip you with the skills to create engaging, impactful content across a range of platforms. You’ll learn how to plan and develop creative ideas, research target audiences, and produce audio, visual and written content suitable for different channels. 
This hands-on, immersive programme combines practical workshops, interactive sessions, assignments and collaborative group projects. You’ll gain experience in creating, recording and editing video and audio content, while developing your planning, presentation and pitching skills. The scheme also provides a foundation in photography and imaging, social media and search engine optimisation (SEO), and website creation, giving you a broad understanding of modern digital content production.
**Want to find out more?** Watch recordings from our webinar series on our [Life at the BBC YouTube playlist](https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PLQirbxfWHEPimmLiTI-yrGoMNMV1FRfWK&si=eCgNZuWfnZICtWz1) to learn more about this scheme and other opportunities we offer, and hear from current apprentices about their experiences.
## **WHY JOIN THE TEAM?**
[BBC Radio Stoke](https://www.bbc.co.uk/sounds/play/live/bbc_radio_stoke) operates a network of radio stations across England and the Channel Islands. From Truro to Newcastle, we are at the heart of the local community. Our services offer a trusted source of local news and information but we also celebrate everything that is great about where we live. Whilst our shows will primarily be studio-based, we are all about getting into the heart of the communities that we serve. We have a unique connection with our audience and love finding and sharing their stories. We’re also passionate about local sport, plus our ‘Make A Difference’ initiative is all about celebrating the people and organisations that make the areas we broadcast to, a great place to live.
## **YOUR KEY RESPONSIBILITIES AND IMPACT**
As a Content Creator apprentice, this is brilliant opportunity to learn, grow, and contribute – you could expect to:  
- Play a part in creating trusted, high-quality content for BBC audiences. 
- Grow your storytelling skills through hands-on experience researching, writing, producing and editing content on a range of subjects. 
- Develop your digital content skills by monitoring audience trends and creating content for social media platforms, including selecting and editing clips from programmes for use on social media platforms.  
- Spot opportunities for digital content, including short clips, behind-the-scenes moments, interviews and talent‑led extras. 
- Learn from experienced professionals, collaborate with expert teams and develop your career at the world's largest public service broadcaster. 
You’ll study for your industry recognised apprenticeship qualification, learning both on and off the job.  This means that as well as learning on your placement at the BBC, you’ll also attend learning blocks (up to a week at a time) with our learning provider, working towards an industry recognised apprenticeship qualification - Level 3 Content Creator.  
Learning blocks will be a mixture of in-person and virtual delivery, including attending instructor-led workships, tutorial sessions, presentations and group work.
For more information on what you will study during the scheme, please see the [Content Creator apprenticeship standard.](https://skillsengland.education.gov.uk/apprenticeships/st0105-v2-0) 
As part of the programme, you will be required to travel to attend in-person learning blocks and other apprenticeship-related activities where necessary. 
## **YOUR SKILLS AND ELIGIBILITY**
We’re interested in your passion for working at the BBC and your enthusiasm for delivering world-class content and operational excellence to our audiences. We’re not focused on your qualifications; instead, we look for potential and offer you the opportunity to apply your transferable strengths and experience to work in different ways. 
If you can bring some of these skills and experiences, along with transferable strengths, we’d love to hear from you and encourage you to apply:
- Bring fresh, creative ideas for engaging and reaching new audiences.   
- A genuine consumer of content who follows what is happening across platforms like TikTok, YouTube and Instagram. 
- Adaptable and versatile, able to switch between serious, issue‑based content and fun, high-energy entertainment. 
- A collaborative team player who is organised, motivated, adaptable and thrive in a fast-paced environment. 
- Passionate about your own self-development, showing the discipline and commitment required to complete the apprenticeship. 
This scheme is aimed at **non-graduates.** If you have a degree and you’re interested in similar roles at the BBC, we recommend applying for jobs at the [BBC careers site](https://careers.bbc.co.uk/) or having a look at our other apprenticeship schemes. 
## **ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA**
To be eligible for an apprenticeship at the BBC, you must: 
- Be 18 years old or over by the time the apprenticeship begins in September 2027.
- Have lived in the UK continuously for the last three years prior to the start of the apprenticeship.
- Be legally eligible to work full-time in the UK for the entire duration of the apprenticeship. 
- Not currently be enrolled in another apprenticeship programme, whether with the BBC or another organisation.
- No prior learning is required to apply.
- If you already have relevant experience or qualifications, your individual learning plan may be adjusted to reflect this – meaning you could complete your apprenticeship in less time.
For candidates under the age of 19 years at 8th September 2027: To complete the apprenticeship, you must have achieved Maths and English GCSE at Grade 4/C or above or National 5 (Scotland) at C or Functional Skills Level 2 or equivalent qualification. If you have not achieved these qualifications by the start of your apprenticeship, you will be required to achieve Functional Skills Level 2 before the end of your apprenticeship when you take your end-point assessment.   
## **READY TO APPLY?**
Don’t leave yourself wondering “what if?” this could be your chance to be part of something exciting. See yourself thriving in this role? Just click ‘Apply Now’! 
You’ll create a candidate profile and answer a few questions - **no CV or cover letter needed.** 
If you're eligible, we’ll guide you through the next steps of the process and what to expect. 
You’ll need to live within a commutable distance of where this role is based. Interested in a different location? Check out our other adverts - but please only apply to one. 
The BBC recognises that you may need to relocate to a new location to take up a BBC Apprenticeship scheme. The cost of relocating can be a barrier for some applicants and where that is a barrier to participation, we want to help where we can. To help ensure our apprenticeship opportunities are accessible to people from a wide range of backgrounds, a limited number of relocation support awards are available each year for those who meet our financial eligibility criteria.  Relocation financial support is available for this role, subject to meeting the financial eligibility criteria. Further information will be shared with applicants during the recruitment process. Details on the wider support, initiatives and networks available at the BBC can be found on [our careers site.](https://www.bbc.co.uk/careers/bbc-life/inclusion/sed/)
This is a fixed-term apprenticeship - your contract lasts for the duration of the scheme. Once you have completed your apprenticeship, you will be able to apply for any suitable open vacancies at the BBC or outside in the wider creative industry. You’ll be supported with career development, employability training, and networking opportunities to help you take your next step.
For apprenticeship opportunities, disabled applicants who choose to apply under the Disability Confident Scheme and who meet the minimum criteria for the role will normally be progressed to the next stage of the recruitment process. For most of our campaigns, this would be an online assessment designed to assess your skills, motivations and suitability for the role.  Further details can be found in the [FAQs section of our careers site.](https://www.bbc.co.uk/careers/work/early-careers/faqs/#applicationguidance)
(CCA27)

This job description is a written statement of the essential characteristics of the job, with its principal accountabilities, incorporating a note of the skills, knowledge and experience required for a satisfactory level of performance. This is not intended to be a complete, detailed account of all aspects of the duties involved.
Our apprenticeship roles are also subject to you having the require qualifications that we have deemed to be necessary for your role and the requirement of the training provider for your scheme.  The offer would be subject to you undergoing and meeting the requirements of a skill scan process with the BBC nominated training provider to determine your eligibility.
Please note: If you were to be offered this role, the BBC will conduct Employment screening checks which include Reference checks; Eligibility to work checks; and if applicable to the role, Safeguarding and Adverse media/Social media checks. Any offer made is conditional on these checks being satisfactory.
Before your start date, you may need to disclose any unspent convictions or police charges, in line with our Recruitment policy. This allows us to discuss any support you may need and assess any risks. Failure to disclose may result in the withdrawal of your offer.
We are unable to accept applications via CV and only applications made online will be considered. Please click on the APPLY NOW button to proceed with your application.
