Position Summary
You will play a key role in shaping and improving planning processes across GSK’s supply chain. This role offers a unique chance to work with diverse teams across planning, manufacturing, procurement, and external supply. We are looking for someone who is collaborative, solutions-focused, and ready to drive change in a dynamic environment. Joining GSK means you will grow your skills while making a real impact on how medicines reach people worldwide. Your work will help us continue uniting science, technology, and talent to get ahead of disease together.
Job Purpose
Reporting to the ERP Process Director – Planning, the Planning Process Manager supports the delivery, deployment and operationalisation of the global S/4 Planning template across GSK’s Rx and Vx supply chains. The role owns defined planning process areas and ensures they are designed to drive business benefit and harmonize the ways of working across the global planning teams and the interface with stakeholders in sites and other functions.
The process owner will be responsible for ensuring that the planning process vision is supported by process definition, documentations (GSOPs, BPSDs, System Instruction, etc.), process testing and creation / update of associated materials (Training materials). This is including integration with OMP, APO and other planning tools. The role will support the ERP Process Director to ensure the process framework is sustainable through monitoring of adoption and adherence. Key Responsibilities:

• Own defined Planning process areas and ensure their end-to-end design integrates effectively with OMP, APO and other planning tools, while maintaining fidelity to global standards and approved template decisions.

• Develop and maintain process-change plans and facilitate process deep dives with business, programme and functional stakeholders to resolve design decisions, dependencies and adoption impacts.
• Define business rules, process controls, KPIs, system roles and operating-model requirements; manage template change requests, including impact assessment and value propositions for governance approval.
• Support Planning data migration, cleansing, validation and alignment across S/4HANA, OMP and connected planning systems.

job_description:
Regional Head of Occupational Health / Regional Medical Director – Europe (including UK)
At GSK, protecting the health of our workforce is fundamental to delivering our mission to positively impact the health of 2.5 billion people by the end of 2030. The Occupational Health Centre of Excellence supports this ambition through specialist medical leadership, clinical governance and assurance, helping to enable safe and sustainable work and contributing expert medical insight to the management of workplace health risks.
Reporting to the VP, Global Head of Occupational Health within GSK's EHS structure, this role provides Occupational Medicine leadership across Europe, contributing specialist medical expertise to the management of workplace health risks, while ensuring robust clinical governance and safe, effective and compliant Occupational Health services.
Success in the role requires strong influencing skills, the ability to align stakeholders across countries and functions, and the judgement to balance global standards with local regulatory and business requirements.
In the UK, this role holds accountability for the governance, quality, performance and continuous improvement of Occupational Health services delivered to UK businesses, including leadership of service strategy, provider performance, clinical governance, operating model development, financial sustainability and alignment with business priorities.
As a member of the Occupational Health Leadership Team (OHLT), this role helps shape and deliver the strategic direction of Occupational Health across GSK, providing leadership to support the management of health risks in the workplace, while ensuring robust clinical governance and high-quality Occupational Health services to support GSK’s mission and strategy.
Key responsibilities include, but are not limited to:
• Act as the regional medical leader for Occupational Health across Europe, championing GSK’s Occupational Health ambition and leading through a matrix of site teams and functional stakeholders.
• Provide expert Occupational Medicine leadership and consultation on workplace health risks, working in partnership with Industrial Hygiene, Toxicology, Ergonomics and other EHS subject matter experts to advise on the potential health effects of workplace exposures, appropriate health surveillance programmes, fitness-for-work requirements and other occupational health interventions.
• Build strong, influential partnerships with leaders, employee representatives, HR/EHW, EHS and technical specialists including Industrial Hygiene and Toxicology to align Occupational Health priorities across countries, sites and functions; use data and insights to inform decisions, manage competing priorities and mitigate health-related business risks.
• Lead and/or contribute to regional strategic improvement programmes (e.g., EHS risk reduction programmes, business model enhancements, capability building, quality and governance improvements), translating strategy into measurable outcomes.
• Monitor changes in Occupational Health legislation, professional standards and emerging health risks across the region, ensuring appropriate governance, compliance and organisational readiness.
• Establish and maintain an effective clinical governance framework across Europe, including oversight and assurance of internal and third-party Occupational Health providers, covering statutory health surveillance, fitness-for-work assessments, case management, referral pathways, competency requirements, clinical audit and other core Occupational Health activities.
• Monitor and review service performance and key metrics across the region; identify trends, escalate risks/opportunities and drive continuous improvement through effective influence and communication.
• In the UK, hold accountability for the performance, quality, governance and continuous improvement of Occupational Health services delivered to UK businesses, ensuring services are safe, compliant, effective, financially sustainable and responsive to business needs.
• Collaborate within the regional and global matrix (Global Head of OH, other Regional Medical Directors/Heads of Occupational Health and functional partners) to shape and implement strategic priorities, sharing insights and lessons learned.
• Support development of the regional OH matrix community, including coaching/mentoring, knowledge sharing and strengthening capability in a matrixed organisation.
• Line management of aligned reports.
• Represent GSK externally as required across UK and Europe with key stakeholders, advisory boards and industry groups, bringing forward best practice and influencing thought leadership in Occupational Health.

We are looking for an experienced Occupational Health physician with these required skills to achieve our goals:
• Qualified physician with full GMC registration (UK) or ability to register with GMC.
• MFOM or FFOM (Faculty of Occupational Medicine), or equivalent specialist qualification in Occupational Medicine.
• Strong technical expertise in Occupational Medicine, including workplace health risk management, health surveillance, fitness-for-work, occupational disease prevention, clinical governance and regulatory compliance.
• Substantial leadership experience within Occupational Health in a large, complex matrix organisation, including strategic leadership, clinical governance and influencing senior stakeholders across multiple geographies.
• Experience leading outsourced or hybrid Occupational Health service models, including governance of third-party providers and performance management through formal governance structures.
• Proven ability to communicate clearly and influence a wide range of stakeholders, including senior leaders, HR, EHS and clinical peers, in a matrixed environment.

If you have the following characteristics, it would be a plus:
• Demonstrated coaching and leadership ability, including developing capability in others and building effective clinical networks.

• Systems-thinking mindset and experience working in a matrixed, regional and/or global organisation.
• Well-developed awareness of self, others and impact of self on others.

job_description:
We create a place where people can grow, be their best, be safe, and feel welcome, valued and included. We offer a competitive salary, an annual bonus based on company performance, healthcare and wellbeing programmes, pension plan membership, and shares and savings programme.

Discover more about our company wide benefits and life at GSK on our webpage Life at GSK | GSK
Senior Director, Global Head of Sample Management
GSK is bringing the physical and digital sides of sample management together under a single global leader for the first time. You will lead a global organisation spanning automated storage, sample preparation and logistics, automation engineering and a digital sample platform built and owned within the function, serving the full range of modalities in our portfolio — from small molecules through large molecules, oligonucleotides and conjugates to emerging formats.
The role exists because of where discovery is going. GSK’s Lab-in-an-Automated-Loop (LIAL) programme is moving research towards continuous, increasingly autonomous design–make–test–analyse cycles. An autonomous laboratory has a hard requirement for sample registration the moment a new molecule is made, for storage that knows its own state, and for plating and delivery that an automated workflow can call without a person in the loop. Sample Management has moved from a support service to a rate-limiting dependency for the entire GSK research ecosystem.
The scale is substantial — collections numbering in the millions of samples and growing quickly in the newer modalities, high-capacity automated stores measured in millions of tubes, millions of assay-ready wells dispensed each year, and routine international distribution to partners across dozens of countries.
This is deliberately a combined role, and the combination is the point. Sample Management is already a strong, high-performing global operation. · Run high-throughput, modality-agnostic operations and global cold-chain logistics with measurable performance on cycle time, reliability, availability and traceability — and treat sample integrity as data, capturing storage history, time out of storage, freeze–thaw cycles and QC results against every sample.
· Own the external sample network in both directions — offsite archives, CROs, collaborators and future external execution partners — with digital manifests, identifier mapping, data return and service levels.
· Lead Sample Management’s part of major site transitions and capital programmes, including a multi-year UK relocation and the readiness of new facilities, from business case through installation, validation and handover.

Why You?

· Working understanding of data standards, data models and integration patterns, including APIs, events and FAIR principles.
· Experience delivering capital programmes end to end, including business case, procurement, FAT/SAT, validation and handover.
· Working knowledge of controlled and restricted materials, chain of custody, material transfer agreements, and international shipping and export requirements.

· Product management practice: roadmaps, backlogs, user research, and measuring adoption and value.

Internal Quality Inspections
• Deliver a planned programme of internal quality inspections across homes, in line with the schedule agreed with the Head of Regulation and Compliance and prioritised according to regulatory risk, inspection history and operational intelligence. • Conduct inspections against the internal quality framework, using the relevant regulatory inspection methodologies for England, Wales and Scotland to assess each home’s compliance position as a regulator would.
• Assess all aspects of home performance during visits, including quality and safety of care, leadership and management, staffing, governance, environment, and resident and family experience.
• Apply ratings and judgements consistently and rigorously, ensuring assessments are objective, evidence-based and accurately reflect the home’s position at the time of inspection. Inspection Reporting and Feedback • Produce clear, accurate and well-structured reports documenting findings, evidence, ratings or judgements and targeted improvement recommendations. • Submit completed reports for review and sign-off within agreed timescales, ensuring findings are robustly evidenced and reports are consistently high quality.

• Ensure improvement actions are specific, measurable, realistic and prioritised according to risk. Follow-Up and Improvement Tracking • Monitor progress of improvement actions following inspections, following up with Home Managers and Area Directors at agreed intervals.
• Escalate homes where actions are not progressing, where re-inspection shows deterioration, or where findings indicate imminent regulatory risk.

Framework Maintenance and Inspection Readiness • Support the Head of Regulation and Compliance to keep the internal quality framework up to date, identifying any changes to regulatory methodologies, rating descriptors or evidence requirements. • Contribute to audit tools, evidence checklists, self-assessment guides and inspection preparation resources, drawing on learning from home visits.
• Stay current with CQC, CIW and Care Inspectorate inspection frameworks and share regulatory insight from inspection activity.
• Support Home Managers and Area Directors to prepare for regulatory inspection, including evidence gathering, self-assessment and presentation of the home’s work. KPI Monitoring, Intelligence and Stakeholder Engagement
• Contribute inspection-based intelligence to Group quality and compliance reporting, helping to contextualise performance data and identify homes where trends align with inspection findings. • Maintain accurate records of inspection activity, findings, ratings and action progress within quality management systems. • Build positive, constructive relationships with Home Managers, Area Directors and Regional Directors, establishing the role as credible, knowledgeable and supportive. ABOUT HIVED 📦
At HIVED, we’re steamrolling forward as one of Europe’s fastest growing startups, and our momentum shows no signs of slowing.
Based in London, we are a climate and logistics start-up building the first sustainable parcel delivery network at scale, powered by a 100% electric fleet. In an ever-growing industry where unreliable service has long been the norm, HIVED has been built from the ground-up to meet the demands of modern consumers and disrupt parcel delivery.
A tech company at heart, our talent and technology is laser-focused on delivering the best possible delivery experience for end-customers and meeting the needs of our retail partners. From our drivers to our data engineers, we are constantly working to improve this customer experience that makes us deliver better.
Already trusted by leading international brands such as John Lewis, Nespresso, Uniqlo, H&M brands and more, we are solidifying our position as the leaders in Europe to tackle this growing market.
Our tight-knit team is made up of ex-Revolut, Bain, HelloFresh, ASOS, Apple and Google employees, and we are backed by some of Europe’s leading investors and VCs in climate-tech, logistics and mobility including Planet A Ventures https://planet-a.com/, Maersk Growth https://www.maersk.com/growth, Pale Blue Dot VC https://sifted.eu/articles/pale-blue-dot-vc-87m-fund/, Eka Ventures https://techcrunch.com/2021/07/12/eka-ventures-closes-95m-impact-vc-fund-for-sustainable-consumption-healthcare-and-society/, NordicNinja VC https://nordicninja.com/ and the British government. We’re passionate about driving innovation and redefining the future of delivery.
 
ROLE OVERVIEW 📝
We're looking for a Senior or Staff Engineer to take on some of the hardest problems at HIVED: the planning systems that decide how every parcel moves through our 100% electric delivery network.
You'll join the Routing Squad, which owns HIVED's entire planning pipeline: demand forecasting, capacity planning and scheduling, sortation, our collections network and large-scale route optimisation. Most of the work is backend engineering on distributed, production-grade systems, built in close partnership with data scientists, analysts and our operations teams. If your depth is in operations research or machine learning and you want to see your models plan a real delivery network every day, we'd love to hear from you too.
This is a hands-on role with a lot of technical ownership. You'll shape how the pieces of the pipeline fit together and your work shows up in the routes our drivers take, the cages filled at our depots and the parcels that arrive on time.
The problems are as varied as they are hard. How much volume will each depot see next week, and how many drivers and vehicles do we need to meet it? How should parcels flow through sortation and our collections network so nothing is handled twice? How do we turn each day's parcels into routes that are efficient, reliable and on time? And how do we model the cost and geography of our network as we expand into new cities?
 
WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING 🚀
- Build the planning pipeline. Design, build and run the distributed systems behind routing, capacity planning, sortation and our collections network.
- Turn ambiguity into designs. Take complex operational problems, break them down, and see them through from first investigation to production.
- Shape the architecture. Shape how the planning pipeline fits together, and coordinate with other squads where our systems meet theirs.
- Put models into production. Build and productionise optimisation, forecasting and ML models, making them robust, observable and ready for peak volumes.
- Stay close to the operation. Work directly with operations teams, see how plans perform on the ground, and close the loop with data.
- Raise the bar. Lead design and code reviews, mentor engineers, and set the standards for testing and reliability.
 
 
WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR 🔎
- Typically 5+ years of software engineering experience, building and operating production systems.
- A track record of technical ownership beyond your own work: you've shaped the architecture or direction of systems spanning multiple components or teams.
- The ability to translate complex, ambiguous operational problems into technical solutions with measurable impact.
- Proficiency in Python or Go, or another language with the ability to ramp up quickly on HIVED's stack.
- An appetite for hard optimisation problems: routing, scheduling, forecasting, supply-demand matching, or other constraint-heavy domains.
- Strong collaboration and written communication skills, with the confidence to work across engineering, data science, analytics and operations.
You also bring depth in at least one of:
- Backend and distributed systems: strong system design skills in distributed, production-grade environments, including event-driven architectures, cloud infrastructure (AWS preferred), and reliability and performance at scale.
- Optimisation / operations research: linear and integer programming, constraint programming or heuristics, and integrating solvers such as OR-Tools or Gurobi into production systems.
- Machine learning: forecasting and predictive models that feed planning decisions, from development to monitoring in production.
 
TECHNOLOGIES WE USE 💻
- Python, Go
- AWS (Lambda, ECS Fargate, Step Functions, SQS, EventBridge, Aurora PostgreSQL), CDK (TypeScript)
- GCP, BigQuery, Looker
- Grafana, Loki, Tempo, Prometheus
- GitHub, GitHub Actions
- Claude Code
- Event-driven architecture and domain-driven design

We believe there is always more to learn, always a better way, and that we're always only just getting started. About DUAL
Working across 21 countries, DUAL has built a reputation as a specialist underwriting group and the market of choice for insurance intermediaries around the world. That’s how we have become one of the world’s largest international underwriting agencies (or MGAs) with US$3.4bn GWP.
DUAL is part of Howden, a leading global insurance group with employee ownership at its heart. Founded in 1994, it provides insurance, reinsurance and underwriting services to clients ranging from private individuals to the largest multinational companies. The Group operates in 57 countries, employs over 24,000 people and manages premiums totalling US$50bn on behalf of its clients.
Administrative Assistant – Bloodstock & Equine (Maternity Cover - 6 month FTC)
As an Administrative Assistant (Bloodstock & Equine), you’ll help the underwriting team enter and process risks accurately, manage the Bloodstock & Equine pipeline, and keep core administration organised. Your work will support timely processing, clear records and effective coordination with internal and external contacts.
You’ll also help manage the online mailbox, maintain client folders and spreadsheets, raise support tickets when issues arise, and produce ad hoc reports. During key renewal periods, you’ll provide accurate and timely support so the team can keep work moving.
What you’ll be doing
You’ll combine risk processing, pipeline tracking and administration to support the Underwriting team day to day. You’ll keep information accurate, route queries appropriately and follow issues through to resolution.
• Enter and process risks in underwriting systems, and track activity across the Bloodstock & Equine pipeline.
• Manage the online mailbox, route emails to the appropriate mailbox and support administration of the internal underwriting system.
• Raise support tickets for identified issues, monitor progress and follow through to timely resolution.
• Maintain spreadsheets and client folders, filing correspondence, proposal forms, contracts and supporting documentation accurately.
• Produce ad hoc reports for the data team and support claims administration when required.
• Coordinate with internal and external contacts, including broking teams, to support accurate and timely risk entry and processing, particularly during renewal periods.
Who we’re looking for
You’ll be able to demonstrate accurate, methodical working, effective prioritisation and clear communication in a role with competing deadlines. You’ll also be comfortable using common Microsoft Office tools and motivated to build your insurance knowledge.
• Essential: Evidence of working accurately and methodically, both independently and collaboratively, with attention to detail.
• Essential: Numeracy and literacy sufficient to maintain records, correspondence, spreadsheets and processing accurately.
• Essential: Clear written and spoken communication, effective organisation and prioritisation, and the ability to plan work to tight deadlines or targets.
• Essential: Competent Microsoft Word and PowerPoint skills, with intermediate Excel capability.
• Essential: GCSE Maths and English at A*–C or equivalent, plus basic working knowledge of FCA requirements relevant to insurance intermediaries.
• Desirable: An insurance background and A-levels or equivalent; willingness to develop knowledge through proactive learning.
What do we offer in return?
A career that you define.
Of course, we offer a competitive range of rewards and benefits to support you, but we know you expect all that. What you might not expect is a job where everyone has a voice, where volunteering in the community is part of the day job, and where everyone is encouraged to play a part towards our sustainability goals. We want people who want to make a difference - not just in the workplace, but in the industry and in the wider community.
Our culture: people first Our core values dictate how we live and work. We’re a group with independence and people at its heart – and a home for talent with a unique culture: the biggest small company in the world.
Being a people-first business has always been central to who we are. Our vision was to create an independent organisation with a distinctive culture that would survive and thrive through the people who shape it. Finding the most talented and entrepreneurial individuals to join the group has been, and will continue to be, key to our success.
Diversity and inclusion
At DUAL, our people are our greatest strength. We are committed to building an open and inclusive culture where everyone feels trusted and that they belong. We work to ensure all candidates, employees, clients and business partners are treated with fairness and respect.
We want every candidate to be able to bring their best to the recruitment process, so if you require reasonable accommodation at any stage, please let us know and we will work with you to provide appropriate support.

In 28 countries, Inspired schools are individually developed and anchored in the vibrant cultures of their respective locations. They collectively form an international family of schools that nurtures each student's academic and personal development in a progressive, dynamic, and innovative learning environment.
By joining our award-winning team of over 14,000 employees, you can work in state-of-the-art facilities alongside industry-renowned educators and leaders in some of the world's most desirable locations. We invest heavily in our team members who enjoy industry-leading professional development, exceptional career opportunities, and mobility across our group.ROLE SUMMARY:
Location: Remote, UK (please note, while this is a fully remote position, candidates must be willing to work from the UK and be authorised to do so in order to be considered)
Start date: November 2026 or January 2027
Contract: Fixed Term (5 months)
Working Pattern: Full-time
Salary: £34,000 - £39,000
 
King's InterHigh (KIH) is launching a new asynchronous learning product: a self-paced study offer spanning iGCSE and International A-Level courses. This is an opportunity to help shape a modern digital learning experience from the ground up — combining strong subject teaching, thoughtful curriculum design, and smart use of technology to support learners wherever and whenever they study.
 
We are hiring Self-Paced Curriculum Designers on a fixed-term basis to design, write, and build courses for Psychology (iGCSE and A Level) — shaping the curriculum, authoring the subject content, and designing it for self-paced, online delivery. You will take the relevant iGCSE or International A-Level specification and turn it into a complete, exam-aligned course that learners can work through independently, using video, assessment, feedback, and interactive digital resources to make learning clear, engaging, and purposeful. This role is about building on strong existing subject knowledge and trusted school materials, then reimagining them for a more flexible, technology-enabled model of learning.
 
These are fixed-term contracts tied to course delivery, with courses to be delivered in September 2027.
 
This is a hands-on creation role with real ownership: you will help define what excellent self-paced online learning looks like for KIH, bringing together pedagogy, digital tools, media, assessment, and learner experience into courses that feel coherent, high-quality, and genuinely useful for students.KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:
Write the course content. Review, adapt, and develop existing materials to design a fully self-paced curriculum for learners
Author lessons, explanations, worked examples, activities, and assessments to the agreed template, structure, and quality standards.
Write to the relevant iGCSE and International A-Level specifications, exam-board requirements, and mark schemes, ensuring content is accurate, complete, and exam-aligned.
Design a mixture of assessment — some that suits self paced learners, with auto-marked and self-checking questions giving learners instant feedback, alongside key pieces throughout the course that deliver teacher-based feedback.
Build it for self-paced delivery. Structure and sequence content for independent, self-paced learners with low teacher contact — using chunking, scaffolding, retrieval practice, and purposeful digital interactions to keep learners moving, thinking, and motivated without a live teacher.
Build courses within school systems to the agreed template and brand, using the available technology to create a polished, consistent learner journey.
Build a suite of multi-modal resources to bring courses to life — video lessons, voiceovers, screencasts, interactive tools, knowledge checks, and other digital learning assets — alongside the written material.
Make content accessible and inclusive to all — SEND-aware, readable, with alt text and WCAG considerations applied.
Deliver to schedule and standard. Work to a production schedule, hitting agreed milestones for each course on a delivery-linked contract.
Submit drafts for editorial / QA review and sign-off, and revise efficiently on feedback.
Understand the constraints around correct licensing and developing IP — using third-party content legally and creating compliant, properly owned material that IOS can continue to use long-term.
THE IDEAL CANDIDATE WILL HAVE:
Essential
Current or recent teacher with a teaching qualification and strong subject and curriculum knowledge.
Experience developing lesson materials for online delivery.
Experience of asynchronous lesson design / course development.
Understanding of how to design for independent, self-paced learners.
Assessment design aligned to iGCSE and International A-Level specifications, exam-board requirements, and mark schemes.
Experience working with an LMS / VLE.
Willing and able to record video lessons and voiceovers, comfortable on camera and mic.
Awareness of accessibility and inclusion (SEND, WCAG, readability).
Self-motivated and self-managing — works to deadlines, comfortable working remotely and autonomously, and confident taking ownership of a course from initial specification through to finished build.
Highly valued
Experience of synchronous lesson design.
Familiarity with iGCSE and International A-Level exam-board requirements and specification alignment.
Interactive content authoring, including an interest in using digital tools to make learning more active, responsive, and engaging.
Basic media editing
Understanding of GDPR, copyright/licensing, and safeguarding in online education.
SAFEGUARDING STATEMENT:
Inspired Education Group is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people and expects all staff, volunteers and other third parties to share this commitment. Safer recruitment practices and pre-employment background checks will be undertaken before any appointment is confirmed.SCHOOL APPLICATION FORM:

The Production Lead is a key support role at the heart of the team, turning Boots offer data into clear, accurate production briefs and orders for agencies and printers. Using recently introduced tools and automated processes, the role takes offer data through to completed briefs, keeping the team’s work flowing smoothly and freeing colleagues to focus on delivering great outcomes for Boots. Key Responsibilities:
Turn Boots offer data into tangible, production-ready briefs, using new tools and automated processes to move quickly and accurately from Boots raw offer data, through ITG’s briefing platform into clear briefs that agencies and printers can use.
Be a friendly, dependable point of contact for assigned category teams and contacts on print production queries.
Join pre-review meetings with category stakeholders to stay across period status and progress, and spot any issues early on.
Check and quality-control briefs generated automatically from SAP PMR offer data, logging issues and supplementing missing or incomplete information — the final check that makes sure what reaches agencies and printers is right.
Process checked and completed briefs through to Flo for content creation, ensuring all necessary information and assets are attached.
Use existing artwork templates wherever appropriate, making sure those batches are processed correctly.
Track briefs through the production process end-to-end, keeping jobs on schedule by checking in with internal and external stakeholders.
Make sure content is created and approved in line with Boots brand and category guidelines before proceeding to print.
Flag recurring data quality or briefing issues to the Senior Production Lead, helping the team continually improve how the tools and processes work.
Escalate any issues via the correct reporting channels so the Senior Production Lead can resolve challenges with the support of the Boots Commercial Operations team.
Help the team through peak trading periods by managing increased brief volumes accurately and within tighter timelines.
Be flexible and ready to move between categories and brief types in line with the Senior Production Lead’s resourcing needs.
Key Relationships:
Senior Production Lead — reporting line, escalation, and support during peak periods.
Category teams, ISM, Opticians, and BMG — day-to-day relationship management.
Agencies and printers — briefing and delivery of production requirements.
Wider production team — working together to share learnings and keep briefs flowing.
Experience in a production, artwork, or coordination role, ideally within retail, FMCG, or agency environments.
A strong aptitude to learn new systems quickly.
Enthusiasm for new tools and process automation (including AI), and a keen interest in making ways of working smoother for the whole team.
High attention to detail, particularly when checking automated outputs and supplementing missing information.
Strong organisational skills, able to manage multiple live briefs across different categories at once.
Friendly, proactive communicator, comfortable liaising with category stakeholders, agencies, and printers.
A supportive team player who takes pride in work that keeps the wider team running smoothly.
Calm under pressure, particularly during peak trading periods with high briefing volumes and tight deadlines.
Work’s a treat!
Perks at ITG — alongside a competitive salary, here's what you can look forward to:
Time off that works for you — 25 days' holiday + bank holidays, a paid Wellbeing Day, flexible bank holidays to honour cultural or religious observances, and the option to buy or carry over up to 5 extra days.
Flexibility & lifestyle — Smart Working with up to 40% from home, and after 12 months, the option to work from abroad for up to 90 days a year.
Family & life milestones — Enhanced family friendly leave, 3 extra days for your wedding/honeymoon, and an Employee Assistance Programme whenever you need support.
Financial perks — Pension scheme, Corporate Medical Cash Plan, electric car salary sacrifice scheme, and tax-efficient payroll giving to your favourite charities.
Growth & recognition — Funding for professional qualifications, monthly Employee of the Month awards (£250 bonus), and referral bonuses of up to £1,500.
Community & wellbeing — Regular Wellbeing Workshops, 30+ Wellbeing Champions, a paid Volunteer Day, and an online perks platform with discounts on top brands, days out, and gym memberships.
We Value Diversity
We champion and welcome diversity in our workforce and ensure all job applicants receive equal and fair treatment, regardless of age, race, gender or gender identity, religion, sexual orientation, disability, or nationality.
We are not only committed to increasing the visibility and recognition of talent from under-represented groups within our organisation, but the wider industry too.
At the end of the day, we make sure we take time to look after ourselves, each other, and the planet, because we’re always stronger together.
ITG have a number of community groups available to employees and exist to offer a safe space for like-minded colleagues, with shared interests to connect, socialise and check in with each other.
What next?
If you found yourself interested in knowing more, drop us your application and someone from our team will be in touch.

Job Title: Director of Access, International

The Director of Access, International is a key leadership role within the International Value & Access organisation, responsible for shaping and executing reimbursement, coverage and market access strategies across international markets. This role plays a critical part in ensuring that people living with diabetes have timely and sustainable access to Insulet's portfolio of innovative technologies.
Working closely with the Director of Value, Director of Policy and Public Affairs and country market access leaders, and cross-functional partners, the Director of Access will lead the development and execution of access strategies that optimise reimbursement, protect and enhance value, and accelerate adoption across both existing and future product portfolios.
As a recognised reimbursement and payer expert, the Director of Access International will influence strategic decisions across the business while building market access capabilities, driving excellence and establishing Insulet as a trusted partner to payers and healthcare systems.
Responsibilities • Deep understanding of reimbursement policy and regulations across multiple markets and able to translate those into requirements for launch and ongoing market access
• Develop and lead reimbursement and market access strategies across international markets aligned with International and Global business priorities. • Partner with country teams to co-create ambitious, evidence-based access plans that maximise patient access, reimbursement uptake and long-term value. • Provide strategic leadership on reimbursement trends, payer dynamics and policy developments to inform business planning and market priorities. • Serve as a trusted advisor to country leadership teams on access challenges, opportunities and strategic trade-offs.
• Lead reimbursement planning and execution for new product launches, lifecycle extensions and market expansion initiatives. • Ensure launch readiness from a reimbursement perspective by identifying and proactively addressing market-specific requirements.
• Maintain oversight of key access milestones, risks and opportunities across international markets.
• Influence evidence strategies to protect pricing, strengthen reimbursement positions and support broader market adoption. • Lead the generation and dissemination of reimbursement and payer insights across international markets. Required Skills and Competencies • Deep expertise in reimbursement, payer policy and market access strategy across multiple international healthcare systems. • Demonstrated success securing reimbursement and expanding patient access in complex payer environments. • Strong understanding of health economics, value communication and evidence generation. • Exceptional communication, presentation and stakeholder management skills. • Ability to synthesise complex information and translate it into clear strategic recommendations. • Experience leading reimbursement submissions, tenders and payer engagement strategies. • Ability to develop tools, frameworks and resources that enable market access success. Education and Experience
• Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience and extensive experience in pharmaceutical and/ or medical device sales (preferably with diabetes products) and 3rd party reimbursement procedures and/or equivalent combination of education and experience.
• Experience working with national, regional and private payer organisations across multiple markets including EU5
• Related business experience working with managed markets, national and regional, public and private payers.
• Experience calling on and developing relationships with key contacts in managed markets and third-party payers.
Additional Information
• This role can be hybrid from our either London, Frankfurt, Utrecht or Paris offices. • Travel is estimated at 30% but will flex depending on business need.

Senior Finance Operations Analyst
Intapp is seeking a Senior Finance Operations Analyst of Sales Compensation to join our global accounting team. This new role owns the technical administration, configuration, and optimization of our incentive compensation management (ICM) platform and reports into the Assistant Corporate Controller organization. You will translate complex compensation plans into accurate, auditable system logic that supports our monthly payouts and accounting close.
Day to day, you will configure crediting rules, quotas, and payout calculations, test and troubleshoot the platform, build reporting and integrations, and partner with Sales Operations, IT, FP&A, Payroll, and HR to keep data accurate from opportunity through final payout. You will also help administer user access and security controls in line with ITGC and SOX requirements.
What you will do
As a Senior Finance Operations Analyst, Sales Compensation, you can expect to:
• Lead aspects of the implementation, configuration, and ongoing administration of our ICM platform, including crediting rules, quota management, payout calculations, and reporting that supports the monthly payout and accounting close.
• Translate compensation plan documents into accurate, auditable system logic, design and maintain workflows for plan changes, exceptions, adjustments, and special cases, and run comprehensive testing to validate accuracy before annual plans launch.
• Advise stakeholders during plan design discussions on system capabilities, limitations, and best practices, turn compensation requirements into prioritized system enhancements aligned to business objectives, and represent Finance in Agile Scrum ceremonies, sprint planning, and backlog refinement.
• Build and maintain reporting within the ICM platform for user dashboards, attainment tracking, and leadership reporting, and develop and implement integrations with source systems to protect data integrity from opportunity data through final payout.
• Serve as part of the finance system administration team for the ICM platform, managing user access and security controls in compliance with ITGC and SOX requirements, while monitoring performance, troubleshooting calculation errors, data discrepancies, and integration failures, automating manual processes, and documenting data flows, transformation logic, and system dependencies.
What you will need
Intapp is looking for intellectually curious, self-motivated professionals who like to get hands-on to contribute to the overall success of the business and their team. To apply for this Senior Finance Operations Analyst, Sales Compensation role, you will ideally have:
• Hands-on experience implementing and administering a sales compensation platform, along with experience working with an HCM system such as Workday
• A strong understanding of sales compensation processes and their accounting impact, with technical skills in SQL, data integration tools, and system configuration
• Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities, with a systematic approach to debugging and root cause analysis
• Excellent documentation practices and the ability to communicate technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders
• Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to interact with all levels of management
• Experience working in a public company environment with requirements to comply with SOX
What you will gain at Intapp
At Intapp, you'll get the opportunity to bring your talents and intellectual curiosity to create better outcomes for our people and our clients. You'll be part of a growing public company, with a modern work environment that's connected yet flexible and where your professional growth and well-being are top priorities. We'll collaborate and grow together, supporting each other in a positive, open atmosphere that fosters creativity, innovation, and teamwork.
Here, you will have the opportunity to:
• Expand Your Skills: Unlock your potential with professional development opportunities supported by a community of experienced professionals. We offer reimbursement for training and continuing education to help you stay ahead in your career.
• Enjoy Where You Work: Thrive in our modern, open offices designed to inspire creativity and collaboration. Our complimentary lunches and fully stocked kitchens ensure you have everything you need to stay energized throughout the day.
• Support What Matters Most: Our comprehensive wellness and flexible time off programs and our benefits are designed to care for you and your family. Our family-formation benefits and support during your family-building journey ensure you have the resources you need when it matters most. We believe in giving back and supporting our communities with paid volunteer time off and a donation matching program for the causes you care about.
Join us and be a part of a collaborative and welcoming culture where your contributions are valued, and your professional growth is a priority. Together, we are building a company of long-term value that we can all be proud of.

Working closely with our Product Lead, Engineering, Design, and Sustainability Experts, you will take ownership of your product's journey from discovery and prioritization to delivery, optimization, and continuous improvement. You will play an important role in shaping AI-native capabilities, balancing innovation with reliability, transparency, and customer trust. In a dynamic B2B SaaS environment, you will combine customer empathy, technical understanding, and strategic judgment to build products that make a difference. What can you expect?
Product Strategy & Prioritization
Translate the Product Lead's strategic direction into actionable roadmaps, clearly scoped features, and measurable outcomes
Own and continuously prioritize your product backlog, balancing customer value, feasibility, effort, and strategic relevance
Make informed trade-offs to focus resources on initiatives that deliver the greatest impact
Product Discovery & Customer Insights
Leverage customer research, market trends, and internal expertise to identify opportunities and inform product decisions
Validate customer problems, assumptions, and potential solutions through structured discovery, experimentation, and testing
Translate insights into product improvements and continuously refine priorities based on evidence
Product Delivery & Performance
Own the end-to-end product lifecycle, from initial concept and requirements definition through launch, optimization, and potential sunset
Collaborate with Engineering, Product Design, and Sustainability Experts to deliver high-quality solutions that meet customer needs
Define success metrics, monitor product performance, and adjust initiatives to achieve measurable business and customer outcomes
AI-Native Product Development
Identify opportunities where AI agents create meaningful customer value, while recognizing when deterministic solutions or human judgment are more appropriate
Develop clear Product Requirements Documents (PRDs) for conventional and AI-native features, ensuring alignment on scope, expected behavior, and quality
Define and maintain quality standards for agentic functionality, including evaluations, golden examples, and governance fact sheets that support reliability and customer trust
Product Operations & AI-First Ways of Working

Ensure product initiatives meet established readiness, validation, and delivery standards
Integrate AI tools into daily product management activities, including research, synthesis, analysis, documentation, and workflow automation
Stakeholder Collaboration & Product Enablement
Act as the central point of contact for your product, communicating roadmap decisions, progress, risks, and changes clearly
Collaborate across Engineering, Design, Sustainability, and business teams to create alignment and share knowledge across the product pillar
Develop clear enablement materials for internal teams and customers to support product understanding, adoption, and continuous learning
What should you bring along?
Experience & Domain Focus
At least 3 years of professional experience as a Product Manager, ideally gained in a start-up or scale-up environment
Strong B2B SaaS experience with demonstrated end-to-end product ownership, including product launches and sunsetting
Experience in procurement, supply chain, or compliance is a strong advantage
Knowledge of carbon accounting and emissions reporting frameworks, such as the GHG Protocol, CSRD, or Scope 1–3, is a plus
Technical/Methodolical Skills
Strong technical understanding and confidence in collaborating with Engineering on system architecture, data models, integrations, APIs, and technical trade-offs
Solid analytical capabilities, including statistics fundamentals, A/B testing, cohort analysis, and data-informed decision-making
Experience developing product requirements, conducting discovery, validating hypotheses, and measuring product outcomes
Practical experience working with AI-native products, including agentic workflows, evaluations, golden examples, and governance documentation
Confident daily use of AI-powered tools and collaborative development environments, including GitHub, shared context repositories, Cursor, Claude, or comparable solutions

High level of ownership, sound judgment, and confidence in making decisions in ambiguous and fast-moving environments

Experimental and evidence-driven mindset, with the willingness to validate assumptions early, learn quickly, and adjust direction when needed
Comfort working asynchronously in a distributed, Europe-based team with overlapping collaboration hours across US and UK time zones

Strong cross-functional collaboration skills, particularly when working with Engineering, Design, and business stakeholders
Ability to build alignment, communicate trade-offs transparently, and keep stakeholders informed about product decisions and progress

Fin, now part of Salesforce, is on a mission to help businesses provide perfect customer experiences.
Our AI Agent Fin is the highest-performing AI Customer Agent on the market today, enabling businesses to deliver impeccable, always-on customer support across the customer journey, from service, to sales, to ecommerce. Powered by our own AI models, Fin resolves complex customer issues end-to-end across every channel, with minimal set-up and integration. Fin can also be combined with our natively integrated Intercom help desk, giving modern support teams one single system.
Together with Salesforce, the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success, we're building the future of customer experience. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn't a buzzword, it's a way of life. The world of work as we know it is changing, and we're looking for Trailblazers who are passionate about bettering business and the world through AI.
Ready to level up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You're in the right place. Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.
What's the opportunity? We’re looking for Staff Product Engineers to join the AI Group to build Fin's AI-powered products. Product Engineers working in ML work closely with both our ML Scientists and product teams. They must deeply understand our product, our customers, our ML tech stack and our broader product stack. Our group is responsible for defining new ML features, researching appropriate algorithms and technologies, and rapidly getting first prototypes in our customers’ hands.
We are an extremely product focussed team. We work in partnership with Product and Design functions of teams we support. Our team's dedicated Engineers enable us to move to production fast, often shipping to beta in weeks after a successful offline test.
We are very passionate about applying machine learning technology, and have productized everything from classic supervised models, to cutting-edge unsupervised clustering algorithms, to novel applications of transformer neural networks. We test and measure the real customer impact of each model we deploy.

About the role
Own how io.tt tests its platform: the strategy, the stack and the quality bar.
You'll decide where testing effort goes, write the frameworks that enforce it, and be the person product, design and engineering turn to when they want to know whether something is ready to ship. There are good foundations to build on and plenty still to shape. In your first few months you'll map where our real risks are, get a cross-service end-to-end suite gating CI, and agree a quality bar the whole team signs up to.
Global brands put io.tt QR codes and NFC tags on their products. When someone scans one, our platform works out which brand and campaign the tag belongs to, applies the brand's rules and risk checks, and sends the person to the right experience in milliseconds. Behind that, every scan is recorded for analytics, pushed live to the brand's dashboard, and passed on to their own tools, from CRMs to data warehouses.
Brands build and change those experiences themselves, and tags printed years ago still have to work. That makes for some interesting testing problems: a product driven largely by configuration, data that has to add up across services, and a long tail of published experiences that must not break when we ship.
Our stack is TypeScript throughout, on Node and Bun services, with PostgreSQL, MongoDB and Redis on AWS, Next.js on the front end and GitHub Actions for CI.
The role is hybrid, with regular time together in our central London (E1) office. We agree the pattern as a team. You'll also get one week a year working from anywhere (on UK hours), 20 days' holiday plus a festive shutdown with an extra day for each year of service (up to 5), private medical insurance with Vitality after probation, a company pension and sick pay, and a cycle to work scheme. In the office there's breakfast, drinks and snacks, regular team events, a dog-friendly policy and a casual dress code.
You'll need the right to work in the UK. We aren't able to offer visa sponsorship for this role.
To apply, email careers@io.tt with your CV and a few lines on a test framework or quality strategy you've built and what you'd change about it now.
What you'll do
• Define the test strategy for the platform: what quality means for us, where the real risks are and where testing effort should go
• Build and maintain cross-service end-to-end and integration suites (Playwright or similar) that gate CI and that teams trust
• Set the quality bar with product, design and engineering, and hold it when deadlines get tight
• Protect backward compatibility so published customer experiences keep working as features and schemas change
• Test experiences that brands configure themselves, using contract, model-based and property-based testing
• Validate analytics and data across PostgreSQL and MongoDB, from pipeline integrity to aggregation accuracy
• Own visual regression and cross-browser and cross-device testing for published experiences
• Build WCAG accessibility checks into the pipeline
• Use AI-assisted tools to generate tests, then review and harden what they produce
What we're looking for
• Strong, hands-on TypeScript. You write test code to the same standard as production code, and you're comfortable reading a Node or Bun back end to work out what to test.
• You've built E2E and integration frameworks from scratch and run them in CI, as gates that teams trust rather than work around.
• A risk-based approach to testing. You can take a product that's only partly specified, work out what matters most, and turn that into a prioritised plan. You care more about the right tests than the number of tests.
• You've owned quality across teams: set a quality bar, explained it to product, design and engineering, and held it under pressure.
• 5+ years in test engineering on web-based SaaS, including time where you owned the test strategy, not only carried it out.
• Experience with contract, model-based or property-based testing, data and analytics validation, visual regression, accessibility testing, or a background in CMS, analytics or other configuration-heavy SaaS products

Role Overview
Role:
We are looking for a HIL (hardware-in-the-loop) Test Manager to build and lead the team that owns our hardware test infrastructure: the systems our quantum-computer control software is tested on before it ever touches a real quantum system.
Every software and science change is validated against shared test systems before it reaches a quantum computer. We are now investing in the next generation of these: representative QA systems for fast feedback, and staging systems as close to a production quantum system as possible, with all the real-time and non-real-time hardware. You will define these systems, build them with our manufacturing team, and own them through their life: maintenance, upgrades to each programme baseline, and availability to the teams that depend on them.
This is a build-from-scratch role with budget and rack space already allocated. You will also act as our test architect: we have deep physics and engineering expertise, and you will bring the formal software-testing experience to shape what gets tested where (simulation versus real hardware) and how testing gates releases. You will start with one engineer hire alongside you and grow the team deliberately, turning the test estate into a reliable service the engineering teams depend on.
Responsibilities:
You will own the hardware test estate end to end and define how it is used. That includes making the estate self-service, with clear reservation and scheduling, published state and availability, and runbooks. Teams own their tests and what they gate on; your team owns the rigs and the plumbing.
You will hire, develop and lead a small team, starting with a hardware-focused test systems engineer, and work across the business with the wider Quantum System Infrastructure (QSI) teams, Compute IT, Facilities, Manufacturing, Software and Science.
Key responsibilities include:
• Own the hardware test estate: today's CI systems through to the new QA and staging systems for our current and future quantum-computer programmes.
• Define the test-system architecture: which systems exist, what each one represents, and how teams use them.
• Plan and deliver new test-system builds with Manufacturing, and own ongoing maintenance and upgrades so every test system tracks its programme's current baseline.
• Shape the testing strategy with the software teams: what runs in simulation or against emulators, what requires real hardware, and how hardware-in-the-loop results gate releases.
• Drive automation throughout: provisioning, firmware flashing, recovery and configuration of test systems as code, not manual effort.
Requirements:

Job Description:
WHAT - Summary & Purpose of the Position
The Director, Business Management, Clinical Development Operations provides an integrated view of portfolio demand, workforce capacity, external-resource requirements, financial plans and operational performance across CDO. Reporting to the Head of Strategy & Operations and acting as a strategic partner to the CDO Leadership Team, the role enables evidence-based decisions on resource deployment, investment priorities and organisational capability.
The Director owns the CDO business management framework and resource-planning assumptions, including the resource algorithms used to translate portfolio demand into internal headcount and CRO/FSP requirements. Working with CDO functions, R&D Capacity Planning, Finance, Clinical Partnerships, Procurement and Portfolio Management, the role leads scenario planning, consolidated forecasting, budget oversight and executive performance reporting.
The role leads a team of approximately three Regional Business Managers who partner with CDO functions and Study, Site Management & Monitoring leadership to coordinate regional and functional resource and budget planning. Through clear governance, consistent data and forward-looking analyses, the Director identifies capacity, funding and delivery risks and provides actionable recommendations to senior leadership.
The Director also contributes to the effective operation of the Strategy & Operations team and supports key CDO leadership activities, including functional reviews, global townhalls and leadership forums.
WHAT - Main Responsibilities & Technical Competencies
1. Business Management Leadership
• Establish and lead a comprehensive CDO Business Management function supporting portfolio oversight, workforce planning, financial management, governance, and business performance.
• Develop and implement business management strategies that enable delivery of CDO and broader R&D objectives.
• Serve as a trusted strategic partner to the Head of Strategy and Ops and CDO Leadership Team on organizational planning, investment decisions, and resource allocation.
• Drive continuous improvement of business processes, governance models, and management reporting frameworks.
• Lead and coach a team of business management professionals where applicable and foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, and operational excellence.
2. Portfolio Oversight & Strategic Planning
• Leveraging tools such as OnePlan and CDO insights, maintain an integrated view of the Clinical Development Operations portfolio across all therapeutic areas, development stages, and geographies.
• Partner with Portfolio Management and Development leadership to understand future portfolio scenarios and associated operational implications.
• Assess portfolio-driven demand and translate future study requirements into workforce and financial impact analyses.
• Lead scenario planning exercises to evaluate capacity, investment, and organizational risks associated with portfolio changes.
• Support governance forums by providing evidence-based analyses and recommendations that facilitate informed decision-making.
3. Resource Strategy, Capacity Planning & Workforce Management
• Lead the development and implementation of enterprise-grade workforce planning and resource management frameworks across CDO.
• Maintain oversight of global operational demand, workforce supply, utilization, productivity, and capacity trends.
• Partner with functional and country leaders to develop resource forecasts and mitigation strategies related to portfolio demand.
• Drive organizational resource planning processes and facilitate discussions regarding investment priorities and staffing requirements.
• Ensure consistency and transparency of workforce planning methodologies, assumptions, and reporting.
• Provide leadership visibility into future capacity needs, resource risks, and organizational constraints.
4. Financial Planning, Budget Management & Governance
• Lead development, monitoring, forecasting, and governance of CDO operational budgets.
• Partner with Finance to develop annual operating plans, quarterly forecasts, and long-range financial projections.
• Provide oversight of departmental expenditures and ensure alignment with approved financial plans.
• Work with S&O Partnership team to develop appropriate Work Orders/Purchase Orders etc. • Monitor budget performance and proactively identify risks, opportunities, and corrective actions.
• Support business case development for strategic investments, organizational initiatives, and resource requests.
• Drive financial transparency and accountability across CDO functions and geographic operations.
• Ensure robust governance, compliance, and stewardship of organizational investments.
5. Business Intelligence, Performance Management & Analytics
• Partnering with Business Enablement and Compliance as well as Global Project Management establish and maintain executive-level dashboards, KPIs, and operational performance measures.
• Integrate portfolio, workforce, budget, and operational performance data into comprehensive management reporting.
• Generate actionable business insights to support strategic and operational decisions.
• Monitor organizational health and performance trends through meaningful metrics and predictive analyses.
• Lead development of management reporting packages for leadership/business reviews, governance bodies, and executive committees.
• Promote data-driven decision-making across the organization.
• Translate complex data into scenarios, recommendations and clear decision points for senior leaders.
6. Leadership Team & Organizational Support
• Serve as a member of the extended CDO Leadership Team and contribute to organizational strategy development.
• Support annual strategic planning exercises and operational reviews.
• Lead preparation of executive communications, business reviews, organizational updates, and leadership presentations.
• Coordinate business management activities across central functions and country monitoring organizations.
• Ensure alignment between operational priorities, workforce plans, budgets, and organizational goals.
7. Enterprise Partnership & Cross-Functional Leadership
• Act as the primary CDO business-management partner for Finance, Human Resources, Capacity Planning, Portfolio Management, Procurement, Quality, and other business functions relating to organizational planning and operations.
• Influence enterprise-wide initiatives impacting workforce planning, budgeting, business performance, and operating model evolution.
• Coordinate business-management activities across central functions, regions and Study, Site Management & Monitoring operations.
• Build strong partnerships across Research & Development and broader Ipsen functions.
• Ensure alignment between operational priorities, workforce plans, budgets and organisational goals. • Lead strategic projects designed to enhance organizational effectiveness and operational performance
HOW - Behavioural Competencies Required
Excellence in Execution • Approaches priority setting through the lens of execution
• Establishes clarity on goals, accountabilities, timelines, and next steps
• Focused and performance driven with clear KPIs
• Plans and aligns effectively (steps, resources, timelines)
• Displays commitment to best practice sharing
• Promotes single points of accountability The role integrates portfolio demand, workforce capacity, external resource requirements and financial plans across a complex global organisation. Success requires disciplined planning, clear accountability, robust governance and consistent follow-through.
Collaborates • Builds partnerships and works collaboratively with others to meet shared objectives
• Communicates and collaborates without boundaries
• Removes organizational barriers and supports continuous improvement
• Integrates learnings and demonstrates strong entrepreneurial mindset Success depends on deep partnership with Oncology, Neuro, Rare, V&A, Operations, IC, Finance, Communications, and Leadership to ensure aligned planning cycles, coordinated field operations, and a unified approach to commercial execution.
Business Insights • Makes decisions based on data, facts, and figures
• Considers different perspectives and the patients’ voice
• Translates insights into objectives and setting the bar The role leads budget oversight, financial analysis, variance monitoring, operational decision support, and cross BU planning—requiring strong analytical capability and the ability to turn data into clear, actionable operational and financial direction.
HOW - Knowledge & Experience
Knowledge & Experience (essential):
• Typically 10-12+ years of relevant experience in clinical development operations, R&D business operations, portfolio or capacity planning, financial planning or a related discipline, including significant experience in a global matrix organisation.
• Significant leadership experience supporting global R&D or Clinical Development organizations.
• Demonstrated experience developing and leading workforce planning and resource management processes.
• Extensive experience managing budgets, financial forecasting, and organizational investment planning.
• Strong understanding of clinical development operations and global study delivery models.
• Experience partnering with senior executives and influencing leadership decisions.
• Expertise in business performance management, reporting, analytics, and business intelligence.
• Track record leading complex cross-functional initiatives within a global matrix environment.
• Strong financial acumen and strategic planning capability.
• Exceptional communication, influencing, and stakeholder management skills.

• Advanced degree preferred (MBA, MSc, PharmD, PhD, or equivalent).

Job Description:
WHAT - Summary & Purpose of the Position
Prepare the CMC regulatory strategy activities for the assigned projects throughout the different phases of development from early clinical trials to initial marketing applications, geo-graphical expansion, and life cycle management as assigned by CMC regulatory senior management including leading the preparation of the CMC submission dossiers.
To manage the CMC Regulatory relationship for their assigned product(s)/projects with Ipsen’s manufacturing sites and/or Ipsen’s External Manufacturing Organisation (EMO), Global Regulatory, CMOs and Alliance partner companies to ensure alignment of strategy.
WHAT - Main Responsibilities & Technical Competencies
CMC Regulatory Strategy:
• Lead the development of CMC regulatory strategy (overall CMC regulatory roadmaps) for the assigned projects (new products in development and/ or commercial product(s) for both lifecycle management and geographical expansion through new MAA registrations) ensuring the CMC reg risks are identified, assessed, shared and managed as appropriate; and verifying the CMC regulatory requirements of the targeted countries are met. Work efficiently with CMC regulatory senior management to ensure coherence of strategies across projects.
• Lead the preparation of the CMC part of the dossier by collaborating closely with Pharmaceutical Development and / or Technical Operations teams, to generate effective CMC regulatory dossiers as per the project timelines.
• Write regulatory technical documentation including updating CTD sections with process and analytical data extracting information from reports, batch records, analytical procedures and quality events as appropriate.
• Work closely with Global Regulatory Affairs Therapeutic Area leads to integrate the CMC regulatory strategy to the overall regulatory strategy of the assigned projects and products.
• Anticipate any gaps for planned regulatory submissions, taking into account emerging regulations and country specific requirements, prioritising and planning associated regulatory strategies to address any identified gaps.
• Communicate with global regulatory lead to propose to de-risking some CMC strategic decisions through early communications and validation with worldwide health authorities.
• Lead the CMC regulatory section preparation of briefing documents for regulatory positioning and justification in collaboration with the SMEs.
• Provide CMC regulatory expertise to project teams.
• Propose innovative CMC regulatory pathways to accelerate product delivery for patient enrolment in clinical studies, as required.
• Review of the Target Product Profile (TPP)/ Regulatory risk assessment/ Regulatory Strategy Document/ CCDS/ / Investigational brochures to ensure single aligned regulatory positioning and appropriateness of any CMC aspects, including paediatric (presentation, formulation, excipients) and ROW considerations, as required.
• Assess CMC-Regulatory impact of all changes proposed to the allocated product portfolio, providing strategic regulatory advice and clearly communicating any Regulatory impact and CMC-Regulatory supporting data requirements for subsequent variations/ amendments.
• Manage all Regulatory interactions for Site Registrations, Site Licences, Site master files s and site accreditations with Regulatory Authorities, Alliance partners and CMO’s for assigned product(s) as applicable.
CMC Dossier preparation:
• Ensure collaboration with teams in Pharmaceutical Development and in Technical Operations, as well as with Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) to deliver (coordination, authoring and review) effective, timely and compliant CTA (IND, IMPD), variations, responses to question and MAA modules 1, 2 & 3 in the correct “Ready For Submission” format for assigned products, in compliance with eCTD requirement.
• Work effectively with Global Regulatory Affairs (GRA) Therapeutic area, and GRA Regulatory Operations teams to ensure that CMC-Regulatory submissions comply with Ipsen group policies and procedures. Ensure that submissions are planned and scheduled appropriately to align with Technical Operations implementation requirements or clinical supply needs, while ensuring adequate time for review, approval and publishing tasks. Ensure the consistency of CMC data across the different modules of the dossier.
• Manage submission of annual reports for assigned product(s) as applicable.
CMC Regulatory expertise & Regulatory intelligence
• Participate and represent CMC regulatory strategy department in CMC project teams and Global project team, as necessary, for the assigned projects.
• Proactively provide Ipsen functions (e.g. Pharm Dev, TechOps, SMEs, GRA, Global project teams, etc) with CMC regulatory expertise.
• Communicate key regulatory CMC related guidance’s to Pharmaceutical Development/ technical Operations teams, SMEs and other stakeholders within Ipsen.
• Perform CMC-Regulatory Intelligence activities as required and work with cross-functional departments to ensure related operations are compliant.
Resources and performance
• Coach and develop junior resource within the regulatory strategic CMC Group.
• Lead and manage assigned projects and associated communication and reporting.
• Monitor and report on CMC Regulatory activities and process performance for the allocated products; identify areas for improvement, implement and monitor subsequent actions.
Communication
• Ensure the CMC-Regulatory Strategy Director/Senior Director, is provided with accurate and up-to-date CMC-Regulatory strategy for the assigned product(s).
• Assess CMC Regulatory activities and process performance, identify areas for improvement. Propose and lead continuous improvement process initiatives within the CMC-Regulatory Strategy function.
• CMC-Reg Strategy lead contact with sites, external Alliance partners and CMOs ensuring aligned strategy and optimised communication as applicable.
• Coach and develop junior resource within the CMC regulatory strategy team.
HOW - Behavioural Competencies Required
• Puts values and ethics at the forefront of everything.
• Anchors Ipsen's purpose, mission and commitments to patients and society.
• Identifies contradictory information/demands/inputs to effectively solve problems.
• Develops and evaluates alternative scenario and solutions.
• Able to identify what truly matters and ruthlessly focus/ prioritize on making decisions with real impact.
• Methodically assesses, transparently shares, and makes risk-informed decisions.
• Establishes clarity about the goals, accountabilities, timelines, and next steps; can identify/spot opportunities for real impact on patient and society.
• Displays a commitment to sharing and implementing best practices and committed to excellence in execution.
HOW - Knowledge & Experience
Knowledge & Experience (essential):
• Proven CMC Regulatory experience in managing small molecules and/ or biologicals in a worldwide environment “(approximately 3-6 years’ experience)”.
• Experience should include registration and clinical development (IND/IMPD) and/ or post-approval activities in US and EU and major RoW markets.
• Demonstrated experience in the development and implementation of global CMC-Regulatory strategies for major regulatory submissions.
• Strong project planning skills and ability to develop sound CMC-Regulatory strategy for multiple global changes.
• Proven advanced technical and regulatory writing experience with pharmaceuticals and familiarity with eCTD formats and publishing support functions.
• Sound technical knowledge of the manufacture of pharmaceuticals and appropriate understanding of all regulatory CMC disciplines.
• Strong knowledge of current global regulatory requirements pertaining to the manufacture of pharmaceutical drug substances and drug products.
• Understanding of Pharmaceutical Quality activities and assessment of cGMP compliance, site registration and licensing.
• Proven experience in both internal and external Stakeholder management.
• Proven experience in handling multiple priorities and complex projects in a fast-paced environment.
• Analytical mindset and excellent attention to detail.
• Excellent critical thinking, written, verbal and interpersonal communication skills.
Knowledge & Experience (preferred):
• Experience with regulatory management of CMC activities for medical devices and maintenance of associated technical files including interactions with a Notified Body.
• Experience of Health Authorities interaction.
• Experience should include activities in export countries particularly e.g. China, Japan, Brazil.
Education / Certifications (essential):
