job_title: Research Leader / Senior Research Investigator (Computational Drug Design), London
job_description:
Isomorphic Labs is applying frontier AI to help unlock deeper scientific insights, faster breakthroughs, and life-changing medicines with an ambition to solve all disease.
The future is coming. A future enabled and enriched by the incredible power of machine learning. A future in which diseases are curtailed or cured starting with better and faster drug discovery. 
Come and be part of an interdisciplinary team driving groundbreaking innovation and play a meaningful role in contributing towards us achieving our ambitious goals, while being a part of an inspiring and collaborative culture.
The world we want tomorrow is the one we’re building today. It starts with the culture at this company. It starts with you. 
 
About Iso
Isomorphic Labs (IsoLabs) was launched in 2021 to advance human health by building on and beyond the Nobel-winning AlphaFold system. Since then, our interdisciplinary team of drug discovery experts and machine learning specialists has built powerful new predictive and generative AI models that accelerate scientific discovery at digital speed.
Our name comes from the belief that there is an underlying symmetry between biology and information science. By harnessing AI’s powerful capabilities, we can use it to model complex biological phenomena to help design novel molecules, anticipate how drugs will perform and develop innovative medicines to treat and cure some of the world’s most devastating diseases.
We have built a world-leading drug design engine comprising AI models that are capable of working across multiple therapeutic areas and drug modalities. We are continually innovating on model architecture and developing cutting-edge capabilities to advance rational drug design.
Every day, and with each new breakthrough, we’re getting closer to the promise of digital biology, and achieving our ambitious mission to one day solve all disease with the help of AI.
 
Your impact
We’re hiring at the Research Leader and Senior Scientist levels, and you can apply for either position using the application form below. These roles are ideal for experienced computational chemists who are eager to shape the future of drug discovery at the intersection of computational chemistry and artificial intelligence.
Working as either a Program Lead or a Computational Chemistry Lead, you will provide scientific expertise and strategic direction for portfolio drug discovery projects, guiding them from initiation towards clinical candidate selection. Working alongside world-leading ML scientists, you will play a critical role in enhancing our AI platform through your technical expertise, and apply these improvements to drug design projects. You will have experience of working broadly across drug discovery projects, with the ability to think originally and critically, knowing when to apply innovative ideas, and think with a fresh approach. If you are a skilled Computational Chemist with a passion for applying cutting-edge technology to complex scientific challenges, this role offers an unparalleled opportunity for impact and growth.
As part of this hiring, some roles will have people management responsibilities for building teams of 2-3 Computational Chemists. In this case, you will be responsible for line managing and mentoring a talented and high-performing team, encouraging their scientific growth and career development. You’ll champion our cross-disciplinary approach, fostering a supportive team culture where continuous learning and the adoption of next-generation tools are the standard, not the exception.
What you will do 
• Apply AI-first approaches to provide technical and strategic directions, and execute drug design programs. Take ownership as either an overall Program Lead or Computational Chemistry Lead.
• Collaborate cross-functionally to support the data-driven delivery of high quality scientific solutions to complex technical problems
• Establish principles for embedding cutting-edge AI/ML into modern computational chemistry workflows, ensuring seamless integration across ML, Biology, and Chemistry teams.
• Provide strategic input and technical direction to our ML platform teams.
• Target Discovery: Successfully identify and validate therapeutic targets for early-stage portfolio projects
• If Program Leadership: Champion the drug discovery pipeline, overseeing external collaborations (with CROs) and leading programs to meet critical go/no-go milestones. Prepare detailed scientific proposals and reports to support new and ongoing programs.
• Embrace and champion our culture of inclusion and continuous professional development.
Skills and qualifications 
Essential:
• PhD in Computational Chemistry, or a related scientific field, or equivalent industrial experience.
• 8+ / 5+ years of professional experience in a Computational Drug Design role, operating within a biotech, pharma or CRO setting.
• Proven track record of project leadership / leading computational chemistry efforts on drug discovery programs, demonstrating significant contributions to project progression (ideally from hit identification through to lead optimisation or candidate nomination).
• Expertise in writing and implementing Python scripts for analysis and tool development, and/or utilising pipelining tools to support cheminformatics and design workflows.
• A genuine passion for drug discovery and enthusiasm for the potential of ML to transform the field.
• Prior experience leveraging machine learning and generative AI methods for hit finding (e.g. ultra-large virtual screening and active learning), molecular design and lead optimisation (e.g. REINVENT, cofolding and AI-powered ligand/pose scoring methods).
• For a people / program management position: experience of leading a high-performing scientific team, mentoring and empowering them to thrive in their roles.
• Strong track record of scientific achievements, evidenced by publications, patents, and presentations.
• Excellent communication (written and verbal) and interpersonal skills, with an ability to work effectively in a cross- functional, collaborative team environment. 
• Track record of strategic thinking and creative problem solving with a strong growth mindset, adaptability, and eagerness to learn new concepts and techniques.
 
Nice to have:
• Experience with using frontier large language models and systems
• Knowledge of other specific drug discovery approaches like fragment-based drug design (FBDD), and alternative modalities like PROTACs, molecular glues, PPI inhibitors or stabilisers, peptides etc.
• Understanding of drug metabolism and pharmacokinetics (ADME + DMPK) principles.
Culture and values
We are guided by our shared values. It's not about finding people who think and act in the same way. These values help to guide our work and will continue to strengthen it. 
Thoughtful
Thoughtful at Iso is about curiosity, creativity and care. It is about good people doing good, rigorous and future-making science every single day.
Brave
Brave at Iso is about fearlessness, but it’s also about initiative and integrity. The scale of the challenge demands nothing less.
Determined
Determined at Iso is the way we pursue our goal. It’s a confidence in our hypothesis, as well as the urgency and agility needed to deliver on it. Because disease won’t wait, so neither should we.
Together
Together at Iso is about connection, collaboration across fields and catalytic relationships. It’s knowing that transformation is a group project, and remembering that what we’re doing will have a real impact on real people everywhere.
Creating an extraordinary company
We believe that to be successful we need a team with a range of skills and talents. We're building an environment where collaboration is fundamental, learning is shared and every employee feels supported and able to thrive. We value unique experiences, knowledge, backgrounds, and perspectives, and harness these qualities to create extraordinary impact.
We are committed to equal employment opportunities regardless of sex, race, religion or belief, ethnic or national origin, disability, age, citizenship, marital, domestic or civil partnership status, sexual orientation, gender identity, pregnancy or related condition (including breastfeeding) or any other basis protected by applicable law. If you have a disability or additional need that requires accommodation, please do not hesitate to let us know.
Hybrid working
It’s hugely important for us to share knowledge and build strong relationships with each other, and we find it easier to do this if we spend time together in person. This is why we follow a hybrid model, and would require you to be able to come into the office 3 days a week (currently Tuesday, Wednesday, and one other day depending on which team you’re in). If you have additional needs that would prevent you from following this hybrid approach, we’d be happy to talk through these if you’re selected for an initial screening call.

Help teams adopt a rigorous experimentation culture, improving how we test and measure product changes.
Uncover insights across the customer journey to improve acquisition, retention, and monetization.
Establish scalable analytics foundations, including clear metric frameworks, data models, and self-service reporting.
Partner with engineering teams to design robust, compliant data infrastructure and pipelines.
Guide the development of machine learning capabilities that enhance marketing acquisition, product personalization, and operational efficiency.
Translate complex data signals into clear, actionable recommendations for leadership.
Define the business unit's data strategy to support product and engineering priorities.

Founded in 2012, LADbible Group is redefining entertainment and news for a social generation. Our global community engages with our content–spanning editorial, video, documentary and live – we reach 1 billion people each and every month. Our mission is to give the youth generation a voice by building communities that laugh, think and act. Using all major platforms, we’ve rapidly risen to become one of the world's largest publishers. 
About the Team 
Our Creator Program sits within CONTENTbible and partners with a roster of leading UK and US creators to grow their channels, audience and revenue. We generate over 1 billion organic views a month for Creators. We use LADbible’s audience insight and platform expertise to drive long-term channel health. The roster has grown rapidly over the past year, and the Program is central to LADbible’s creator-led growth strategy and its pipeline into new IP.
About the Role
We’re looking for a Lead Channel Manager to own our Tier 1 creator channels across YouTube, Facebook and Snapchat. You’ll lead the day-to-day strategy, optimisation and growth for some of our biggest talent, help shape how the Program scales, and support a team of Channel Managers across the wider creator roster.
You’ll bring a curious and data-driven mindset to the role. You’ll spot what’s working, try new formats and push boundaries, turning those insights into clear plans that drive revenue, retention and subscriber growth for our creators. As their go-to contact, you’ll build strong relationships and share the insights that help them grow their audiences.
What the opportunity looks like 
• Lead the day-to-day running, scheduling and strategic direction of content across Facebook, Snapchat, YouTube and other relevant platforms for our Tier 1 accounts.
• Monitor and optimise revenue, watch time, engagement, retention and audience growth. Developing strategies that drive consistent performance across Tier 1 accounts.
• Monitor and respond to changes in platform algorithms, monetisation products, community guidelines and emerging platforms.
• Coach and support junior Channel Managers through regular feedback, knowledge sharing and quality control, ensuring consistent delivery across the wider portfolio.
• Be a key contributor to the growth strategy for Tier 1 accounts and lead testing across content formats, thumbnails, metadata, publishing schedules and emerging platform features to identify scalable best practice.
• Analyse each platform’s performance and channel-health data, turning insights into actionable recommendations that improve audience growth, content performance and revenue. Communicate results clearly to internal stakeholders and clients.
• Ensure all published content is fully rights-cleared, monetisable and compliant with platform copyright policies, community guidelines and music-licensing frameworks. Support the monitoring and protection of managed content to minimise rights and monetisation risks.
Skills and experience we'd like you to have 
• At least 5+ years of hands-on experience managing and growing large-scale video channels across platform within a major digital publisher, MCN or creator agency.
• Deep technical and strategic knowledge of YouTube Studio, Meta Business Suite and Snapchat’s CMS, including platform algorithms, monetisation products and audience-development tools.
• Ability to interpret data, identify meaningful trends and translate analytics into clear execution plans.
• An understanding of content licensing, digital rights management tools such as Content ID and Rights Manager, and intellectual-property protection on social platforms is preferred but not required.
• Previous experience managing a team / mentoring junior team members. At LADbible Group we've rolled out blended working which means the majority of departments across the business (including London, Manchester and International offices) work in the office 4 days per week.

As the leading social youth publisher, we have a powerful global platform to better represent our audience and enable those that do not have equal opportunities to have their voices heard. As a business, we are committed to building a diverse and inclusive workforce, in an environment where everyone feels comfortable to be themselves.

## Senior Design Manager / Design Manager (Extra High Voltage EHV)
### Grimsby West 400kV Substation | Great Grid Upgrade Programme
**Location:** Birmingham (with travel to Grimsby, designers and suppliers as required)
Help deliver one of the UK's most significant power infrastructure programmes
Laing O'Rourke is seeking an experienced **Senior Design Manager or Design Manager** to play a key role in the delivery of the **Grimsby West 400kV AIS Substation**, a critical element of National Grid's **Great Grid Upgrade Programme** and the wider **Grimsby to Walpole Network Connection (GWNC)** project.
This is an opportunity to influence the design and delivery of nationally significant electrical infrastructure from the earliest stages of development through to construction. You'll join the project during pricing before moving into an extensive Early Contractor Involvement phase, collaborating closely with National Grid, WSP and key supply chain partners to shape efficient, buildable and innovative solutions.

About the role
This role is for someone wanting to start a career in operations within a financial services firm. You'll join as a Graduate focused on working complaints and train to become a fully competent Complaints Officer, investigating and resolving our more complex customer interactions across loans, cards and auto-finance. A critical role to help the business understand how it can serve customers better.
This is a casework role. From early on you will hold your own caseload, speak to customers directly, make decisions on whether we got it right, and put things right where we didn't. You will be supported through structured training, coaching and quality feedback as you develop in the role
Some of the areas you'll delve into are:
- The regulatory framework for complaints: FCA regulation, the DISP rules, Consumer Duty, and how the guidance is applied to real cases.
- Investigation technique: gathering evidence, interrogating system records and call recordings, and testing what actually happened against what should have happened.
- Decision making and redress: reaching fair and objective outcomes, and calculating and explaining any compensation due.
- Customer communication: writing final response letters that break complex issues down into plain English.
- The Financial Ombudsman Service: how cases are referred, how FOS reaches its view, and how we apply those learnings to future cases.
- Root cause and feedback: spotting the product and process failures behind complaints and feeding them back to frontline and product teams.
Reporting to a Complaints Manager within the Operations Team, you will be responsible for a live caseload and for the quality of the decisions you make on it.
No prior complaints experience needed, we care about how you think, not what you already know. This role requires an ability to learn quickly, work to deadlines and support our customers effectively.
Your team's objectives
Lendable aims to resolve all complaints promptly, ensuring that they are investigated diligently and fairly for customers. We are committed to providing excellent customer service and to reaching the right outcomes for our customers.
Feedback is an important part of how we evolve as a business. The team is encouraged to speak up, take each complaint on its own merits and provide valuable insight back into the business so we can improve and grow.
Our ability to handle complaints effectively for our customers and therefore for us as a business has never been more important than now, as we expand our existing products in the UK and US financial markets.
What you'll be doing
- Investigating and resolving complaints about our loans, cards and auto-finance products, taking each case on its own merits
- Self-managing a varied and increasingly complex caseload: prioritising cases, choosing the best contact mechanism for each customer, and working efficiently enough to meet our KPI minimum standards
- Communicating with complainants in writing and by phone — managing expectations, handling difficult situations with tact and professionalism, and finding solutions to the issues raised
- Writing professional final response letters that set out our decision, our rationale and the customer's right to refer to the Financial Ombudsman Service
- Following our complaint handling standards and keeping clear records, making sure every decision is backed by demonstrable evidence and a documented rationale
- Working to resolve complaints without the customer needing to refer to FOS, and applying the learnings from both internal and FOS outcomes to future cases
- Feeding back to frontline and product teams on the product and process improvements your cases surface, across Operations and the wider Lendable business
- Keeping your knowledge of Lendable's products current through effective use and review of our policies, procedures and business tools
- Turning your hand to other areas of operational need as the business requires
What we're looking for
- Educated to degree level
- Exceptional written communication - you can structure an argument and explain a complex decision clearly to someone who is not an expert
- An aptitude for investigation, analysis, problem-solving and dispute resolution
- Strong organisation and self-management - you can hold a caseload, prioritise it and work to deadlines without being chased
- Sound judgment and a sound moral compass: willing to speak up to make sure good customer outcomes stay at the heart of what we do
- Resilience and adaptability in a fast-paced, changing environment
- A willingness to learn FCA regulation and the DISP complaint handling rules and guidance

We're not a corporation so we try our best to get things moving as quickly as possible. For this role we'd expect:
- A 15 minute cognitive assessment
- A quick phone call with one of the Talent team
- An onsite assessment centre with a role focus and a final stage interview with the Complaints Management team to discuss your fit and capability for the role.

The FPGA Academy is a 16‑week structured training and development programme designed for engineers with transferable technical skill sets (such as electronic engineering, embedded software, or systems engineering) who wish to transition into FPGA / Firmware Engineering.

• Post training deployment into established engineering teams

Your world of expertise
The Climate Monitoring and Attribution group (CMA) at the Met Office Hadley Centre is an internationally recognised group that specialises in working with observations to monitor and understand our climate.
We work closely with experts both within and outside of the Met Office, and with international agencies and initiatives, such as the World Meteorological Organisation (WMO), the European Space Agency and EUMETSAT, the European meteorological satellite agency, and we provide climate information to customers and end users, including the UK government and the public
We are recruiting into three different positions in CMA:
- Global Surface Temperature Climate Monitoring Scientist: This position sits within the ‘Observing Climate: Marine and Cross-Domain Analysis’ team. In this role, you will develop global observational data sets and use them to monitor and report on the Earth’s climate across land, ocean and ice, with a focus on temperature change at the Earth’s surface. You will use your data analysis skills to combine current and historical instrumental data to quantify observed changes, assess uncertainty in those changes, and put current observed climate into historical context. You will develop data sets that have a wide range of applications in climate science and that are relevant to informing international climate policy and agreements.
- Satellite Climate Observations Scientist: This position sits within the ‘Observing Climate: Land and Atmosphere’ team. The role is primarily focused on using satellite data for UK and global climate monitoring. This includes development of novel satellite-based climate indicators to characterise and track impactful climatic events, such as extreme heat, drought, vegetation stress and wildfires, and combining satellite and station data to produce new ‘blended’ datasets for key variables. This role provides the opportunity to contribute new satellite-based metrics to our https://climate.metoffice.cloud/, which is used internationally as a trusted source of global climate monitoring information.
- UK Climate Scientist: This position sits within The National Climate Information Centre (NCIC) team. We are looking for a scientist with strong data management and communication skills to work closely with the existing team developing the flagship climate data sets https://www.metoffice.gov.uk/research/climate/maps-and-data/data/haduk-grid/haduk-grid and https://www.metoffice.gov.uk/hadobs/hadcet/ and supplying UK climate information to a variety of users. We communicate our analysis through regular reports and media output, most notably the high-profile annual https://www.metoffice.gov.uk/research/climate/maps-and-data/about/state-of-climate report.
Through your work and through collaboration with experts both within and outside of the Met Office, you will utilise observational data to quantify climate change and variability by applying your analytical and scientific software skills. This role will include opportunities to apply cutting edge research such as ML approaches and new data gridding/mapping methods.
We welcome applications for all three roles from candidates with a range of scientific backgrounds. We are particularly interested in individuals who are motivated to apply their scientific and analytical skills to climate observations and climate monitoring, and who are enthusiastic about developing a career in this area.
Your key duties:
- Working with data from a variety of sources, including UK and global weather stations, satellites, ships and buoys to create new observational climate data sets and update existing data sets.
- Effectively conveying confidence in results through robust quantification of observational uncertainty and evaluation.
- Analysing new and existing observational data sets to characterise and monitor global, regional and UK climate change.
- Documenting and disseminating scientific findings via peer-reviewed papers, reports, webpages, press releases and through presentations at national/international meetings and conferences. Providing guidance to internal and external users of climate observation data.
- Working collaboratively within a team of scientists and scientific software engineers to deliver and communicate high-quality scientific output.

From science to technology, from meteorology to management, and from planning to communication, our expertise helps us stand out as the authority on weather accuracy and climate prediction. **Your world of expertise**
The Climate Monitoring and Attribution group (CMA) at the Met Office Hadley Centre is an internationally recognised group that specialises in working with observations to monitor and understand our climate.
We work closely with experts both within and outside of the Met Office, and with international agencies and initiatives, such as the World Meteorological Organisation (WMO), the European Space Agency and EUMETSAT, the European meteorological satellite agency, and we provide climate information to customers and end users, including the UK government and the public
We are recruiting into three different positions in CMA:
- **Global Surface Temperature Climate Monitoring Scientist:** This position sits within the ‘Observing Climate: Marine and Cross-Domain Analysis’ team. In this role, you will develop global observational data sets and use them to monitor and report on the Earth’s climate across land, ocean and ice, with a focus on temperature change at the Earth’s surface. You will use your data analysis skills to combine current and historical instrumental data to quantify observed changes, assess uncertainty in those changes, and put current observed climate into historical context. You will develop data sets that have a wide range of applications in climate science and that are relevant to informing international climate policy and agreements.
- **Satellite Climate Observations Scientist:** This position sits within the ‘Observing Climate: Land and Atmosphere’ team. The role is primarily focused on using satellite data for UK and global climate monitoring. This includes development of novel satellite-based climate indicators to characterise and track impactful climatic events, such as extreme heat, drought, vegetation stress and wildfires, and combining satellite and station data to produce new ‘blended’ datasets for key variables. This role provides the opportunity to contribute new satellite-based metrics to our [Met Office Climate Dashboard](https://climate.metoffice.cloud/), which is used internationally as a trusted source of global climate monitoring information.
- **UK Climate Scientist:** This position sits within The National Climate Information Centre (NCIC) team. We are looking for a scientist with strong data management and communication skills to work closely with the existing team developing the flagship climate data sets [HadUK-Grid](https://www.metoffice.gov.uk/research/climate/maps-and-data/data/haduk-grid/haduk-grid) and [HadCET](https://www.metoffice.gov.uk/hadobs/hadcet/) and supplying UK climate information to a variety of users. Through your work and through collaboration with experts both within and outside of the Met Office, you will utilise observational data to quantify climate change and variability by applying your analytical and scientific software skills. This role will include opportunities to apply cutting edge research such as ML approaches and new data gridding/mapping methods.

- Analysing new and existing observational data sets to characterise and monitor global, regional and UK climate change.

job_title: Interim Head of Marketing & Communications (14 month maternity cover)
job_description:

This is an expansive, hands-on leadership role that touches every area of the business and involves working directly with external clients and partners. The role will be a 14 month fixed term maternity cover. 
You will turn business priorities into practical delivery that supports customer engagement, commercial opportunities, and growth. You will bring broad marketing and communications experience, operational discipline and sound judgement, working across Sales, Commercial and the wider business to set priorities and get work delivered.
You are not expected to do everything yourself or be a specialist in every discipline. Success means knowing when to roll up your sleeves, what to delegate and where to bring in specialist expertise, balancing cost and capability as the business grows. As a trusted adviser to the CEO and senior leadership team, you will connect strategy with day-to-day delivery.
Because of the nature of this work:  • You will be required to travel to our Summertown, Oxford office regularly, ideally 1-2 times per week, attend client sites and attend events both in the UK and internationally.
• You will need to hold existing or be eligible for UK Security Checked Vetting (SC), details of which can be found on the Gov UK website. 
Key responsibilities:
Marketing strategy, planning and performance
• Deliver Mind Foundry’s marketing and communications strategy in support of company and commercial priorities.
• Translate business objectives into focused plans, campaigns, budgets and measurable outcomes.
• Establish clear priorities for the function and direct resources towards activity with the strongest strategic and commercial value.
• Monitor and report on campaign effectiveness, audience engagement, website performance, lead quality and contribution to commercial opportunities.
• Manage the marketing budget, external suppliers, and agency relationships, and maintain an effective operating rhythm for the function.
Brand, positioning and external communications
• Own Mind Foundry’s brand, positioning and messaging architecture.
• Ensure communications are clear, credible and appropriate for Defence and National Security customers, partners, investors, government, and prospective employees.
• Lead PR, media engagement, thought leadership, and product marketing.
• Maintain brand consistency across digital channels, presentations, events, partner materials, recruitment activity, and internal communications.
• Coordinate sensitive external comments, interviews and information requests, ensuring claims are evidenced, and customer or partner confidentiality is protected.
Content, digital channels and campaigns
• Lead high-quality content including website copy, case studies, partner marketing, thought leadership, and social content.
• Own the website as a strategic marketing, commercial and employer-brand channel.
• Develop integrated campaigns for priority capabilities, markets, partnerships, and events.
• Ensure customer stories, programme evidence, and operational proof points are used appropriately and with the necessary permissions.
Internal communications and organisational alignment
• Own Mind Foundry’s internal communications approach, working closely with People and Operations teams, so employees understand company priorities, decisions, progress and upcoming activity.
• Continue to drive clear communication rhythms across leadership updates, company meetings, Teams, email and internal content.
• Plan and run quarterly all-company onsites, coordinating agendas, workshops, and logistics, alongside summer and Christmas parties that bring the team together.
• Run regular employee surveys and feedback opportunities, translating insights into practical improvements, and communicating the actions taken.
• Partner with People on employer brand, recruitment marketing and onboarding communications.
ESG
• Oversee Mind Foundry’s ESG programme, ensuring commitments are planned, delivered, measured and communicated credibly.
• Maintain an achievable roadmap for environmental, social, and governance activity.
• Continue to drive credible ESG evidence for bids, customer engagement, investor materials and partnerships.
Team leadership and function development
• Lead and develop a blended team of permanent employees, interns, consultants, and agencies.
• Provide clear priorities, effective delegation, constructive feedback, and professional development.
• Assess capability and capacity needs as the business grows, and lead recruitment and resourcing decisions to build the most effective mix of permanent employees, contractors and specialist support within agreed budgets.
• Balance hands-on delivery with effective delegation, making clear decisions about priorities, ownership and where specialist expertise will have the greatest impact.
Core Experience
• Marketing and communications leadership experience in B2B technology, Defence and National Security, and/or Government.
• Broad, hands-on marketing experience spanning operations, events, brand, content, digital channels and integrated campaigns.
• A track record of turning business strategy into prioritised plans and measurable growth outcomes.
• Strong operational experience managing budgets, suppliers and cross-functional delivery, adapting priorities and resources as business needs evolve.
• Experience leading a small blended team and making effective hiring, delegation and specialist resourcing decisions.
• Excellent written and verbal communication, editorial judgement and stakeholder management, with confidence advising senior leaders and translating technical expertise into clear communications.
• Experience delivering internal communications and employee engagement, including company events, feedback, and employer-brand activity.
• Sound judgement in handling sensitive communications and producing credible, evidence-led messaging, including ESG-related content.

If our team and mission resonate with you, but you do not necessarily meet all of our requirements, we still encourage you to apply.
Why Mind Foundry?
At Mind Foundry, people have the opportunity to work on problems that are technically challenging, operationally important and genuinely meaningful. We are a close-knit, multidisciplinary team working on complex problems where advanced AI has the potential to make a meaningful difference in the real world. Our work sits at the intersection of research, engineering, product, customer need and operational impact, which means everyone can contribute beyond their job title.

Job Description
Description
We are a research-driven biopharmaceutical company. Our mission is built on the simple premise that if we “follow the science”, great medicines can make a significant impact to our world. And we believe that a research-driven enterprise dedicated to world-class science can succeed by inventing medicine and vaccine innovations that make a difference for patients across the globe.
We have an exciting opportunity for a new Associate Principal Scientist to join our Oncology health economic modeling team in the Health Economic and Decision Sciences group. The preferred location for this role is West Point, PA; although alternate locations may be considered, including Rahway, NJ; Boston, MA; the UK, and Switzerland. Hybrid and flexible work arrangements are possible, consistent with local office and country policies.
The Health Economic and Decision Sciences (HEDS) department is part of our Company’s Biostatistics and Research Decision Sciences (BARDS) organization. BARDS is responsible for strategic design and analysis to enable informed decision making in the discovery, development and delivery of our Company’s innovative products, and is a leader in quantitative scientific methodology and its application to enable the targeting, discovery, development, manufacturing, and marketing of drugs and vaccines for the benefit of patients and global public health. In collaboration with internal and external partners, the BARDS-HEDS department specifically provides strategic and technical leadership to enable patient access, measure and quantify the value of our Company’s products, inform internal and external decisions, and shape methodology and external health policy and practice. This position will focus on health economic modeling for oncology products.
Role
Under the direction of an HEDS Senior Director, the Associate Principal Scientist provides strategic development and use of industry-leading predictive and economic models to enhance our understanding of disease and to quantify and communicate the value of our oncology products to patients, providers, and payers.
• Serve as the BARDS HEDS lead for one or more Value and Implementation teams to develop health economic, disease, and predictive models to enable business insights for the product.
• Utilize discovery, real world evidence, clinical trial and published data, and publicly available information and tools to provide economic and integrated models to answer key questions in all phases of drug and vaccine development – Phase I through loss of data exclusivity.
• Advance the use of integrated quantitative approaches, focusing on economic, disease, and predictive modeling and simulation in partnership with other internal groups and external organizations.
• Development and maintenance of health quality global health economic models and tools in-house or in collaboration with external vendors to provide critical business insights and fully demonstrate the value of our company’s products.
• Support and training of HEDS models and tools to support country/regional team adaptations and communications with external stakeholders.
• Dissemination of health economic data via presentations at congresses and publications in scientific journals.
• Work closely with external collaborators (clinical/economic thought leaders, payer/HTA experts, alliance partners) and internal cross-functional teams to ensure that new methodologies, models and advanced analytics are fully utilized for our products.
• Maintain awareness of external data, modeling methodologies and IT tools to collaborate across relevant internal stakeholders to enhance our Company's capabilities in health economic modeling, simulation, and data visualization. • Ensure sharing of work product and relevant best practices across our Company's enterprise.
Education
• PhD (preferred) or Master’s degree, in Health Economics, Biostatistics, Health Services Research, Actuarial Sciences, Operations Research or a closely related quantitative field
Required Experience and Skills:
• Relevant work experience in health economics and outcomes research (HEOR) beyond PhD or Master’s degree
• Knowledge and experience in economic evaluation of oncology drugs and interventions
• Expertise and solid hands-on experience in the conceptualization, design, development and dissemination of health economic model approaches to enable internal and external decisions
• Track record of submissions to Health Technology Assessment bodies and research publications in conferences and peer-reviewed journals
• Strong interpersonal, organizational and communication skills with ability to interact with individuals from a variety of disciplines
• Understanding of the market access environment and challenges in the US and key international markets

About us
 
At National Grid, our commitment to a cleaner, greener energy future is powered by the dedication and ingenuity of our people. Join our team as a Product Management Lead and be a part of something bigger—where your unique skills and passions can make a real difference. Together, we are superpowered. 
 
National Grid is hiring a Product Management Lead on a permanent basis. This position is based in Warwick. This role operates under a hybrid working model. Hybrid work expectations are subject to business needs and company policy.  About the role  
As Product Management Lead, you'll create explicit ownership of product outcomes, value and lifecycle decisions across a federated operating model. This is a practice leadership role rather than a role managing an individual product: the postholder owns a single product management framework and a single discovery framework that every product line adopts, so that products run in different lines of business are managed, evidenced and assured to one consistent standard.What you'll do
 
Product management framework and taxonomy
 
Own and publish a single product management framework for our federated operating model: the lifecycle stages every product passes through, the decision gates at each stage, and the artefacts a team must produce to pass them. Review and reissue it annually.
Maintain the product taxonomy and the product portfolio and ownership map across every line of business, so that each product has a named owner, a defined boundary and a current lifecycle status.
Run a quarterly assurance review of product teams against the framework, publish the findings, and agree remediation actions with each Product Line Director.
 
Discovery framework and investment artefacts
 
Own a single discovery framework used by every product line, covering problem framing, user research, opportunity sizing and experimentation.
Define the artefact set discovery must produce before investment is approved — the financial case, the architectural impact and option assessment, the benefits profile, the dependency map and the capability requirements — and set the quality bar for each.
Review the evidence pack for every major product investment ahead of sanction and advise the Head of Product, in writing, whether it meets the bar and where the gaps are.
Assess capability requirements holistically across the organisation, so that the people, skills, platform and partner capacity implied by the portfolio are visible as one picture, and flag where lines of business are competing for the same scarce capability.
 
Value, performance and lifecycle decisions
 
Publish product scorecards each quarter covering adoption, cost to serve, user satisfaction and benefit realisation against the approved case.
Chair the quarterly value review and recommend continue, change or retire decisions for products that are not delivering their intended outcomes.
 
Capability, career pathway and hiring
 
Own the product management career pathway and capability framework, including role profiles, capability levels and the assessment criteria used at interview.
Act as hiring standard-setter for product roles: assure interview panels and agree the assessment approach with HR and Talent Acquisition.
Run the product management community of practice across the federated lines of business, including onboarding for new product managers and a continuing development curriculum.
 
Tooling
 
Own the product tooling landscape covering roadmapping, discovery, user insight and value tracking, including selection, licensing, cost and adoption, and retire duplicated tooling.
 
Leadership and collaboration
 
Line manage the product practice team, setting objectives, managing performance and developing capability.
Partner with the Solution Architecture, Engineering Enablement and Delivery Orchestration Leads so that product, design, engineering and delivery standards form one coherent operating model.
Deputise for the Head of Product on product matters as required.
About you  
Extensive product management experience in a complex, technology-enabled organisation, with a clear and defensible view of what good product practice looks like and why.
Proven track record of defining and embedding product management standards, frameworks and taxonomies across multiple teams, rather than running a single product.
Experience of defining hiring standards and capability frameworks for product roles, including career pathways and structured assessment.
Deep practical knowledge of discovery and product research methods, and the ability to codify them into a framework teams will actually use.
Experience of selecting, governing and driving adoption of product tooling across an organisation.
Experience of assuring practice standards and measuring maturity, with the judgement to know when to enforce and when to coach.
A good understanding of financial management, benefits management and realisation linked to business results.
A good understanding of current and emerging product methods, agile methodologies and trends.
Ability to successfully operate at a senior manager level, forming strong relationships and engagement as needed across all levels of the Business Entity.
Experience of working within a heavily matrixed organisation, with the ability to drive for results through influence.

- **Glasgow**

- Excellent communication and influencing skills, with the confidence to engage effectively with a wide range of customers and colleagues

job_title: Golang Technical Lead (Perm, UK, Remote + Travel)
job_description:
This is a permanent, full-time remote opportunity open to candidates based in the UK. While the role is primarily remote, occasional travel to client sites across the UK may be required to attend meetings, workshops and other project-related activities.
About Nearform
Nearform is an independent team of data & AI experts, engineers, and designers who build intelligent digital solutions and capability at pace. We create AI-enabled solutions that enhance digital experiences, empower developers, and deliver measurable results. In these ways, we partner with ambitious enterprises to deliver enduring impact.
Our deep expertise in solving the world’s most complex digital problems, along with our collaborative, people-first approach, enables enterprises to build breakthrough products and modernise legacy systems by unleashing the power of AI.
Today, our team of 500 experts in 20+ countries is trusted by leading enterprises including Lululemon, Puma, Sun Life, Starbucks, Travelex, Virgin Media 02, and Walmart.  
As part of our Engineering function, you will work closely with clients to translate complex business requirements into innovative digital products. 
Whether you are a Senior Engineer, Tech Lead, or DevOps Engineer, you will collaborate with distributed teams, leveraging cutting-edge technologies to build secure, high-performance applications. Our Nearform engineers are known for building high quality, scalable solutions that solve real world problems.
 
About the Technical Lead Role:
As a Technical Lead at Nearform, you will be responsible for leading and guiding development teams while working directly with clients to translate business and technical requirements into impactful applications. However, as you’ll likely work on a variety of projects in your time here, your responsibilities may also include:
• Provide technical and line-management leadership to your development team.
• Take responsibility for the successful delivery of projects.
• Identify and resolve blockers before they become issues.
• Ensure best practices in software development, DevOps, and agile methodologies are upheld within the team.
• Work directly with clients, translating requirements into technical briefs.
• Shape and define architectural decisions ensuring scalability, security, and maintainability.
• Provide updates to client and Nearform leadership to ensure clear understanding of project status and drive good decision-making.
What we are looking for in this person:
• Significant experience in software engineering as either a Senior Engineer leading projects and mentoring or as a Technical Lead. For this particular role, you will ideally be using Golang, experience with additional other languages such as JavaScript or Python would be desirable. 
• Experience working directly with clients or customers to understand technical requirements.
• Experience leading software engineering teams through technical delivery and either direct line management or mentoring.
• Deep understanding of agile ways of working, best practices and design patterns.
• Deep understanding of test-driven development and testing best practices.
• Deep understanding of version control tools, e.g. Git.
• Understanding of DevOps practices and cloud technologies (AWS, Azure, GCP)
• Understanding of operational concerns (such as monitoring, performance testing, security considerations, accessibility, GDPR)
• Empathy and people skills
• Financial services industry experience 
Benefits and Perks we offer at Nearform
• Annual Company Bonus - We all help Nearform to hit company goals so we all receive a share of the profits on an annual basis in line with company performance. 
• Work Remotely and Flexibly - We have a genuine dedication to work/life balance. Our flexible working culture allows you to work around what matters - school run, no problem! 
• Paid Time Off Package - We offer an annual leave of 25 days plus public holidays. We also offer sick leave, marriage leave and many more.
• Remote Working Allowance - Every 2 years, you will have a budget of up to €1250 (equivalent in GBP) to help you set up a comfortable and productive workspace in addition to your essential equipment provided by Nearform when you join.
• Training and Development Allowance - Nearform is committed to supporting and investing in employees’ ongoing learning and professional development. You will be encouraged to pursue relevant learning opportunities that support your growth and the growth of others, subject to manager approval.
• Healthcare - It’s important to always take care of your health, so we offer additional private healthcare here at Nearform. If you wish to learn more about the plan offered feel free to reach out to our team.
• Pension & Insurances - We offer a pension match of up to 5% and Income Protection and Death in Service for peace of mind.
 
Our Interview Process
Talent Call (30 mins via Zoom)
An initial conversation with a member of our Talent Team to explore your background, leadership experience, and career goals. We’ll provide an overview of Nearform, discuss potential alignment, and answer any questions you may have. This step helps us assess initial alignment.
Technical Lead Assessment (90 mins, Zoom)
A structured assessment led by a senior Technical Lead or Head of Engineering, designed to evaluate key aspects of a Technical Lead role. This session includes a selection of tasks to cover:
Architecture Design – We want to see how you approach a high level problem, demonstrating your design thinking and decision-making process.
Technical Implementation – How do you turn a design into reality, taking into account business needs?
Code Standards and Feedback – We want to see not just your own skills, but also how you improve those around you
Hiring Manager Interview (45 mins via Zoom)
A conversation with a Hiring Manager focused on your approach to teamwork, client collaboration, and problem-solving in an enterprise development setting. We'll also share more details about Nearform and the potential projects you may join.
There may also be an additional interview with the client depending on the project. 
 
Ready to Join Us?
If you're passionate about building high-quality applications, solving complex challenges, and driving innovation in enterprise development, we’d love to hear from you.
Apply now via our careers page at Nearform and be part of a team that values technical excellence, collaboration, and continuous learning.
Nearform is committed to shaping a better world in all that we do. Our global team is built based on respect, inclusivity, diversity and excellence. 
If you require any adjustments to the interview process as part of your application, please let someone from our Talent Team know so they can help.

job_description:
Finance Graduate Programme: Commercial Finance & FP&A
London | Competitive starting salary + progression | Fully funded CIMA | Starting January 2027.
The Super Bowl. Wimbledon. The Premier League. Eurovision. The Olympic Games.
Behind the moments the world watches, there's a team making them happen. Behind that team, there's a finance function keeping it all moving.
NEP is the global partner behind some of the biggest live events on the planet. We work in 25 countries, have more than 5,000 people, and have supported productions in over 100 countries across all seven continents. As we celebrate 40 years of bringing content to life, we're launching a programme to find the finance leaders of the future.
Is that you?
What you'll do
Over 3 years, you'll complete two 18-month rotations, one in Group Commercial Finance & FP&A and one in NEP Europe Finance. This is real work from day one, not shadowing. You'll:
- See how a global business performs: help prepare month-end reporting across regions for Group leadership
- Find the story behind the numbers: analyse results against budget and forecast, and explain what's driving them
- Help shape what comes next: support budgeting, forecasting and revenue models
- Track risks and opportunities: maintain the Group view of what could help or hurt performance
- Work as a business partner: build relationships with finance teams and stakeholders across our international businesses
- Make things better: suggest ways to improve our reporting, processes and tools
What you'll get
- A fully funded CIMA qualification, covering tuition, materials, registration, subscriptions and exam fees
- 2 days' paid study leave for every exam, on top of your annual leave
- International experience across Group and European finance teams
- A structured development plan, with quarterly check-ins and reviews at the end of each rotation
- Access to senior leaders, with regular exposure to an experienced senior management team
- A permanent role from day one, with a clear path into a qualified finance role when you finish the programme
- Competitive starting salary, with progression as you develop
Who we're looking for
You don't need to know everything about finance yet. You do need to be curious about how businesses make money and want to find out more. We're looking for people who are:
- Good with numbers and analytical, and like solving problems
- Strong communicators, confident to ask questions and share ideas
- Adaptable and resilient, comfortable in a fast-paced, changing environment
- Team players who are happy to roll up their sleeves when it counts
- Ambitious, with the drive to grow into a future finance manager or leader
Why NEP?
Our values are Reliable, Ethical, Innovative and One Team. They shape how we work with each other and with our clients. When something needs to happen, everyone pitches in.
Ready to start your finance career where the world's biggest moments happen?
Applications close on 15 November 2026, although we reserve the right to close the advert early if we receive sufficient applications. Face-to-face interviews will be held in NEP's London office w/c 16 + 23 November 2026. Preferred start date is 12 January 2027, although we’re happy to be flexible for the right candidate.
NEP is committed to diversity, equity and inclusion. We welcome applications from all backgrounds and are happy to make adjustments throughout the recruitment process. This advert is not an exhaustive of the role and opportunity and is subject to change at the needs of the business.

This role operates in a fast-paced, high-volume, 24/7 service environment, supporting both routine and emergency service requests. The position requires strong organizational skills, adaptability, sound judgment, and the ability to independently manage competing priorities while collaborating closely with team members.
Service Coordinators must be dependable, self-motivated, and comfortable working during shifts when direct leadership support may be limited.
This position requires a reliable internet connection and a dedicated workspace in a quiet environment suitable for focused work.

• Receive, review, and prioritize incoming service requests based on customer requirements, service level agreements (SLAs), and urgency.
• Source qualified field technicians and vendors based on technical requirements, availability, location, and cost considerations.

• Maintain proactive, professional communication with customers, technicians, vendors, and internal teams.
• Provide timely updates regarding service schedules, progress, delays, and completion.
• Collaborate with fellow coordinators to balance workloads, share responsibilities, and maintain service continuity.
• Ensure clear communication and accurate handoffs of outstanding work between shifts.

Location: Manchester area (Cheadle)
Reports to: Senior Engineer Leader, Technical Product Dev. (R&D)
Contract type: Permanent
Your Role & Team in a Nutshell
As a Product Engineer, you will turn new small household appliance ideas into products that are ready for launch under the Breville brand as well as other global brands in other countries. You'll lead the engineering side of new product development projects, making sure products meet expectations for performance, quality and cost. Working closely with colleagues across Programme Management, Marketing, Industrial Design, Manufacturing, Quality, Regulatory and Supply Chain, you'll solve technical challenges and help bring innovative products to market. You'll take ownership of your work, use the latest engineering and AI-enabled tools, and play an important role in delivering successful launches. You will be part of the R&D team of seven and work in a hybrid working model.
We will help you achieve your goals and develop by providing regular feedback and access to online training courses.
Your Key Responsibilities:
• Develop innovative products that meet customer needs, financial goals, and industry and regulatory requirements. Translate customer insights and product use feedback into clear technical specifications.
• Lead multiple new product development (NPD) projects through Newell's Stage-Gate process. Define engineering timelines, achieve key milestones, and deliver products on time, within budget, and to the required quality standards.
• Create engineering product specifications and lead the development of Design Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (DFMEA) documentation, Design Verification Plans and Reports (DVP&R), and quality specifications.
• Develop test plans and work with internal and external laboratories to validate designs against requirements. Review manufacturing trial results, test data, and Production Part Approval Process (PPAP) documentation, and lead design, tooling, or process improvements based on findings.
• Prepare and review Engineering Change Notices (ENCs). Lead design and technical reviews, and review CAD design models and drawings with cross-functional teams.
• Create basic CAD design models, using AI-assisted design tools where appropriate, to develop early prototypes and quickly evaluate new ideas.
• Conduct intellectual property (IP) searches and work with legal teams on IP clearance and patent applications.
• Analyse competitor products and identify opportunities for innovation, product improvement, and cost reduction.
• Work closely with teams across the business to assess product safety, manufacturability, and reliability. Drive product and process improvements, from small enhancements to large-scale cost-saving initiatives.
• Investigate product complaints and provide technical support to resolve issues. Apply knowledge of materials and manufacturing processes, including injection moulding, to support product design and material selection.
What You’ll Need
Minimum:
• Bachelor’s degree in Electrical, Mechanical, Plastics, Mechatronics Engineering, or a related engineering discipline.
• Demonstrated experience in a product development, manufacturing, or engineering environment.
• Practical experience with prototyping, design validation, testing, and engineering problem-solving.
• Working knowledge of 3D CAD software, preferably SolidWorks or Creo, including the ability to review 3D models and 2D engineering drawings.
• Strong project management and organisational skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and support projects through a structured stage-gate development process.
Your advantage:
• Strong understanding of, or the ability to quickly learn, manufacturing processes used in small household appliances.
• Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the confidence to collaborate across functions and influence stakeholders.
• Experience developing consumer products and bringing new products from concept through to launch.
• Familiarity with electro-mechanical products and technologies.
• Exposure to AI-assisted or generative design, simulation, prototyping tools, or using AI-generated code to support concept development and testing.
What You Gain
Newell Brands has a strong footprint in the EMEA region, with several thousand employees spread over many corporate offices and manufacturing facilities. You might recognise some of our iconic brands, like Parker, Sistema, Spontex, Crockpot, NUK, Coleman, and Yankee Candle, to name a few.
Join us and benefit from:
• Flexible hybrid working system (on average 3 days in the office and 2 days at home p.w.)
• Unlimited access to LinkedIn Learning – 17,000+ courses for your professional and personal development
• Bravo – our global recognition programme where teammates can recognise each other and exceptional work is rewarded
• Employee Referral Program – an opportunity to get a bonus
• Global Employee Assistance Program – confidential support for you and your family, complementing our commitment to your well-being at work and beyond
• Corporate Citizenship Philosophies – environmentally sustainable and socially sensitive business practices
• Give@Newell – paid time-off for charity activities dedicated for local communities right where you live/work
• Access to Employee Resource Groups that foster an inclusive culture
• Core Values: Integrity, Teamwork, Passion for Winning, Ownership, Leadership

The Design Studio brings NewGen’s ideas to life, building strong creative concepts, campaign visuals and design systems across social, digital, print and real-world activations.
We work closely with Creative, Strategy, Accounts and Production to take work from the first idea through to the final asset, often at pace and across multiple formats and markets. From Pepsi and Samsung to 7UP and Marriott Bonvoy, we make sure the work is original, beautifully crafted and unmistakably on brand.
The Role
We’re looking for a talented Senior Designer to join our growing Design Studio on a 12-month maternity cover contract.
You’ll lead the creative thinking and hands-on design behind high-impact, social-first campaigns, taking ideas from early concepts through to polished, multi-format delivery. You’ll be a trusted senior design contact throughout the cover period, helping maintain creative quality, project ownership and a confident, collaborative studio environment.
Creative Thinking & Direction
Develop bold, culturally relevant ideas, visual concepts and creative routes, bringing fresh references and design thinking into briefs from the outset.
Shape and confidently communicate creative direction, presenting a clear design rationale and constructively challenging briefs or feedback when the work can be stronger.

Work closely with Creative, Strategy, Accounts and Production partners, bringing motion and channel requirements into the process early.
Manage deadlines and expectations proactively, flagging risks or resourcing pressures early while balancing creative ambition with delivery needs.
Studio Support & Development
Act as a reliable senior design point of contact during the maternity cover, making sound day-to-day creative decisions and giving constructive feedback.
Share relevant trends, creative inspiration and new design, motion or AI techniques that raise the quality and ambition of the studio’s work.

Become embedded in the team, clients and ways of working, building trusted relationships across Creative, Strategy, Accounts and Production.
Independently take briefs from concept to delivery and contribute strong creative work from the outset.
First 6 Months
Confidently own complex, multi-format projects, present creative rationale, manage feedback and keep work on track.
Become a dependable senior design contact who protects creative quality while finding smarter ways of working.
First 12 Months
Consistently deliver strong creative work and reliable project leadership throughout the cover period.
Help maintain high studio standards and provide a clear, organised handover of live work, key files and decisions.

ILIOS Overview
ILIOS is the Construction Partner for the UK’s STEP (Spherical Tokamak for Energy Production) fusion programme, the UK’s world‑leading programme to design and build a prototype fusion energy power plant at West Burton in Nottinghamshire.
ILIOS is a consortium led by a joint venture between Kier and Nuvia, supported by AECOM, AL_A and Turner & Townsend, bringing together extensive experience across major national infrastructure, nuclear and safety‑critical engineering, complex site transformation, programme and cost management, and world‑class design.
Working as part of the public–private sector integrated team led by UK Fusion Energy (UKFE), a wholly owned subsidiary of the UK Atomic Energy Authority (UKAEA), ILIOS is embedded in the programme as STEP transitions from planning into delivery.
The consortium supports the design and construction of buildings, infrastructure and facilities across the STEP site, alongside constructability, programme planning, site management, supply‑chain engagement and project controls, helping to ensure delivery is safe, buildable and fully integrated with the wider programme.
The appointment of ILIOS marks a significant milestone in the UK’s transition to clean energy and supports STEP’s mission to demonstrate fusion energy and develop a world‑leading fusion supply chain, creating long‑term economic and skills opportunities for the UK.

Odin is building the investment infrastructure for the future of private markets.
We believe capital is one of the most powerful tools for shaping the world - and more people should know how to put it to work. Our mission is to make it radically easier to raise and deploy capital, so that anyone, anywhere, can back the companies and ideas they believe in.
Our first product is a full-stack platform for launching and running private investment firms, allowing you to run everything from your phone - think Shopify for VC and PE. We handle all the infrastructure: from legal structuring and investor onboarding to KYC/AML, payments, tax, reporting, and exits.
We're already trusted by over 10,000 angels, VCs, and founders. We administer over $750m in assets, covering investments from pre-seed to series E. This includes household names like ElevenLabs, OpenAI, SpaceX, xAI, Anduril, etc. but also new companies creating everything from synthetic brains to small nuclear reactors.
 
Why we're hiring
- We are automating a decades old part of the financial services industry. AI pilled builders like you are the beating heart of this plan, because LLMs & agents allow us to turn this services business entirely into software.
- This is a product role, and your product is how Odin operates. Think of it as our ghostbuster: every operational problem lands with you, you decide what gets fixed, and you ship most of the fixes yourself rather than writing tickets for someone else.
- We're post-PMF, fast-growing, and rolling out new products (fund admin) & geographies (USA). Customer & deal volume is climbing fast.
- Today we're on track for roughly 700 deals a year, with a team of ~20, and we'll process $500m-$750m of investment in 2026 alone.
- The next goal is 7,000 deals a year and billions in annual investment flows.
- We believe this can be achieved with a team of around 50 people. But it will only be possible if we turn human-driven services workflows into software.
- Odin's operations run on around 50 processes, some code and some people, and plenty still held together by spreadsheets. Your job is to take each one apart, question why it exists, then rebuild it or kill it.
- The simplest way to think about it: the numerator is how many deals we close, the denominator is what each deal costs us to run. You'll focus on the denominator, and the right person won't be able to stop themselves thinking about the numerator too.
- We expect the right hire to be spending more time in Claude Code than in Excel, email or anything else.
 
What you'll own
- Triage: Every operational problem comes to you before it reaches product and engineering. For each one you decide: scope it so precisely that engineering knows exactly what to build, or build it yourself.
- Cost per deal: There will be big early wins where a whole process can be ripped out and replaced. After that, doubling ops efficiency comes from 150 small changes, and you'll be the one making them.
- Automation: You'll sit with the deal operations team, learn each workflow end to end, then build what replaces it. Most of what you ship you'll build without engineering. What does go to them arrives simple, scoped and usually with a working prototype attached.
- Deleting things and saying no: You decide what belongs in our processes and what doesn't. If a request from sales doesn't scale and isn't highly profitable we don't do it. If a way of working exists for no good reason, you kill it.
- The ops team: You'll lead the core deal operations team, deciding where their time goes while you rebuild the work around them.
 
What we're looking for
- You build, not buy: Clear evidence, at work or in your own time, that you've built real solutions with AI with no budget and no engineers. Buying a tool or setting up workflows in Sheets doesn't count. We want to see what you've shipped in Claude Code or similar.
- Founder or product DNA: You've founded something, been early on a founding team, or worked as a product manager. That usually means four or more years of experience and a track record of finishing what you start.
- Systems thinker: You look at any process the way a good product manager looks at a product: What's the job? Why are we doing this at all? What's the smallest, simplest system that achieves the goal? You think about the whole business, not just your corner of it.
A lot of what happens in fund admin is inherited convention, an industry "given", or a constraint of some third party. You should find it physically difficult to accept any of that.
- In the details and extremely on top of things: You understand every single aspect of our systems end to end. You close loops, you chase, you push hard to get things done.
- Numerate: Comfortable with financial mechanics, strong mental arithmetic. You'll be automating a lot of numerical work - carry, allocations, fee calculations, distributions, and the edge cases that make all of them interesting.
- Big plus: regulated financial services background: Fund administration, custody, payments, brokerage, audit, tax or another back office function. Useful, but not required. We care much more about the traits you have and the things you can build than specific skills or experience on your CV.
 
How we work
There are five things we care about deeply:
1. Reason from the ground up
Seek to understand what is true by always asking why. Do not trust convention or experts.
2. Speed begets speed
We work fast. Speed compounds, it's the best form of defensibility, and it's energising to be around. If you work slowly, or tolerate slow work around you, you do not belong at Odin.
3. Take ownership
Do not wait for permission to do things. Find the answer, force the thing into existence and hold others to an extremely high standard - the same standard you hold yourself to.
4. Brutal honesty
If work doesn't meet the bar, people need to hear it, and the right people want to.
5. Truly excellent customer service
Be a stickler for detail in every single interaction a customer has with us, and always strive to make this experience better, smoother, faster.
 
This role is probably not for you if
- You'd rather write specs and hand tickets to engineers than build the thing yourself;
- You prefer close management of your responsibilities;
- You are risk-averse;
- You want a 9-5;
- You take yourself too seriously;
- You care about working for a company that's raised lots of money rather than one that's extremely capital efficient and focused on building a profitable giant that has a positive economic impact
 
Salary
£90k - £120k base, plus a meaningful equity grant. We're flexible on the mix of cash and equity.
 
Hiring process

course corrections

engineers, teams, and vendors so blockers are resolved quickly and together
* Triage bugs and production issues with attention to detail, minimizing
disruption to the customers who rely on our platform

and team documentation

ramp-up time and onboarding errors

limits, and escalate unresolved or higher-impact issues to senior engineering
leadership in a timely way

testing, documentation, and debugging across the team
* Uphold secure, ethical, and resilient engineering practices, including data
and information security expectations, across everything the team ships

managing or formally leading a software engineering team
* Working familiarity with our core stack (Ruby on Rails, React, AWS,
PostgreSQL) and with API management, cloud computing, DevOps practices, and
software design, with enough technical acumen to guide discussions and
evaluate trade-offs
* Proven track record of running a team's daily delivery reliably: consistent
adherence to coding and QA standards, accurate and timely task completion,
and dependable schedules
* Strong problem-solving skills, with a habit of identifying challenges early,
evaluating options, and driving practical resolutions
* Exceptional collaboration and communication, equally effective with
engineers, non-technical stakeholders, and external vendors

ramp-up times and growing team capability
* Sound judgment about when to resolve issues locally and when to escalate, and
a record of escalating clearly and promptly

Also known in the market as: Innovation Engineering Manager; R&D Engineering Manager; Engineering Manager, Applied Research; Prototyping Engineering Manager.
About the Role
Pearson Labs is the applied R&D function within the Office of the CTO. We explore, experiment with and prototype emerging technologies that could transform how people learn, are assessed and work. Our portfolio spans areas including AI tutoring, agentic systems, immersive environments, knowledge graphs, voice agents and novel hardware.

You will bring professionalism to ambiguity while protecting the curiosity, energy and enjoyment that make an innovation lab effective.

• Lead the day-to-day operation of the Labs engineering team and allocate work across a changing research portfolio.

• Establish practical standards for prototyping, documentation, experimentation, evidence quality and demo readiness.
• Help teams frame hypotheses, define measurable objectives and reach explicit scale, pivot or stop decisions.
• Maintain an accurate view of portfolio health and communicate progress, risks and recommendations clearly.
• Coordinate customer sessions, showcases and executive demonstrations so the story travels as well as the work.
• Stay alert to emerging technology, changing business priorities and opportunities for Pearson Labs to explore next.
