Patient-Centered Research, In-trial qualitative research Evidera’s Patient-Centered Research (PCR) group combines a unique portfolio of scientific disciplines, including health sciences, psychometrics, epidemiology, psychology, and many other social sciences. Our PCR staff conduct a variety of studies using quantitative and qualitative approaches to develop clinical outcomes assessments, evaluate patient preferences and utilities, execute various implementation science studies, conduct Delphi panels and do secondary data analysis using advanced statistical techniques.
Within the PCR group, the ITR team conduct qualitative (interviews) studies and/or surveys in the context of a clinical trial to obtain feedback from clinical trial participants (patient, caregiver, investigator or study staff) on various topics i.e., understanding patients’ experience with their condition, its impacts on their lives, exploring treatment benefit, describing trial participant experiences and identifying aspects of burden from their participation. ITR can be implemented using an embedded design (e.g., ITR is defined as clinical trial activity in the clinical trial study protocol and ICF) or associated design (ITR is covered under separate protocol, separate ICF, and IRB/EC approval, with separate site recruitment and contracting). ITR can be conducted at any trial phase and at any time in the trial (screening, mid-trial, exit). Over the past few years, there has been a growing interest in ITR studies by regulators to support relevance and interpretation of trial outcomes, meaningful change and/or meaningful treatment benefit.

We are looking for a Head of Data Domain Products who is strategic, collaborative and business-focused to join our Patient Evidence Digital Transformation organization. This position can be based in our Atlanta, Georgia, Raleigh, North Carolina, or Boston, Massachusetts offices. This hybrid role is limited to 10% domestic/ international travel.
About the role
UCB is building a permanent enterprise data capability to improve how data is understood, connected and applied to critical business decisions, helping accelerate the development of medicines through trusted, reusable and interoperable data products which will support the development of AI.
As Head of Data Domain Products, you will build and lead the enterprise portfolio of strategic data domains and a team of seven Data Domain Product Leads. Your team is comprised of individuals with deep expertise in both data and the business questions to be answered in the clinical pathway. For example, an expert on patient data – real world data, clinical data, biomarker data – how it comes together to answer strategic questions on how to develop assets – like feasibility and recruitment. You will have experts on public data and disease landscape.
You will set strategic direction, establish consistent ways of working and guide priorities, investments, dependencies and trade-offs across the portfolio. Working across business, data and technology, you will ensure domain data products connect business meaning with trusted data and are governed, reusable and capable of supporting business processes, analytics and AI-enabled use cases.
At the heart of the role is a clear objective: aligned domain leadership, reusable enterprise data products and measurable value at scale.
Who you’ll work with
You will lead seven Data Domain Product Leads and partner closely with Patient Evidence leadership, Data Strategy & Architecture, the Data Office, business process owners, domain subject matter experts, Digital Technology, Enterprise Architecture and business and functional leaders.
You will also work closely with Data Portfolio Leads. Domain Product Leads identify, understand and connect data across UCB, while Portfolio Leads draw from multiple domains to address recurring business questions.
What you’ll do
Lead, coach and develop seven Data Domain Product Leads.
Set strategic direction for the enterprise data domain portfolio.
Align domain strategies, roadmaps and investments with business priorities.
Establish consistent product management and ways of working across domains.
Lead prioritization of dependencies, investments, risks and trade-offs.
Drive adoption, reuse and measurable value from domain data products.
Resolve cross-domain ownership gaps, duplication and strategic issues.
Ensure alignment with data governance, privacy and compliance requirements.
Drive consistency with enterprise semantic and architecture standards.
Enable interoperability across domains, processes and business use cases.
Strengthen collaboration between Domain Product Leads and Portfolio Leads.
Ensure data products support priority analytics, automation and AI use cases.
Communicate portfolio progress, risks, investment needs and outcomes to leadership.
Interested? For this role, we’re looking for the following education, experience and skills:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor’s degree in Business, Data, Analytics, Life Sciences, Information Management, Technology or a related field.
10+ years of relevant experience in data expertise and the appilcation of that data to business questions, data strategy, product management, busines data management or enterprise transformation.
Pharmaceutical industry experience with strong knowledge of data supporting the development and lifecycle of pharmaceutical assets.
Experience leading enterprise data from a business perspective (not IT or data office), strategic data domains or comparable capabilities.
Demonstrated experience leading and developing senior product, data or business professionals.
Proven accountability for a portfolio of products, capabilities or strategic domains.
Experience translating enterprise strategy into coordinated roadmaps, investments and measurable outcomes.
Strong understanding of data governance, data quality, metadata, semantic models and interoperability.
Experience enabling analytics, automation or AI through trusted enterprise data.
Experience navigating complex cross-functional priorities and trade-offs.
Strong leadership, coaching, stakeholder management and influencing skills.
Preferred Qualifications
Advanced degree in Business, Data, Analytics, Life Sciences, Information Management, Technology or a related field.
Experience working with data to answer business questions across multiple stages of the pharmaceutical asset-development lifecycle.
Experience establishing or scaling enterprise data operating models.
Experience connecting business context, data relationships and semantic standards.
Experience supporting advanced analytics, automation or AI-enabled transformation.

LIFE AT UIPATH
The people at UiPath believe in the transformative power of automation to change how the world works. We’re committed to creating category-leading enterprise software that unleashes that power.
To make that happen, we need people who are curious, self-propelled, generous, and genuine. People who love being part of a fast-moving, fast-thinking growth company. And people who care—about each other, about UiPath, and about our larger purpose.
Could that be you?
YOUR MISSION
As a Partner Sales Executive focused on Financial Crime Compliance (FCC), you'll navigate partner ecosystems, building strong executive relationships, trust, and new revenue streams through value-based selling. You'll grow revenue and drive adoption of the UiPath platform for FCC use cases — such as anti-money laundering, KYC, and fraud — by partnering with world-class consulting and service organizations, and build the plans that help those partners deliver maximum success for their financial services customers.
This is a unique overlay role: you'll drive partner sales for FCC across the entire company, and no two days will look the same. You'll build offerings and go-to-market strategies — and see them through to execution — with sophisticated, non-transactional partners such as global systems integrators and advisory firms.
WHAT YOU'LL DO AT UIPATH
- Analyze market potential and build strategic go-to-market plans with partners to maximize revenue
- Hit agreed sales targets and outcomes each quarter, growing partner-sourced revenue, registered deals, and joint solutions
- Evangelize the UiPath brand and value proposition so UiPath becomes the automation platform of choice for your partners' customers
- Show partners how our solutions benefit their customers financially and support their strategic initiatives
- Build trusted relationships with partner automation practices, account owners, vertical leaders, and executives
- Work with regional sales leadership and partner leadership on a coordinated go-to-market strategy for high-value solutions
- Coach UiPath sales reps on working with your partner, managing joint pursuits and keeping communication tight
- Respond quickly to partner leads, agree deal-support priorities, and nurture opportunities into expansion
- Drive ongoing partner enablement: training and certification, product updates, quotes, and new release information
- Team up with field sales, Customer Success Managers, and pre-sales to make sure customers get maximum value and issues are resolved fast
- Track competitors, new products, and market conditions, and report partner needs, competitive activity, and new opportunities to leadership
- Keep the UiPath CRM accurate and up to date
WHAT YOU'LL BRING TO THE TEAM
- 10+ years of business and sales experience, including developing sales with partners and building offerings and go-to-market strategies with sophisticated partners (consulting backgrounds welcome)
- 2–3 years of industry experience in financial crime compliance, either at a bank or with a vendor in the FCC space (vendor experience is a strong plus)
- The credibility to hold solid, in-depth conversations on financial crime topics with partners, customers, and compliance leaders
- Solid knowledge of the automation and AI landscape, and the ability to explain UiPath's key differentiators and customer benefits
- A track record of building multiple senior-level relationships across a partner ecosystem, including the leaders who shape go-to-market strategy and own key client relationships
- Experience building account plans that meet sales and profit goals, and taking full ownership of partners across assigned verticals or geographies
- An agile, confident problem solver who is organizationally savvy and disciplined in execution
- A proactive self-starter with superlative collaboration and communication skills
- The ability to handle conflict constructively and balance the interests of the partner, the customer, and UiPath to reach the best outcome
- Experience working in a CRM (such as Salesforce)

Organizational Summary
Contraceptive care is basic healthcare. Yet too many patients in the U.S. struggle to access the care they need, when they need it. Founded in 2014, Upstream USA is a national, nonpartisan nonprofit dedicated to ensuring that equitable, patient-centered contraceptive care is available to everyone.
Our Mission and Impact
Upstream works to ensure individuals can make fully informed, autonomous decisions about the contraceptive methods that are best for them. We are currently the largest contraceptive organization in the country improving contraceptive care in primary care settings, operating in 37 states and Washington, D.C.
While our foundational work focuses on partnering with healthcare organizations offering primary care, such as federally qualified healthcare centers (FQHC) and health systems, we are always evolving. We are actively pursuing additional, innovative paths to ensure every patient has streamlined access to the contraceptive service of their choice, where and when it is most convenient for them.
A Different Kind of Nonprofit
Upstream is a venture philanthropy-backed nonprofit with a current annual budget of $50M+. Operating in a dynamic external landscape, Upstream maintains a high-performance culture anchored in actionable, observable behaviors. It keeps its patient-centered mission at the core of every decision, continually adapting and embracing change to meet evolving patient needs. Its culture prioritizes resilience, strategic nimbleness, and a focus on measurable outcomes over effort—ensuring it remains responsive, accountable, and capable of driving long-term impact at scale.
Recognition: We are a 2023 Audacious Project recipient, with our work featured in publications like Harvard Public Health, Bloomberg, and MedPage Today.
We welcome individuals who are driven by impact and scale to join us in making equitable contraceptive access a reality for all.

Back to jobs
Sr. Analyst, Technology & Project Management (Reproductive Healthcare - Hybrid)
Remotely based in Boston, MA area (requires two days a week in our Boston office)
Apply
Organizational Summary
Contraceptive care is basic healthcare. Yet too many patients in the U.S. struggle to access the care they need, when they need it. Founded in 2014, Upstream USA is a national, nonpartisan nonprofit dedicated to ensuring that equitable, patient-centered contraceptive care is available to everyone.
Our Mission and Impact
Upstream works to ensure individuals can make fully informed, autonomous decisions about the contraceptive methods that are best for them. We are currently the largest contraceptive organization in the country improving contraceptive care in primary care settings, operating in 37 states and Washington, D.C.
While our foundational work focuses on partnering with healthcare organizations offering primary care, such as federally qualified healthcare centers (FQHC) and health systems, we are always evolving. We are actively pursuing additional, innovative paths to ensure every patient has streamlined access to the contraceptive service of their choice, where and when it is most convenient for them.
A Different Kind of Nonprofit
Upstream is a venture philanthropy-backed nonprofit with a current annual budget of $50M+. Operating in a dynamic external landscape, Upstream maintains a high-performance culture anchored in actionable, observable behaviors. It keeps its patient-centered mission at the core of every decision, continually adapting and embracing change to meet evolving patient needs. Its culture prioritizes resilience, strategic nimbleness, and a focus on measurable outcomes over effort—ensuring it remains responsive, accountable, and capable of driving long-term impact at scale.
Recognition: We are a 2023 Audacious Project recipient, with our work featured in publications like Harvard Public Health, Bloomberg, and MedPage Today.
We welcome individuals who are driven by impact and scale to join us in making equitable contraceptive access a reality for all.
Position Summary
Upstream's Data, Analytics and Technology (DAT) team works cross-functionally to ensure software, hardware, and data function optimally while leading improvement projects that shape the business and promote organizational effectiveness, efficiency, and data-driven decision making. The team also supports Upstream's growing, organization-wide use of AI.
This role exists to expand the team's capacity to deliver. Reporting to the Manager of Data, Analytics, Technology & Security, the Sr. Analyst, Technology & Project Management partners closely with the DAT leadership team and colleagues across Upstream to own and move forward the work that keeps initiatives shipping: project management, data analysis and reporting, and the hands-on execution in between the planning and the doing, and adds a versatile, technically capable partner who can both plan the work and do it.
The ideal candidate is a pragmatic, highly organized, and exceptional communicator who is as comfortable running a stakeholder meeting as building a report or completing a project. They are curious, detail-oriented, and energized by turning ambiguous needs into finished work in a fast-moving, lean environment.
Essential Duties and Responsibilities
Technical Project Management (60%)
• Own end-to-end project management, from intake through delivery, for DAT initiatives on the team's roadmap, including data migrations, IT operations improvements, and the central data-layer buildout.
• Manage scope, timelines, dependencies, and stakeholders using agile/Kanban methods; align people on outcomes, owners, and deadlines, and keep work visible and moving, anticipating blockers and keeping initiatives and the team on track.
• Cultivate cross-departmental relationships and drive projects to completion, bringing a technical skill set that lets you both coordinate the work and contribute to it directly, including by not limited to supporting Upstream's evolving central data warehouse / data-layer strategy.
• Serve as a resource for turning data into decisions across teams.
Automation, Tooling & Process Improvement (25%)
• Build and improve MVP (Minimum Viable Product) workflow automations and solutions that remove manual work across teams, then iterate based on real use and feedback.
• Translate staff pain points and ideas into documented, repeatable, right-sized workflows. Train others so improvements stick and scale.
• Drive initiatives to completion, often coordinating and contributing directly to the work.
Systems, AI Adoption & Operations Support (15%)
• Support software and hardware administration and asset lifecycle management (SaaS apps, laptops, office tech) and coordination with third-party technology vendors.
• Support Upstream's AI adoption efforts with hands-on help on pilots, education and training, documentation, and change management.
• Support selection, implementation, and administration across Upstream's SaaS application stack (Google Workspace, Snowflake, Power BI, Vena, ADP, Greenhouse, and others)
• Help improve and, where possible, automate helpdesk and support functions; monitor and elevate recurring issues, propose, and help implement process enhancements.
• Additional duties as assigned.
Required Education, Experience, Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities
Upstream fosters a mission-oriented workplace and welcomes applicants of all backgrounds. The ideal candidate upholds our mission of accessible, patient-centered contraceptive care, builds trust through empathy and honesty, and contributes to a collaborative culture. They bring enthusiasm to their work, creating opportunities for connection and celebration.
• Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills, including clear writing and confident facilitation. Able to translate between technical and non-technical audiences and build trust with colleagues, vendors, and leadership.
• 4+ years of relevant experience across some combination of project management, data analysis/reporting, and technology/operations.
• Demonstrated project management experience. Able to run multiple projects and incoming requests simultaneously, ideally using agile/Kanban methods and a work-management or ticketing system (Asana, Autotask, etc.).
• Hands-on experience doing data analysis and reporting, building dashboards and reports (Power BI, Google Sheets/Excel) and preparing and transforming data ("ETL-type" work).
• Demonstrates a strong bias toward action and ownership. Comfortable both developing strategy and executing it—delivering an initial solution quickly, then iterating and improving over time.
• Proven ability to learn new systems and processes quickly and to solve ambiguous problems with high attention to detail.
• Comfort with using AI tools and a willingness to experiment and innovate with them to help Upstream accelerate towards achieving our mission.
• AI Fluency & Tool Integration: Ability to identify and leverage generative AI tools (such as LLMs, image generators, or industry-specific copilots) to streamline workflows, automate repetitive tasks, and enhance overall output quality while maintaining the proper human checkpoints.
• AI Prompt Engineering & Critical Output Evaluation: Proficiency in crafting effective prompts to achieve desired outcomes and the critical thinking skills necessary to audit, fact-check, and refine AI-generated content for accuracy and brand alignment.
• Ethical AI Awareness: A foundational understanding of the ethical implications of AI, including data privacy, bias recognition, and the responsible use of company information in third-party AI environments.
• Demonstrates the ability to remain focused, adaptable, and solution-oriented in the face of challenges, setbacks, or ambiguity. Approaches obstacles with a growth mindset and maintains a steady commitment to goals, even under pressure or changing circumstances; resilient.
• While we are a remotely based organization, we maintain an on-camera culture during meetings to support connection, engagement, teaming and collaboration. Must be comfortable and able to participate in this environment
Valued and Non-Essential Education, Experience, Knowledge, Skills, and Ability (Not required to apply)
• Bachelor’s degree in Business, Information Technology, Computer Science, Data/Analytics, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent work experience; relevant industry certifications are a plus.
• Scripting (Python, Google Apps Script), SQL, or APIs.
• Experience with ETL/ELT pipelines and data-warehouse tooling (e.g., Snowflake, Fivetran) and data validation techniques.
• Familiarity or experience with Salesforce
• Experience building workflow automations, AI agents, and other AI-based solutions.
• Familiarity with SaaS administration and best practices.
• Familiarity with enterprise AI platforms (Gemini, Claude, Cortex, etc.).
• Experience in a healthcare, nonprofit, or other mission-driven setting.
• Awareness of information security and/or HIPAA concepts.
Travel Requirements
This role will require up to 15% business travel. All Upstreamers can expect a minimum of 8 days of business travel per year to attend 1 annual organizational retreat and 1 or 2 annual team/department meetings.
Hiring Range
$100,000 - $110,000 USD
Pay Transparency
Final offers for this position will be based upon several factors including the scope of the role, market compensation analysis, position requirements, candidate’s experience level and capabilities, fairness in internal pay considerations and will be made within the parameters of Upstream USA's compensation framework and philosophy.
Other Upstream Staff Expectations
• All Upstreamers must be able to attend work-related in-person meetings and functions as needed. • In our hybrid work environments, there is a basic expectation that our Upstreamers will ensure that their work from home setups will have reliable access to phone and Internet to ensure connectivity to their teams.
• At Upstream we gather for moments that matter for training, teaming and connection. Our teams come together for occasional in person meetings and organizational retreats. As part of our hybrid work practices, this travel expectation will be applicable for all Upstreamers, even those based remotely.
• Engage in organization-sponsored learning & development
Upstream Benefits
Upstream USA offers a comprehensive benefit package including medical, dental, vision, life insurance, long and short term disability, 401K with a match, generous vacation, personal, sick and holiday time off, parental leave, professional development, a fitness and cell phone allowance for all full time employees and part time employees who work a minimum of 24 hours per week. Intern positions and contingent worker roles are not eligible for benefits.
Hiring Process
Candidates who advance in our preliminary review process will have an opportunity to discuss the position, their employment background and lived experience with a member of our talent acquisition team by telephone. Those who advance to subsequent steps in our interview process may participate in up to three rounds of meetings by Zoom or in person and in a thought exercise/case study assignment. Each round could consist of multiple meetings with various Upstreamers. If you need anything in advance of your interviews, please reach out to your recruiter. Our Culture We are dedicated to fostering a fair and accessible talent lifecycle, ensuring that every individual has the opportunity to thrive. From recruitment to career development, we strive to create a workplace where talent is recognized, supported, and empowered to contribute meaningfully. Building a strong, representative workforce is essential to our success, and we prioritize collaboration, transparency, and shared leadership to cultivate an environment where all voices are heard and valued.
Our commitment extends beyond hiring—we invest in professional growth, mentorship, and inclusive workplace practices to support long-term success for our employees. You can learn more about our organization on our career site. Upstream Careers
Our goal is to attract, develop and retain exceptional people, and to create a work environment that is dynamic, rewarding and enables each of us to realize our potential. Upstream is committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, genetic information, gender identity or Veteran status. We also consider qualified applicants regardless of criminal histories, consistent with legal requirements. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please let us know. Upstream USA participates in E-Verify.

2 Oliver Street, Suite 402, Boston, MA 02109

The Global Investment & Finance Systems (GIFS) Lead Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) is a senior individual contributor who partners directly with the business while remaining accountable to IT priorities, engineering standards, and governance. Working alongside investment professionals and quantitative researchers, the Lead FDE identifies high-value opportunities and personally architects, builds, and validates solutions from experimentation through the appropriate GIFS SDLC pathway.
Based in GIFS UK, the role partners across Vanguard’s Investment Management Group (IMG), including the Investment Strategy Group (ISG), using rapid, hands-on iteration to explore quantitative and analytical challenges, test potential solutions, and determine which opportunities warrant further investment and productionalization.
The Lead FDE also sets technical direction, mentors engineers, advises IMG and GIFS leaders, and turns direct delivery experience into reusable capabilities and engineering practices for the broader organization.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:
- Partner closely across all teams within the UK Investment Management Group to understand complex workflows and rapidly shape, test, and prioritize high-value quantitative and analytical opportunities.
- Translate ambiguous investment challenges into actionable technical opportunities, selecting the right approach across software, data, AI, machine learning, optimization, and human judgment.
- Personally architect, build, and validate solutions from rapid experimentation through MVP and initial production deployment.
- Lead the productionalisation of research code, quantitative models, analytical tools, and high- or critical-risk EUCTs, strengthening testing, reproducibility, performance, data lineage, and operational support.
- Establish scalable engineering patterns for AI-enabled solutions, including human-in-the-loop controls, reusable components, and evaluation methods addressing quality, safety, latency, cost, and readiness.
- Exercise senior technical judgment with Product, Engineering, Architecture, Platform, Security, and enterprise governance teams on whether capabilities should be refined, elevated, transitioned, reused, or retired.
- Lead through hands-on delivery by setting technical direction, developing critical components, mentoring engineers, and resolving complex delivery barriers.
- Translate successful UK engagements into reusable code, evaluation methods, and engineering patterns, working with Innovation and Emerging Technology to bring emerging capabilities into local delivery and share lessons across GIFS.
WHAT YOU BRING TO THE ROLE (COMPETENCIES):
- Strong understanding of investment management, portfolio, trading, and quantitative research workflows, with the judgment to turn ambiguous problems into actionable technical opportunities.
- Deep software and data engineering expertise, with a record of personally delivering reliable, maintainable, well-documented production solutions using modern testing, CI/CD, logging, and source-control practices.
- Strong quantitative grounding in mathematics, statistics, numerical methods, or a related discipline, with the ability to work effectively alongside quantitative researchers and distinguish research questions from implementation decisions.
- Hands-on expertise across Python, data engineering, cloud platforms, AI and machine learning, optimization, and modern application development.
- Experience architecting AI-enabled and agentic solutions, including RAG, tool use, human-in-the-loop controls, and evaluation frameworks.
- Ability to understand and modernize logic embedded in Excel, Access, VBA, SQL, Tableau, and other EUCT solutions while preserving essential business and quantitative logic.
- Strong enterprise delivery judgment across architecture, security, privacy, controls, auditability, data governance, evaluation, and operational readiness.
- Ability to influence senior business and technology leaders, communicate tradeoffs clearly, and guide decisions on investment, adoption, reuse, and retirement.
- Ability to lead through hands-on delivery across distributed teams and global locations while maintaining accountability for technical quality and business outcomes.
Qualifications
- Bachelor’s degree in computer science, engineering, mathematics, statistics, physics, or a related quantitative or technical field, or equivalent experience.
- 10+ years of relevant software, data, quantitative, or analytics engineering experience.
- Demonstrated experience leading technical workstreams and delivering production-quality solutions across teams or business areas.
- Experience supporting investment management, quantitative research, or related front-office analytical functions.
- Financial services experience and experience with cloud-based data or AI platforms preferred.

Vanguard has implemented a hybrid working model for the majority of our crew members, designed to capture the benefits of enhanced flexibility while enabling in-person learning, collaboration, and connection. We believe our mission-driven and highly collaborative culture is a critical enabler to support long-term client outcomes and enrich the employee experience.

Vanguard, one of the world's leading investment management companies, serves individual investors, institutions, employer-sponsored retirement plans, and financial professionals. We have a diverse and talented crew with a culture that promotes teamwork, along with an unwavering focus on serving our clients' best interests.

Tech Leads can expect a visible role implementing changes to complex, high-traffic experiences at the centre of Vanguard's UK growth strategy. Candidates should enjoy a fast-paced group that builds, supports, and enhances applications used by millions of investors. In this role you will

Lead design, development, and implementation across the monorepo's apps and shared libraries. - Solution Architecture & Governance Define and enforce architectural standards (module boundaries, shared-library design, SSR/rendering strategy) that align with Vanguard's technology strategy. Drive continuous improvement and foster a culture of learning. - Documentation Excellence Create and maintain clear technical documentation — architecture diagrams, integration and deployment guides, and operational runbooks — that stay accurate and accessible as the platform evolves. - Innovation & Continuous Improvement Identify opportunities to improve the public-site capability through new tooling, automation, build/caching improvements, and rendering/performance enhancements. Qualifications - Proven related work experience, with at least three years of development experience. - Undergraduate degree or equivalent combination of training and experience. As a Staff Network Engineer at vCluster Labs, you aren't just configuring switches; you are building the automation logic that configures them. AI Clouds run on InfiniBand and high-speed Ethernet fabrics that most teams still wire up by hand, one customer at a time. You will build the automation that turns that fabric into repeatable provisioning logic. You start in a small R&D group alongside our CTO and grow into owning this area as it becomes a core part of our platform.
As a Staff Network Engineer, your role will include:
- Fabric automation: You will design and build the systems that automatically provision and configure NVIDIA switches and InfiniBand fabrics, including integration with NVIDIA UFM. Manual, per-customer switch setup is the thing you are replacing.
- Network config management and sync: You will build the control loop that keeps switch, VLAN, and VXLAN state consistent with what our platform intends, detects drift, and reconciles it safely in production.
- NAT gateway and L4 load balancing: You will build the gateway and load balancing layer that tenant clusters depend on for connectivity, with failover designed in from day one rather than bolted on later.
- Scale and failure engineering: You will define how our network layer behaves at large scale: BGP route table limits, convergence, failover, and what happens when a link, switch, or gateway dies under real AI workloads.
- Customer Zero for AI networking: You will run your automation on real AI Cloud environments, bring back what breaks, and turn hard-won operational lessons into product behavior our customers never have to think about.
- Technical direction: You will help decide what we build versus integrate with partner solutions, write the design and requirements docs, and set the standards for how networking works across vCluster products.
This role could be a fit for you if you bring:
- You have built network automation, not just operated networks: You have shipped software that configures switches, routers, or load balancers programmatically, ideally as part of a product or internal platform other teams relied on.
- NVIDIA networking experience: Hands-on work with NVIDIA UFM, NVIDIA Spectrum or Quantum switches, Cumulus Linux, or NVUE, including programming against their APIs.
- Deep fabric fundamentals: Strong command of InfiniBand, VLAN, VXLAN and EVPN, and BGP, including how they behave and fail at production scale.
- Production scale scars: You have run networks at real production scale, seen them break, and helped fix the root cause with automation rather than runbooks.
- Software engineering ability: You write production code in Go or Python, use version control and code review as a matter of course, and think of network config as code.
Bonus points for:
- AI networking depth: Experience tuning fabrics for GPU training or inference workloads, such as RoCEv2, congestion control, rail-optimized topologies, or Spectrum-X.
- AI Cloud or hyperscaler background: You helped build network automation at a GPU cloud, hyperscaler, or large CDN.
- Load balancer and gateway internals: Experience building L4 load balancers or NAT gateways, including with eBPF/XDP or DPDK.
- Open source: Contributions to networking or Kubernetes projects such as SONiC, FRRouting, Cilium, or MetalLB.

Craven Street Wealth is an award-winning Chartered financial planning and wealth management firm, helping individuals, families and businesses make confident financial decisions. About the Role
Craven Street Wealth are looking for an experienced Operations Director to join the executive management team.
This is a senior leadership role with real influence, helping to shape the firm’s strategy, people development, client proposition and overall performance.
The role has a strong focus on operational excellence. You’ll be responsible for designing, delivering and improving the firm’s Target Operating Model (TOM), ensuring client service, paraplanning and operational teams operate efficiently, consistently and in line with regulatory expectations.
This is a full‑time, permanent position, but flexibility in working patterns can be discussed.

As Operations Director, you’ll lead and oversee the firm’s day‑to‑day operations while keeping a strategic, forward‑looking perspective. Key areas include:
Strategic leadership: Contributing at board level to business strategy, policy and decision‑making, and helping translate strategic ambitions into practical, well‑run operations.
Operational excellence: Designing and continuously improving end‑to‑end client service processes, from onboarding through to ongoing advice and servicing.
Financial planning technical operations: Ownership of policies and procedures to support the delivery of financial planning, including ownership of advice policy, adviser competence assessments, advice suitability checking procedures.
Client-first service: Embedding high service standards aligned with Chartered status and FCA Consumer Duty, using clear workflows, SLAs and performance measures.
Regulatory and governance oversight: Ensuring operations fully support FCA requirements, strong systems and controls, and effective risk management.
Growth and scalability: Building an operational infrastructure capable of supporting regional expansion and future mergers and acquisitions, including integrating new teams smoothly and consistently.
People leadership: Leading, developing and motivating operational, client service and paraplanning teams, and building a strong leadership structure for the future.
Financial management: Managing the operational budget, ensuring cost efficiency without compromising client outcomes or service quality.
Culture and ethics: Promoting a positive, ethical and inclusive culture, and acting as a senior ambassador for the firm when required.
You’ll work closely with the Managing Director, Compliance and other senior leaders to ensure the business runs smoothly, responsibly and is well positioned for future growth. About You
This role would suit a proven operational leader from an IFA, wealth management or financial planning background. You’ll bring: • Senior leadership experience in a regulated financial services environment
• A strong understanding of financial advice operations, paraplanning and client service models
• Experience designing and implementing scalable operating models
• Solid knowledge of FCA regulation, Consumer Duty and governance expectations
• A people focused approach, with experience leading and developing teams
• Budget management and commercial awareness
• Experience supporting growth, regional expansion or M&A integration
• Experience within a Chartered firm, integrating acquisitions, or working with wealth management technology and CRM platforms would be an advantage
• At least Level 4 Diploma in Regulated Financial Advice or equivalent
What Success Looks Like
Success in this role means delivering a scalable and efficient operating model, consistently high client service across all regions, strong regulatory alignment, and an operation that is fully prepared to support future growth and acquisitions.
Rewards & Benefits
At Craven Street Wealth, we believe in supporting our people both professionally and personally. In return for your contribution, you'll have access to a range of benefits including:
• Competitive salary.
• Hybrid working, with time split between home and office.
• Discretionary annual bonus.
• 34 days holiday per calendar year, including bank holidays, with the option to purchase up to five additional days per year.
• Supported and encouraged professional development.
• Contributory pension scheme
• Medical cashback plan, helping cover the cost of everyday healthcare expenses such as dental treatment, eye care and physiotherapy.
• Occupational sick pay scheme.
• Group income protection scheme.
• Life assurance scheme
• Cycle to Work scheme.
• Up to 10 hours of volunteering leave each year.
• Opportunities for internal progression within Craven Street Wealth and across the wider Quanta Group.
• A collaborative and supportive culture where colleagues are encouraged to grow, contribute and succeed.
